headline: UnaStella secures 5 billion won to develop 5‑ton rocket engine under Global TIPS
content: Korean startup plans electric motor‑pump cycle and clustering engines for UNA EXPRESS series over four years Korean space launch vehicle developer UnaStella will receive 5 billion won in government funding over four years to develop a 5‑ton electric motor‑pump engine for small launch vehicles. The company will also seek demonstration partnerships with overseas customers that need microgravity experiments or in‑orbit testing of space components. UnaStella announced on the 24th that it has been finally selected for the general research and development project of the “2026 Global TIPS” program overseen by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups and the Korea Technology and Information Promotion Agency for SMEs. Global TIPS is a program that links private investment with government R&D support to back technology development and global growth of promising small and venture companies. While companies carry out core technology development and performance verification, an operator consortium supports their growth through investment, commercialization consulting, and overseas network connections. Founded in 2022, UnaStella has continued its technology development through R&D support programs from the Ministry of SMEs and Startups since its establishment. Through “TIPS,” the company began engine design and manufacturing, and under “Scale-up TIPS” it carried out development and verification of the electric motor‑pump system. UnaStella succeeded in launching UNA EXPRESS-I in May 2025 and is currently developing follow-up launch vehicles and an “electric motor‑pump–based engine.” With its selection for Global TIPS, the company plans to extend its accumulated development achievements into further R&D and overseas commercialization.

headline: Over 2k Himachal-made drug samples failed quality tests over 3 years, assembly told
content: Kullu: A total of 2,216 medicine samples manufactured in Himachal Pradesh failed quality tests over the past three years, with 47 pharmaceutical companies recording 10 or more failures, according to data tabled in the state assembly.The figures were disclosed by the health and family welfare department in a written reply to a question by Bharmour MLA Dr Janak Raj during the recently concluded winter session in Dharamshala. The samples were tested in different laboratories during 2024-25, 2025-26 and 2026-27 up to Nov 1.Of the 2,216 failures, 844 were recorded in 2024-25, 963 in 2025-26 and 409 in the current financial year. The manufacturing units were located in Solan, Sirmaur, Una and Kangra districts.Several companies disputed the test findings, with some challenging the analysis reports.Of the 47 companies with repeated failures, 43 were jointly inspected by the state drug control administration and the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO). The state drug controller also conducted separate inspections.The department said manufacturing licences of three companies had been cancelled, while production at 19 companies was fully or partially stopped until they complied with the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules, 1945.In all, 1,608 product licences were suspended and 59 cancelled over the three years. Warnings were issued in four cases. The action affected 1,667 products, and the govt directed the recall of medicines corresponding to all samples declared Not of Standard Quality (NSQ). Legal action was initiated in 17 cases.The reply also flagged suspected spurious or counterfeit medicines carrying the names of established pharmaceutical companies. These included cough syrups and medicines for high blood pressure and bacterial infections. The companies denied manufacturing the products and described them as spurious or counterfeit.The department said drug inspectors had been directed to inspect every pharmaceutical manufacturing unit at least once a year. Units with repeated quality failures were being inspected independently by the state department and jointly with CDSCO.

headline: Missed flight after 4-hour train delay, Jammu couple gets Rs 63,000 from Indian Railways
content: A couple travelling from Jammu to Delhi missed their connecting flight to Guwahati after their train arrived nearly four hours late, forcing them to book fresh air tickets and pay for a hotel stay. Holding the Railways responsible for failing to provide evidence explaining the delay, the Jammu District Consumer Commission has directed it to pay Rs 63,199. The Jammu District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission president Pawan Dev Kotwal and member Neelam Bala Bhardwaj were hearing a complaint by Mohit Singh Bhau and his wife Damini Billoria against Northern Railways and the Union of India, alleging that a nearly four-hour train delay made them miss their connecting flight to Guwahati. They sought Rs 60,000 for financial losses, Rs 50,000 for mental agony and inconvenience, and Rs 30,000 in litigation expenses. “Every passenger's time is precious, and they might have booked the tickets for further journey,” the commission said on November 4, referring to a Supreme Court verdict, holding that the Railways could not escape responsibility without producing evidence to explain the delay. “Since the complaint faced inconvenience and discomfort and mental agony due to deficiency in service on the part of OPs (Railways and its officials), they are also entitled to receive compensation for the same,” it added. Couple forced to book fresh flight, pay for hotel The couple had booked tickets on the Jammu-Delhi DEE Duronto Express for December 19, 2022. The train was scheduled to reach Delhi at 3.55 am on December 20, while their flight to Guwahati was scheduled to depart at 7.15 am. However, the train was delayed by three hours and 55 minutes, leaving them unable to catch their flight. According to the complaint, the couple had to book fresh air tickets to Guwahati and arrange hotel accommodation after missing their flight. They spent Rs 35,699 on fresh flight tickets and Rs 2,500 on hotel accommodation, bringing their additional expenditure to Rs 38,199. The couple approached the consumer commission on February 13, 2023, alleging deficiency in service by the Railways. However, the Railways opposed the complaint, arguing that it could not be held liable for delayed train arrivals under Rule 115 of the Indian Railway Conference Association Coaching Tariff. During the proceedings, the Railways' counsel argued that the train had been delayed because of fog and that the administration was protected from liability under the applicable railway rules. The commission, however, noted that the Railways had failed to produce evidence establishing that fog had caused the delay. It also recorded that the couple had disputed this explanation, stating that there was no fog on the day of their journey. The commission further noted that the Railways had not filed its written version within the statutory period and that its subsequent reply could not be taken on record. Although its counsel participated in the proceedings and cross-examined the complainants, the Railways did not lead any evidence explaining the delay. It observed that the couple had established a prima facie case of deficiency in service, while the Railways had failed to substantiate its defence. The commission also referred to an earlier Supreme Court ruling involving a passenger who missed a connecting flight because of a delayed train. Finding the circumstances similar, the Jammu commission said the Supreme Court's reasoning applied to the couple's complaint as well. “Citizen/passenger cannot be at the mercy of the authorities Somebody has to accept the responsibility,” the commission observed. Allowing the complaint, the commission directed the Railways to reimburse Rs 38,199 towards fresh flight tickets and hotel accommodation, with simple interest at 7.5 per cent per annum from February 13, 2023, until realisation. It also awarded Rs 20,000 as compensation for inconvenience, discomfort and mental agony, and Rs 5,000 towards litigation expenses. The total award comes to Rs 63,199, besides interest on Rs 38,199. The commission directed the Railways to deposit the amount within six weeks of receiving a copy of the order. Takeaway Preserve your train and flight tickets, hotel bills and other receipts if a train delay makes you miss a connecting flight. The Railways may be held liable if it fails to provide evidence explaining the delay and establish that it was beyond its control. For consumer-related grievances, individuals may contact the consumer helpline in their respective states and union territories (Himachal Pradesh: 1800-180-8087) or call the National Consumer Helpline at 1915 for assistance. headline: Bank holiday today Tuesday, 24 November: Branches closed in these 21 cities across India — Check RBI list and reasons
content: Banks in several parts of India will remain closed today, Tuesday, 24 November, on account of Guru Nanak Jayanti. However, the holiday is not applicable across the country.According to the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) holiday calendar, branches in 21 cities will remain closed today under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Banks in other cities will continue to operate as usual.Meanwhile, stock market trading will also remain closed today, with both the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) observing a trading holiday.Which cities are observing a bank holiday today?According to the RBI's November 2026 holiday calendar, bank branches in the following cities/ states will remain closed on 24 November:Aizawl (Mizoram)Belapur (Maharashtra)Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)Bhubaneswar (Odisha)ChandigarhDehradun (Uttarakhand)Hyderabad (Telangana)Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh)Jaipur (Rajasthan)Jammu (Jammu and Kashmir)Kanpur (Uttar Pradesh)Kohima (Nagaland)Kolkata (West Bengal)Lucknow (Uttar Pradesh)Mumbai (Maharashtra)Nagpur (Maharashtra)New DelhiRaipur (Chhattisgarh)Ranchi (Jharkhand)Shimla (Himachal Pradesh)Srinagar (Jammu and Kashmir)This means that branches of all public and private sector banks, including State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, will remain closed in these 21 cities. However, the bank holiday will not affect most routine digital banking services. Customers can continue to access their accounts through mobile banking and internet banking, transfer money using UPI, NEFT and IMPS, check account balances, download statements and make bill payments.Why are banks closed today?The RBI has listed the 24 November holiday as Guru Nanak Jayanti/Karthika Purnima/Rahas Purnima. Guru Nanak Jayanti: It marks the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, the founder of Sikhism and the first of the ten Sikh Gurus.Karthika Purnima: It marks the full moon day of the Hindu lunar month of Kartik. The occasion is considered auspicious in Hinduism and Jainism.Rahas Purnima: Also known as Raas Purnima, it celebrates Lord Krishna's divine Raas Leela with Radha and the Gopis.Where will banks remain open today?Bank branches in cities not covered by the 24 November holiday will continue to operate as usual, with regular banking services available to customers. These include Agartala, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gangtok, Guwahati, Imphal, Kochi, Panaji, Patna, Shillong, Thiruvananthapuram and Vijayawada.Customers should check with their respective bank branches for any local operational changes.Disclaimer: This information is based on the RBI's regional bank holiday calendar and is provided for informational purposes only.

headline: Jai Ram demands rollback of hotel fee hike in HP
content: Shimla: Leader of opposition Jai Ram Thakur on Monday demanded the immediate rollback of a 2.5-fold hike in consent-to-operate fees imposed on Himachal Pradesh’s hotel industry by the State Pollution Control Board, accusing the Congress government of burdening tourism operators with excessive charges.The former chief minister said hoteliers were being forced to pay five years’ fees upfront, despite most properties in the state being leased out on an annual basis.Questioning the rationale behind the move, Thakur pointed out that owners of small green-category hotels with 10 to 13 rooms would now have to pay Rs 1.8 lakh for five years, up from Rs 72,000 earlier.With the annual fee raised from Rs 14,400 to Rs 36,000, small hotel operators face an additional financial burden of Rs 1.08 lakh over five years, he added.Thakur alleged that instead of framing effective policies to strengthen the state’s economy, the government was focused on extracting revenue from citizens, warning that the decision would discourage entrepreneurs and hurt a sector vital to Himachal’s economy.Contrasting the move with successive governments’ efforts to promote tourism, he criticised the current dispensation for demanding five years’ advance fees and recalled its earlier attempts to tax homestays.Accusing the govt of repeatedly hiking levies across sectors, Thakur also cited increased taxes on tourist vehicles, higher educational fees, and raised charges for medical and revenue-related services.

headline: Himachal Pradesh eyes 1,000 more e-buses to cut HRTC costs
content: The state government will add 1,000 e-buses to make Himachal Pradesh clean and green and to make the Himachal Road Transport Corporation (HRTC) a self-reliant corporation, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said today. He was inaugurating a new bus route at Majhyar in the Nadaun Assembly constituency of Hamirpur district.The route will connect villages around Sera with Hamirpur, meeting a long-pending demand of residents of Nadaun, Sera and several adjoining villages. The Chief Minister said it would significantly improve public transport connectivity in the area and particularly benefit patients and their attendants visiting Dr Radhakrishnan Government Medical College at Jol Sappad, besides students, employees and other daily commuters.The HRTC, he said, bears substantial financial liabilities on account of pensions, salaries and other expenses, so it was essential to reduce its operating costs. Electric buses were cheaper to run than diesel buses, which would improve the corporation’s financial health. The government was giving priority to promoting electric buses and more would be added in the coming years to move the HRTC gradually towards electric mobility.Himachal’s geographical conditions were different from those of other states, the Chief Minister said. Diesel buses would continue to run in remote, inaccessible and difficult mountain terrain to ensure uninterrupted services and would remain important in areas where electric buses faced technical or geographical challenges.The government was committed to providing the best health, transport and education facilities to people, he said, and had started many welfare schemes for the poor and needy. It was making concerted efforts to modernise public transport and make it more economical and environment-friendly. In its very first budget, he said, the government had envisioned making Himachal a green energy state and had accordingly prioritised electric mobility.Meanwhile, the Chief Minister attended the wedding ceremony of his niece, Nikita, at his ancestral village of Bhavdan in the Nadaun constituency last night. He congratulated the newlyweds and wished them a happy and prosperous married life.

headline: Educational exposure visit to DIET-Solan, PM Shri schools
content: A delegation of officials of the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), District Institutes of Education and Training (DIETs), Block Resource Centres (BRCs) and Cluster Resource Centres (CRCs) from New Delhi undertook an educational exposure to DIET-Solan, PM SHRI School, Baddi, and PM SHRI School, Nalagarh, recently and interacted with faculty.The visiting team observed the teaching-learning environment, infrastructure, instructional resources and student activities and held detailed discussions with the faculty members and students in these institutes.The interactions focused on teacher education, classroom practices, school leadership, mentoring, student engagement, learning outcomes, inclusive education and the implementation of the PM SHRI initiatives which are aimed at strengthening teacher capacity and institutional leadership through structured professional development supported by DIETs.The faculty members and coordinators from both New Delhi and Himachal Pradesh shared good practices being implemented in their respective institutions and school systems. The discussions covered effective teacher-training strategies, academic support mechanisms, use of teaching-learning materials, community participation, monitoring of classroom processes and innovative approaches to improving student learning.The participants also discussed challenges and issues commonly faced by schools and teacher-education institutions. These included teacher workload, diverse learning needs, resource constraints, ensuring quality in classroom transactions and sustaining educational innovations. Practical solutions and successful strategies adopted by both sides were also shared during the deliberations.Deputy Director, School Education (Quality), Himachal Pradesh, Rajinder Verma, apprised the visiting delegation of new practices and initiatives in the state to improve the quality of school education and strengthen teacher capacity.Principal, DIET-Solan, Mamta Gupta, and coordinator Babita Thakur shared the details of the institute’s academic, training and outreach activities. Coordinators Amit and Anamika from New Delhi spoke about the good practices of their institution while also participating in the discussions.

headline: AI lab, auditorium planned for Bilaspur engineering college
content: The state government is providing financial assistance to encourage research and innovation and to help youth in their pursuits, Technical Education Minister Rajesh Dharmani said on Sunday. He was addressing ‘Emerge-2026’, a technical and cultural festival, at the Government Hydro Engineering College, Bandla, in Bilaspur district.He announced an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) lab at the college to give students access to modern technical facilities and a modern auditorium to provide better infrastructure for academic, technical and cultural activities.Dharmani said the government was committed to fostering the creative thinking and innovative spirit of youth. Through the State Innovation Policy 2026 and a State Innovation Fund of Rs 2 crore, efforts were under way to help students turn ideas into prototypes, provide seed funding for startups, strengthen incubation centres and promote training and capacity building. Research and development projects were also being encouraged through the Department of Science, Technology and Environment and HIMCOSTE, he added.Earlier in the day, the minister distributed prizes to students at the Government Senior Secondary School, Kapahra, in the Ghumarwin Assembly constituency. He said the school would be developed as a ‘Centre of Excellence’ to improve the quality of education in government institutions and prepare students for a competitive era. The school, he said, is affiliated with the CBSE and has 14 teachers from the CBSE cadre.Dharmani said the government was prioritising road connectivity in Kapahra and neighbouring panchayats. Nearly Rs 20 crore was being spent on the construction, repair and paving of roads in the area and about Rs 16 crore on the upgradation of the road from Barthin to Chhat and Junala, on which work worth Rs 4 crore to Rs 5 crore had already been completed.

headline: Himachal Pradesh CM Sukhu visits ailing Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania at IGMC
content: Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu today visited Indira Gandhi Medical College (IGMC), Shimla, to enquire about the health of Himachal Pradesh Vidhan Sabha Speaker Kuldeep Singh Pathania, who is undergoing treatment at the hospital. The Chief Minister wished him a speedy recovery. Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri also visited the hospital to enquire about the Speaker’s health.Pathania was admitted to IGMC today on the advice of doctors after experiencing repeated bouts of fever and general weakness. According to Vidhan Sabha sources, he had been feeling slightly unwell during the winter session of the Assembly, held in Dharamsala from November 16 to 21.Doctors suspect typhoid, although confirmatory blood test reports are awaited. A doctor said that the Speaker had no apparent health issues apart from recurring fever. His ultrasound and X-ray reports were normal and he had been put on antibiotics. His condition is stable, the doctor added.During his visit, Chief Minister Sukhu also enquired about the health of Leader of Opposition Jai Ram Thakur’s sister, who is undergoing treatment at IGMC. He wished her a speedy recovery.

headline: ‘Supplements cannot cure diseases’: Tukaram Mundhe warns gyms & pharmacies against misleading claims
content: New Delhi: Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Commissioner Tukaram Mundhe is back with a warning for supplement sellers and promoters: health supplements cannot claim to cure diseases. In a post on social media platform X on Tuesday, Mundhe said claims made on product labels, websites, e-commerce platforms and through influencers must comply with the law. He added that gyms, pharmacies and fitness centres selling supplements must obtain a licence or registration from the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI). “No supplement can claim to cure a disease. If a product label, website or influencer makes such a promise, it is not just misleading; it is against the law,” he said. Those publishing or promoting misleading advertisements, including social media influencers, would be held accountable, he said. The warning follows a statewide compliance order issued by the Maharashtra FDA on 20 November, directing stricter enforcement of existing regulations for three categories of products — health supplements, nutraceuticals and foods for special dietary use. Health supplements, which include products such as vitamin tablets, protein powders and mineral supplements, are meant to add nutrients to a person’s regular diet. Nutraceuticals contain ingredients derived from food, such as plant extracts or other concentrated compounds, which are marketed for their nutritional or physiological benefits. Foods for special dietary use are formulated for people with particular dietary requirements, such as those with diabetes or other health conditions, or for groups such as pregnant women and sportspersons.

headline: Sabarimala trek: Health department issues fresh heart safety guidelines for devotees
content: Keralam's Health Department has issued fresh health guidelines for Ayyappa devotees doing the "strenuous" Sabarimala trek. In a statement on its site, it reads, "Ayyappa devotees arriving at Sabarimala for darshan must strictly follow all the instructions issued by the Health Department and healthcare personnel while undertaking the strenuous trek. People with heart conditions should undergo a medical examination before the pilgrimage and obtain medical clearance from their doctors." Devotees walk through forested, hilly terrain to reach the Sabarimala Ayyappa temple, traditionally following 41 days of fasting and religious observances. According to the guidelines, those who have recently suffered a heart attack, undergone heart surgery or angioplasty, or experienced heart failure should not undertake the hill climb without the advice of a specialist. "Devotees should ensure that lifestyle-related diseases are under control and continue taking their prescribed medicines regularly. They should carry all necessary medicines along with their prescriptions. Devotees should climb the hills according to their physical capacity and avoid excessive speed and physical exertion," it stated. It also prescribed some essential measures. *Take frequent breaks and drink plenty of water. (Those advised to restrict fluid intake due to heart failure should follow their doctor's instructions.) *Do not climb the hills on an empty stomach. Avoid pushing through crowds or running. "If chest pain or breathlessness occurs, stop the journey immediately and seek medical assistance. Symptoms such as chest pain, heaviness, tightness or discomfort, breathlessness, excessive sweating, dizziness, fainting, abnormal changes in heartbeat, sudden extreme fatigue, or pain radiating to the arms, jaw or back should be treated as a cardiac emergency. In such situations, stop walking immediately and rest in a safe place. Seek assistance at the nearest emergency medical centre. If necessary, use ambulance services to reach a hospital. Health Department officials have informed that devotees can call 04735 203232 for emergency assistance." DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine. For devotees undertaking the traditional Erumeli forest route to Sabarimala, also known as the Periya Pathai or Kanana Patha, the pilgrimage is as physically demanding as it is spiritual. The trek covers approximately 46–48 km and typically takes two days to reach the Sannidhanam, or the temple's sanctum sanctorum. "The Sabarimala pilgrimage involves considerable physical exertion, and devotees must be mindful of their heart health while undertaking the hill trek," said Dr Nikhil Parchure, director, intervention cardiologist, Gleneagles Hospital Parel, Mumbai. Balakrishnan Dorai, 66, an Ayyappa devotee and Guruswami of Saran Seva Sangh, Chennai, has been undertaking the Sabarimala pilgrimage for 45 years. He told indianexpress.com that while the traditional forest route can be physically demanding, medical facilities along the way have improved considerably since he first began the pilgrimage in the 1980s. Devotees can now access medical assistance at several points, including first aid and oxygen supplies, facilities that were hardly available when he started making the trek. "They even station medical personnel on the Periya Pathai trekking route, at important points," he said. Here's what you should consider (Photo: Getty Images/Thinkstock) He recalled two instances when fellow devotees experienced heart-related complications during the pilgrimage. One of them had previously undergone bypass surgery and was given medical attention for two days before being airlifted to Chennai. Another devotee with a similar condition also received timely medical care, he said. Dr Nikesh Jain, consultant, interventional cardiologist, Wockhardt Hospitals Mumbai Central, concurred that physical exertion increases the heart's demand for oxygen and requires it to pump blood more efficiently. "During an uphill climb, this workload rises considerably. In individuals with underlying coronary artery disease, reduced heart function or abnormal heart rhythms, the additional strain can trigger symptoms or potentially serious cardiac events," described Dr Jain. One concern is that people who have been managing their daily activities comfortably may underestimate the demands of a prolonged climb. "Those with a previous heart attack, angioplasty, bypass surgery or heart failure should seek an individual assessment from their cardiologist before attempting the trek. Being symptom-free during routine activities does not automatically mean someone is fit for strenuous climbing," Dr Jain told indianexpress.com. Dr Haresh Mehta, consultant, interventional cardiologist, Lilavati Hospital & Research Centre, Bandra (West) too noted that in individuals with underlying coronary artery disease, even if it has not yet been diagnosed, walking uphill as an additional workload, can sometimes trigger a cardiac event. "Age alone is not the only factor; diabetes, hypertension, high cholesterol, smoking and a family history of heart disease can also increase the risk. People should not assume that being able to manage their everyday routine means they are prepared for several hours of continuous climbing," said Dr Mehta. Dr Jain noted that chest pressure, heaviness or discomfort should never be dismissed as ordinary exertion, particularly if accompanied by sweating, breathlessness or nausea. "Pain may also spread towards the shoulder, arm, jaw or back. Some people, especially older adults and those with diabetes, may experience less typical symptoms such as sudden exhaustion, dizziness or unexplained breathlessness without prominent chest pain. If any such warning signs appear, stop walking immediately and seek assistance at the nearest medical facility. Do not attempt to resume the climb once the discomfort subsides without medical evaluation. In a suspected heart attack, every minute matters, and reaching emergency medical care promptly can significantly influence the outcome," said Dr Jain. Ayyappa devotees arriving at Sabarimala for darshan must strictly follow all the instructions (Photo: Sabarimala.Kerala.Gov.In) Dr Ajay Sawant, consultant, internal medicine, KIMS Hospitals Thane, said a pilgrimage involving several hours of walking and climbing requires more preparation than many people realise. "Devotees with diabetes, high blood pressure, respiratory illnesses or other chronic conditions should get their health parameters evaluated before travelling. It is important to ensure that these conditions are reasonably controlled and that prescribed medication is taken regularly," said Dr Sawant. Older adults and those who do not exercise routinely should be especially careful about sudden physical exertion, he cautioned, adding that a medical consultation before the journey can help identify individual risks and determine any additional precautions. What to note? According to Dr Sawant, the biggest mistake is trying to keep pace with others or complete the climb quickly. "Physical endurance varies from person to person, so devotees should take breaks whenever they feel tired instead of pushing themselves. Adequate hydration is essential, and carrying water along with an oral rehydration solution such as oral rehydration salts can help replenish fluids and electrolytes during prolonged physical activity," Dr Sawant said. Starting the trek without eating can contribute to weakness, particularly among people with diabetes who may experience fluctuations in blood glucose levels. "Carrying essential medicines, a small supply of food, and personal medical records is advisable. Devotees should also pay attention to their feet during the climb. Any blister or skin injury should be addressed immediately rather than ignored, as continued friction and walking can aggravate the problem. If someone experiences unusual weakness, dizziness or difficulty breathing, they should stop and seek medical attention rather than assume it is simply a result of walking," said Dr Sawant. DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to. Always consult your health practitioner before starting any routine.

headline: For NEET-UG 2027, Centre weighs letting students choose between computer-based & pen-and-paper tests
content: New Delhi: For next year’s NEET-UG exams, the Centre is considering giving candidates the option to choose between the CBT (Computer-Based Test) and pen-and-paper modes so that they have a “level playing field”, government sources told ThePrint. All competitive exams, including NEET-UG, conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA), will eventually move to 100 percent CBT mode, the sources added. “Since the NEET-UG exams were being conducted in physical mode all this while, many of the students who will be appearing next year would be preparing accordingly. If we transition to full CBT mode next year, these students can claim that they are at a disadvantage. To give them a level playing field, the government is considering giving them the option to choose,” one of the sources said. The Nandan Nilekani-led high-powered task force set up to reform competitive examinations is also in favour of giving candidates the option to choose between the CBT and pen-and-paper modes, the source said, adding that a similar approach was followed when JEE Main transitioned from pen-and-paper to CBT. The transition for JEE Main was not immediate. The CBT format was first introduced as an option in 2011, alongside the offline mode, with both formats continuing for several years before the examination moved entirely to CBT in January 2019. With 22.79 lakh students registering for NEET-UG 2026 and around 20 lakh appearing for the examination across more than 5,400 centres in 13 languages, conducting the test offline involves an enormous logistical exercise. The entire process, from printing question papers in multiple languages to transporting confidential packets to examination centres across the country, also creates multiple points of vulnerability to paper leaks.

headline: Delhi government set to revive annual opt-in power subsidy system | Latest News Delhi
content: The power subsidy system in Delhi is set for another overhaul, with the government planning to launch a dedicated portal by end of this year that would reintroduce a system under which consumers have to actively opt in for the benefit and renew their choice every year, officials aware of the matter said on Monday.The proposed system, if enforced, will reintroduce the opt-in power subsidy system for consumers in Delhi, which had been temporarily in place between October 2022 and March 2023 under the previous Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government.The portal is likely to go live from December and consumers will be given a month’s time to opt-in for power subsidy, the officials cited above said. “If consumers fail to opt-in in that period, they will have to wait another year to avail the option. However, you will be able to opt-out whenever you want,” said an official.Also Read | Delhi power demand hits a new record of 8,748 MW amid intense heatPortal Registration and Subsidy SpendingThe power subsidy scheme in the Capital remains one of Delhi’s largest expenditure commitments. The government released ₹4,037.63 crore towards power subsidies in the 2025-26 financial year till February 2026, according to the Economic Survey tabled in the Delhi Assembly in March. Nearly 4.76 million households were receiving the subsidy, while Delhi has more than 7.3 million electricity consumers, with domestic consumers accounting for 84.1% of the total.The portal, officials said, will also centralise the subsidy registration process and give consumers a single point for registering for the power subsidy. Discoms will validate consumers’ account details. Consumers are likely to log in using their 14-digit consumer account number and authenticate their Aadhaar details before confirming whether they wish to avail of the subsidy. “The work on the portal is almost complete. Users will have to validate their Aadhaar details. Consumers will get the options to opt in or opt out,” an official said.The portal, to be hosted and maintained by the power department, is expected to be launched either in December or in January, with the government aiming to implement the system in the new year.Also Read | Delhi's power demand hits a new May high of 8,439MW amid heatwaveHow Delhi’s Power Subsidy System WorksThe subsidy system was rolled out in March 2015 when the AAP came to power in Delhi. Under that system, consumers received automatic free electricity up to 200 units and a 50% subsidy for consumption between 201 and 400 units, irrespective of willingness to avail of the benefit. Domestic consumers using up to 200 units a month receive a 100% subsidy on energy charges, while those consuming between 201 and 400 units get a 50% subsidy up to ₹800 in subsidy. The benefit is not available to households consuming more than 400 units.However, in October 2022, the AAP government made it an opt-in system where consumers had to send a text message to a designated number. To be sure, the other contours of the scheme – the amount of subsidy and requirements – remained the same. Officials said more than 80% of domestic consumers had opted in.The opt-in system was discontinued around five months later, with all consumers made eligible after Atishi took over as the power minister. That automatic eligibility remains in force till date.Also Read | Free solar panels for Delhi houses using 400 units of powerHistory of the Annual Opt-In SystemThe opt-in system was first introduced with the AAP government arguing that consumers who could afford to pay should have the option of foregoing the subsidy, allowing public funds to be directed towards other priorities. Consumers were initially allowed to register through multiple channels, including online platforms, WhatsApp, missed calls, and QR codes printed on electricity bills. By April 2023, around 4.93 million consumers had opted in, accounting for 84.1% of domestic electricity consumers.Under the opt-in system, the scheme was envisaged as an annual subscription, with beneficiaries required to renew before the end of each financial year. However, the government subsequently extended existing registrations instead of requiring fresh applications. In March 2023, then power minister Atishi announced that consumers who had opted in would continue receiving the subsidy until March 31, 2024. The AAP government subsequently extended the scheme through March 31, 2025.The continuation of the subsidy under the BJP government meant consumers were not required to go through the annual opt-in process in the same manner, even as the government now plans to introduce a centralised portal to formalise the system.

headline: BJP, SAD to fight Punjab polls as 'true partners': Kewal Singh Dhillon
content: After the BJP announced an alliance with its oldest partner, the Shiromani Akali Dal in Punjab, the state BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon spoke about the upcoming alliance with DH’s Amrita Madhukalya. .In Punjab, you will have to contend with the Aam Aadmi Party. Where do you see the BJP-SAD Alliance in this mix? .On this auspicious day of Gurpurab, this alliance has been formed. It is very good for Punjab. The key issues facing Punjab today are the drug menace and unemployment. The state’s financial situation is also in a very poor state. Considering all of this, if the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal, which is an alliance that many people had been calling for, come together, it will be for the betterment of Punjab. .The BJP has never formed a government in Punjab alone; do you think that you will do so now that you are in an alliance with SAD. .We will secure a substantial majority, and the NDA, together with the SAD, will form the government. .Now that an alliance is announced, what happens now? What are the next steps, following the announcement that has been made? .We will sit down together and conduct a seat-by-seat analysis. We will look at which seats are vulnerable, which ones the alliance can secure, and which ones the BJP can take – we will work together as true partners. .What are the key issues the elections will be fought on? .Law and order is a major issue; the drug problem is an even bigger one, as is the state of financial health. The lack of industrialisation is another major concern. There’s a crisis regarding jobs; farmers, students. There isn't a single segment of society that is happy with the Aam Aadmi Party. They are not popular at all. People are just waiting for the Model Code of Conduct to come into effect. The moment it does, people will say, ‘We will not let them enter our villages or our cities.’ They will be completely wiped out. . What will the Alliance guarantee the youth, farmers and women? .Fixing the drug abuse issue is our top priority. We previously organised a campaign against drugs, which was highly successful. We visited every village across all 117 assembly constituencies. People shared their stories; for instance, I met a woman in Punjab who had lost all six of her sons and her husband to drug addiction. To the farmers, we are providing MSP on 24 different crops in neighbouring Haryana. As for women, look at what we are doing in the states where we have won elections. In some, we provide ₹1,100; in Haryana, we provide ₹2,100; and in West Bengal, we provide ₹3,100.

headline: Arvind Kejriwal slams BJP-SAD alliance for Punjab elections, says AAP's ties are with state's people
content: New Delhi: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday hit out at the BJP over its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the Punjab Assembly polls early next year, saying the BJP could join hands with any party out of greed for power. .He also asserted that the AAP's alliance was with the women, Scheduled Caste community, farmers and traders of Punjab. .Reacting to the announcement of the SAD-BJP alliance, Kejriwal said the two parties had repeatedly come together and parted ways for political interests. .It's 'thaggjod', says Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on SAD-BJP reunion."Sometimes they come together, sometimes they separate and then come together again. Our alliance is with the people of Punjab. We are working for the development of the state," Kejriwal said. .He said the people of Punjab have witnessed the work done by the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government over the past five years. Kejriwal said the AAP government has been trying to address the problems affecting the state for several decades. .People of Punjab have not forgotten the farmers' protest against the three farm laws, during which "more than 700 farmers had died", Kejriwal alleged. .He also referred to sacrilege incidents during the SAD government's tenure and alleged that Punjab had witnessed a period of drug abuse under its rule. .Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh said the SAD-BJP alliance would have no impact in Punjab, comparing the two parties to zeroes that added up to zero. .BJP-Akali Dal alliance will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance: PM Modi.He said the AAP was the only party in the country that sought votes on the basis of its work, adding that people should vote for it if they were satisfied with its performance. .Kejriwal also extended greetings to people on the birth anniversary of Sikhism founder Guru Nanak Dev, saying his life and teachings offer guidance in difficult times. ."His life itself was a message for the entire world. We must follow the path shown by him. Whenever we face difficulties, his life and struggles offer us solutions," he said.

headline: 'Udta Punjab' to 'Ubharta Punjab': BJP's Tarun Chugh pitches drug-free, gangs-free state
content: NEW DELHI: BJP leader Tarun Chugh on Tuesday said the party and Shiromani Akali Dal had resolved to make Punjab drug-free and free from gangsterism, extortion and organised crime.He said the state would be freed from these menaces by December 31, 2029, as the two parties prepare to contest the 2027 Punjab assembly elections together.Chugh made the remarks after paying obeisance at Gurdwara Sahib Chhevin Patshahi in Amritsar on the occasion of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's Prakash Purab. He said the BJP and SAD shared a commitment to Punjab's welfare, development and prosperity.He said the vision was to transform Punjab from 'Udta Punjab' into 'Ubharta Punjab', with development and prosperity replacing drugs, gangsterism and extortion. Chugh also expressed confidence that a double-engine government would be formed in the state.Earlier the day, Union home minister Amit Shah, announced the BJP-SAD alliance in New Delhi. He said eliminating drugs, corruption and gangsterism would be the alliance's top priorities in Punjab."Our topmost priority will be a drug-free Punjab, fixing law and order to provide security in this border state, and eliminating these gangs," Shah said. He added that these commitments would be prominently included in the manifestos of both parties.Shah also set December 31, 2029, as the deadline to eliminate drugs from the state. Targeting the Aam Aadmi Party government, he alleged that its promise to eradicate drugs within three months of coming to power had not been fulfilled.On the alliance's political arrangement, Shah said SAD would play the role of the senior partner and indicated that the chief minister would be from the party. headline: PSTET-based promotions of non-teaching staff scrapped in Punjab
content: The School Education Department has cancelled the promotions of non-teaching employees to the Master Cadre that were granted on the basis of clearing the Punjab State Teacher Eligibility Test-2 (PSTET-2). The department has directed employees who have already joined the promoted posts to return to their original cadres with immediate effect.In an order issued on November 23, the Director of School Education (Secondary) said the decision had been taken to maintain uniformity in the promotion process as the eligibility test was meant only for in-service teachers.According to the order, the department had issued a notice on April 1 inviting applications for the PSTET examination for in-service teachers. While filling out the online application forms, candidates were asked whether they were regular teachers.However, some non-teaching employees selected ‘Yes’ in response to the question. Hence, they were subsequently issued roll numbers to appear for the examination held on April 26. The result was declared on May 11.The department stated that the examination was conducted solely for in-service teachers, but a number of non-teaching employees had managed to appear for it.In view of this, the department has decided to cancel all promotions of non-teaching staff to the Master Cadre.The Director has instructed all District Education Officers (Secondary) in the state not to allow such employees to join the Master Cadre. Those who have already joined the cadre will be reverted to their respective feeder cadres, and their promotion orders will be treated as cancelled.Following the state-level directions, the District Education Officer (Secondary), Jalandhar, also issued an order on November 23 directing all Drawing and Disbursing Officers (DDOs) and heads of government senior secondary and high schools in the district to ensure strict compliance with the instructions.

headline: ‘Marriage of political convenience’: Punjab Congress slams SAD-BJP reunion
content: Chandigarh, Nov 24 (PTI) The Punjab Congress on Tuesday dismissed the reunion between SAD and the BJP as “opportunistic political arrangement”, claiming that it is a desperate exercise aimed at political survival by two parties that have lost the confidence of people of the state. Asserting that the alliance for the 2027 assembly elections would have no impact on the Congress’ electoral prospects, the party termed the tie-up as “a marriage of political convenience between two rejected political forces”. The BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced their tie-up for the Punjab Assembly polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years. Union Home Minister Amit Shah made it clear that the CM post will go to SAD if the alliance wins the 2027 elections. Launching a scathing attack on SAD and the BJP following their decision to revive their alliance, senior Congress leader Partap Singh Bajwa said, “They may have come together hoping to revive their fortunes, but Punjab’s political arithmetic is very clear: zero plus zero equals zero.” The Congress also said the alliance would have no impact on the party’s electoral prospects, recalling that it had defeated the SAD-BJP combine in the 2002 and 2017 assembly elections. “We will defeat them again in 2027,” Bajwa said. The leader of the opposition in the Punjab Assembly described the alliance as “a desperate exercise in political survival by two parties that have lost the confidence of the people of Punjab”.

headline: SAD-BJP alliance returns in a Punjab of shifting politics, deepening crisis
content: The (re)alliance between the Shiromani Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party has charged the electoral landscape of Punjab. No political party enjoys an unassailable position, as anti-incumbency gathers momentum and voters' preferences remain fluid. This renewed alliance has brought the Akali Dal and the BJP back into the contest. Congress, which appeared to be the principal beneficiary of growing anti-incumbency against the ruling Aam Aadmi Party, will need to rework its electoral game plan. In 1992, the election in Punjab was held in an exceptional environment, following the state's tryst with militancy in the 1980s. The subsequent political settlement developed unevenly, through the recovery of electoral competition, reassessment of the experience of extremism and state repression, and the search for a language capable of accommodating Punjab’s distinct communities. The Moga Declaration of 1996 by the SAD was an important articulation of this shift, rather than its single cause. Three changes lay at its core. First, Punjab’s language, resources and federal claims increasingly had to be expressed as concerns of Punjabis, rather than as the exclusive claims of Sikhs or Hindus. Second, the protection of Sikh religious institutions and the rejection of political violence acquired a wider civic meaning; violations of religious sanctity and excessive state coercion could not be treated as matters affecting only one community. Third, the legitimacy of a political party came to depend increasingly on its response to issues of livelihood, employment, welfare and governance. Of course, these tendencies coexisted with profound inequalities and recurrent breaches of trust. This was reflected in electoral alliances in the post-1992 phase. Punjab’s post-1992 political grammar rested on three commitments: To build alliances before asking for votes, to express Punjab’s demands in the name of all Punjabis, and to keep both radical violence and excessive state force outside ordinary politics. These were never observed consistently, but they defined the political centre for three decades. Akali alliance politics mirrors the change. Between 1967 and 1980, the Akalis and the Bharatiya Jana Sangh formed four post-election coalitions, each approaching the election with distinct support bases. After militancy, the SAD and BJP came together before polling. Their 1997 pre-poll alliance brought historically separate blocs into a common arrangement, and Congress and the CPI also allied before polls that year. The arrangement made cooperation across a perceived communal divide part of the offer to voters, though the seat division still reflected older rural-urban and social bases. This alliance could win with a massive majority in 1997, 2007 and 2012. The 2012 victory of the SAD-BJP government broke the expectation of a routine alternation with Congress, suggesting that voters could reward continuity when an incumbent assembled a persuasive coalition of leadership, welfare and governance. In 2022, the AAP's historic majority rested on the claim that Punjab needed a break from established parties, setting “new” against “traditional”, the latter portrayed as corrupt and undelivering. A politics initially shaped by the search for peace became a politics of performance and accountability. The BJP, post-2017, started its own experimentation by entering into alliances with splintered Akali groups, Congress breakaway factions, and learnt the hard way that their political baggage outweighed the potential gains. It was seen to be indirectly soft with radicals like Amritpal Singh, which weakened the moderate SAD. A moderate Akali Dal has historically performed an important stabilising function. It gave Sikh political aspirations a constitutional, electoral and federal platform. It became evident that when moderate Sikh politics weakens, the vacuum may be filled by radical, sectarian, preacher-led, diaspora-funded or grievance-based politics. The SAD's improved performance in the panchayat and municipal elections indicates that its organisational base has remained resilient. Notably, in several urban local bodies the party performed better than BJP, suggesting that it retains pockets of traditional support. The return of the SAD-BJP alliance for 2027 must be seen against this backdrop. This alliance is distinct from the earlier post-election and pre-election coalitions. The BJP, in the post-2017 period, while exploring its own political space in Punjab, misread its post-1990 grammar of politics. It has disproportionately relied upon symbols, personalities and commemorative narratives associated with Sikh religious history, while giving comparatively less emphasis to Punjab's wider cultural history. This created an impression that Punjab’s historical identity is synonymous with Sikh history. Consequently, the party’s engagement with the state’s intellectual ecosystem has appeared to remain largely confined to Sikh religious scholars, Sikh businessmen and Sikh opinion leaders. Ironically, this framing resembled the narrative long advanced by sections of Sikh fundamentalist thought, that Punjab should primarily be understood through an exclusively Sikh political and historical prism. Mainstream Punjab, however, has historically evolved through a much wider and more inclusive understanding. An excessive focus on Sikh identity politics risked inadvertently overlooking other equally significant social constituencies. The BJP’s Punjab problem is not insufficient Sikh outreach. It is the absence of a coherent political identity connecting Sikh outreach, Hindu confidence, imported leadership, organisational expansion and the ambition to form a government. Its inconsistency on religious issues has allowed it to appear conciliatory towards contested panthic symbolism in one context and restrictive towards uncomfortable historical representation in another. Its political inconsistency has led it to outsource organisational growth to former Congressmen while seeking Sikh support principally by weakening the moderate SAD. The central lesson is unambiguous — radicals must never be allowed to occupy moderate political space. The first target of radical politics has invariably been moderate leadership. The alliance also became necessary as Sukhbir Singh Badal could consolidate the SAD despite the many challenges. The challenge before this alliance would be how far it is able to credibly promise agrarian security and economic transformation. Farmers require viable alternatives before existing protection is withdrawn. Agricultural labourers need explicit inclusion in transition policies. Small manufacturers require reliable infrastructure, finance and access to technology. Towns need functioning services and planning capable of supporting employment. Punjab’s development agenda must therefore extend beyond the defence of its existing crop economy. Agro-processing, competitive small and medium industry, the knowledge economy and better public education require coordinated investment. A decline in agriculture’s relative economic share does not diminish farmers’ claims. It makes more urgent the creation of wider productive opportunities. The binary in Punjab has shifted in 2022, from traditional parties versus new, to regional versus national. It remains to be seen how far this alliance can reconcile this dichotomy. The writer is chairperson, Institute for Development and Communication, Chandigarh

headline: PhysicsWallah enters higher education; Punjab notifies Digital University in Patiala
content: Digital Univ​ersity​New Delhi: Edtech company PhysicsWallah (PW) is entering the formal higher education sector with the establishment of Physicswallah Digital University in Patiala, Punjab. The Punjab government notified the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, on October 29, following the Governor's assent on October 23.The move marks PW's expansion beyond school education and competitive examination preparation into undergraduate, postgraduate and career-oriented degree programmes through an online learning model.Nextseed Foundation, a wholly owned subsidiary of PhysicsWallah Limited, will serve as the sponsoring body of the university. The institution will operate on a self-financed model and is headquartered in Patiala.The university is targeting July 2027 for the commencement of its first academic session. It plans to offer programmes through five academic schools: Business and Management; Computer and Information Technology; Humanities and Social Sciences; Journalism and Media Communication; and Skills and Vocational Studies.Its proposed programme portfolio will include undergraduate and postgraduate degrees, along with certifications in areas such as Banking and Financial Services, Digital Marketing with AI and Social Media Marketing. These offerings will be subject to University Grants Commission (UGC) recognition and other applicable regulatory approvals.The university plans to adopt an AI-enabled approach to online and distance learning, integrating technology into teaching, assessments, student engagement and academic support. Its learning model will also include live sessions, faculty mentoring and global faculty connect.According to the company, the digital infrastructure will support mobile-first access and low-bandwidth connectivity, with the aim of reaching learners in smaller towns and remote locations.Speaking on the development, Alakh Pandey, Founder and Educator, PhysicsWallah, said the university would extend the company's focus on accessible and affordable education to formal higher education.“Since its inception, PW has been focused on providing students across the country with accessible quality learning at affordable costs and equal opportunity for all students irrespective of geography or economic status. The Digital University will help us take this vision into formal higher education. We want students to access good teachers, the right guidance, and learning opportunities that prepare them for robust careers,” he said.University to follow UGC regulationsThe university has been established under the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, based on the Punjab Private Digital Open Universities Policy, 2026.The framework provides for credit mobility through distance and online courses and micro-credentials, subject to applicable regulations. It also provides for an independent ombudsman to address student grievances.The institution will be required to comply with applicable UGC regulations, including those governing online and open and distance learning programmes.PW's entry into higher education comes amid growing attention to the alignment of academic programmes with industry requirements and employment opportunities. NITI Aayog's Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047 report, citing the Economic Survey 2024-25, notes that 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications.With the proposed university, PW aims to extend its education offerings to degree-led learning and career-oriented programmes, building on its existing digital infrastructure and academic capabilities.

headline: The OGs reunite: SAD gets 'bada bhai' tag in Punjab, but BJP has bigger ambitions
content: NEW DELHI: Two of Punjab's oldest political allies are back together, six years after a bitter parting over the contentious farm laws. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, reviving a partnership that once governed the state for 15 years across three terms.The reunion, announced on the Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, brings together parties whose relationship was famously described by former Punjab chief minister Parkash Singh Badal as "nau-maas da rishta", the bond between the nail and the flesh.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed the development, saying the alliance would put Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first."Ours is a natural alliance that will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress," he said in a post on X, adding that the partnership, nurtured by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, LK Advani and Parkash Singh Badal, had "stood the test of time".Union home minister Amit Shah, who announced the reunion alongside BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, called the Akali Dal the NDA's "oldest ally" and said PM Modi had described the development by saying the "NDA is now complete".Shah also said SAD would retain its senior-partner status, adding that the "big brother" would get the chief minister's post. "Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," the Union minister said at the joint press conference.The two parties will contest all 117 assembly seats together, although the seat-sharing arrangement is yet to be finalised.The reunion comes after months of political manoeuvring, including Sukhbir Badal's meeting with PM Modi in August and a shift in SAD's position on the Centre's delimitation proposal. It also brings together two parties whose electoral fortunes have declined sharply since their separation.However, Punjab is no longer the state in which the old alliance enjoyed its strongest run. AAP has emerged as the dominant force, Congress remains a significant contender, and the BJP and SAD have both undergone changes in their support bases and political strategies.Why SAD-BJP patched upThe partnership actually predates the BJP. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, shared power with the Akalis in Punjab as far back as 1967 and 1969. The modern alliance, however, was forged in 1996, when SAD's Moga Declaration pivoted from purely Panthic politics to a broader pitch of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat."The partnership brought together the Akalis' predominantly rural Sikh support base and the BJP's largely urban Hindu constituency. It also helped both parties build a political coalition in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab.The alliance won 93 of 117 assembly seats in 1997, with SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. After losing power to Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 and retained power in 2012, winning 67 and 68 seats respectively.ALSO READ: From 'nau-mass da rishta' to bitter rivals and back; how BJP-SAD relations played out over the yearsBut the emergence of AAP, coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, weakened the alliance. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three.The final rupture came in September 2020, when SAD walked out of the NDA over the Centre's three farm laws. Sukhbir Badal's wife Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister on September 17, and the Akali Dal formally ended its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP nine days later.The laws were repealed in November 2021, but the political damage endured.The alliance's decline is evident from its electoral record. In 2007, SAD won 48 seats and the BJP 19, taking their combined tally to 67. They improved to 68 seats in 2012, with SAD winning 56 and the BJP 12. But the numbers fell sharply thereafter. In 2017, SAD was reduced to 15 seats and the BJP to three. By the 2022 assembly elections, the two parties managed just five seats between them, with SAD winning three and the BJP two.In 2022, SAD secured 18.38% of the vote and the BJP 6.60%, while AAP swept the election with 92 seats and a 42.01% vote share.Their separate performance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections provided another reason to reconsider the alliance. The BJP failed to win any of Punjab's 13 seats despite securing 18.56% of the vote. SAD won one seat, Bathinda, with 13.42%.ALSO READ: From 9.63% to 18.56% - BJP’s saving grace after drawing a blank in PunjabTogether, their vote shares added up to nearly 32%, compared with 26.30% for Congress and 26.02% for AAP.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The numbers make a case for pooling their support bases, although the combined vote share does not automatically translate into transferable votes or assembly seats.For the BJP, the alliance offers access to SAD's traditional rural and Sikh support networks. For the Akali Dal, it brings back a national ally and an opportunity to rebuild its electoral machinery, which is the BJP's strong suit.Sukhbir Singh Badal described the reunion as more than an electoral arrangement."This is not just a political alliance. There is an emotional bond. As my late father used to say, Akali Dal-BJP is an inseparable, deeply bonded relationship," he said.Six years later, a very different PunjabThe old partners are back again, but the state the BJP and SAD are returning to is markedly different from the one they left behind in 2020.The 2027 assembly election will be the alliance's first major state-level electoral test without Parkash Singh Badal, the five-time CM who died in April 2023. A towering figure in the Akali Dal, he was also a key bridge between the SAD and the BJP. Though Sukhbir Badal was already leading the party before his father's death, he now has to rebuild the party's standing without his political stature and influence.Another factor the alliance must keep in mind is that the farm issue has not disappeared. The repeal of the three farm laws did not automatically undo the distrust they created. Farmers' demands, including a legal guarantee for minimum support price, remain unresolved, keeping the issue politically alive in an agrarian state like Punjab. The BJP-SAD alliance will have to reckon with that trust deficit, particularly in the rural Malwa belt, which is the largest and most populous region covering major farming districts like Bathinda, Mansa, Sangrur, Patiala, Ludhiana and Muktsar.This is why the choice of Gurpurab for the reunion announcement is rich in symbolism. PM Modi had announced the repeal of the farm laws on the occasion in November 2021. The two parties have now chosen the same religious occasion to announce their political reconciliation. Whether that symbolism can translate into renewed trust among farmers is a different question.Another thing that has changed is that the Akali Dal can no longer assume that it commands the entire Panthic vote. In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, independent candidates Amritpal Singh and Sarabjeet Singh Khalsa won from Khadoor Sahib and Faridkot, respectively. Between them, they also led in 15 assembly segments.ALSO READ: 'O Captain, My Captain' - Should Congress make room for Amarinder Singh again?This makes the party's return to its traditional Panthic space more difficult. The SAD has tried to reconnect with its core constituency through issues of Sikh identity and historical memory. The controversy surrounding 'Satluj', a film based on activist Jaswant Singh Khalra's work documenting alleged extrajudicial killings in Punjab, offered one such opportunity. After the film was taken down from an OTT platform, Sukhbir Badal announced screenings across the state, saying young people should know about the events it depicts.The bigger, bolder BJPSix years on its own have transformed the BJP from a junior partner that contested just 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats into a more assertive player. Under the old arrangement, the SAD contested 94 assembly seats and the BJP 23, largely in urban constituencies. For the Lok Sabha elections, the split was 10 seats for the Akalis and three for the BJP.Its vote share in the 2024 Lok Sabha election rose to 18.56 per cent, up from 9.63 per cent in 2019. The BJP contested all 13 seats in 2024, compared with just three under the old seat-sharing arrangement in 2019. Though it won no seats, the saffron party's vote share was higher than the SAD's 13.42 per cent. In the 2022 assembly election, the BJP had polled 6.60 per cent and won two seats.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();The party has also strengthened its ranks through a steady stream of defections. In April 2026, AAP Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha led six other MPs into the BJP which included Sandeep Pathak, Ashok Mittal, Harbhajan Singh, Vikramjit Singh Sahney, Rajinder Gupta and Swati Maliwal. Six of these seven were Rajya Sabha members from Punjab. The exits dealt a major blow to the AAP's parliamentary strength and brought into the BJP leaders who had been closely associated with the party's Punjab strategy. Chadha and Pathak, in particular, had played key roles in the AAP's political and electoral planning.The BJP has since moved to put these former AAP leaders to work against their old party. Chadha and Harbhajan Singh have been named to its Punjab manifesto committee, while Pathak, Mittal, Sahney and other former AAP MPs have been assigned roles in the party's chargesheet committee, which will prepare its case against the Bhagwant Mann government.Earlier, in March 2024, AAP's then Jalandhar MP Sushil Kumar Rinku and Jalandhar West MLA Sheetal Angural had also joined the BJP. In November 2026, three more AAP legislators, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, crossed over. The BJP has also inducted senior Akali leaders, including Surinder Singh Chauhan and Jaswinderpal Sohal, as well as AAP functionaries from Moga led by spokesperson Navdeep Singh Sangha.The BJP's recruitment drive has not been limited to the AAP and SAD. Its Punjab ranks also include former Congress leaders such as Sunil Jakhar, Manpreet Singh Badal, Ravneet Singh Bittu and Preneet Kaur.That changes the terms of the reunion. The BJP returns with a larger vote share, a wider organisational footprint and experienced leaders. The SAD, meanwhile, needs the alliance to recover lost ground and reconnect with rural voters. Amit Shah has announced that the BJP is okay with the junior-partner label in the alliance. It is, however, unlikely that the BJP will settle for the old seat-sharing formula.Can the alliance unsettle AAP?The immediate target of the alliance is the AAP government, which swept to power in 2022 with 92 seats and 42.01 per cent of the vote. Its vote share fell to 26.02 per cent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election, when it won three seats, but it remains a formidable player.The SAD-BJP reunion gives the opposition a potentially stronger combination of urban and rural networks. It could also help consolidate voters who want an alternative to the AAP government. The drug problem, in particular, is likely to be a central campaign issue.At his press conference, Amit Shah listed three priorities for a future NDA government: eliminating drugs, eliminating corruption and strengthening nationalist forces. He promised that Punjab would be "completely drug-free" by December 31, 2029. He also targeted Congress, recalling Rahul Gandhi's 2017 promise that drugs would be eliminated within one term and accusing the party of doing nothing when it was in power.The attack gives the alliance a ready-made campaign plank. But it also puts the BJP and SAD on the spot, as both parties have been part of Punjab's political establishment for decades. The voters, thus, will judge their record as well as their promises.There is another complication. The Congress remains a strong third front and could split the anti-incumbency vote. Rural Sikh voters who continue to view the BJP through the lens of the farm agitation may also be reluctant to back the reunited partners. The AAP could benefit if opposition votes remain divided.The BJP-SAD reunion also complicates the Congress's position. With an established opposition pole, the contest for voters dissatisfied with the AAP government will now intensify. Amit Shah's attack on the Congress over its record on drugs made it clear that the alliance intends to take on both the ruling party and its principal rival.The Congress can still draw on its independent support base, but it will have to navigate a more crowded opposition space, as well as its own internal factional differences.Six years after a split that left both allies on the margins, the BJP and the Shiromani Akali Dal have chosen pragmatism over past grievances to challenge AAP and Congress. The 2027 election, however, will not be a simple replay of the coalition's past victories. And tough seat-sharing talks are yet to be held.The OGs may be back together, but winning over a changed Punjab will require more than old chemistry.Get the latest India News and Live updates.
