headline: Much-needed step, in larger interest of Punjab: BJP leader Sodhi on SAD-BJP alliance
content: Chandigarh, Nov 24 (PTI) Senior BJP leader and former minister Rana Gurmit Singh Sodhi on Tuesday described the reunion between SAD and the BJP for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls as a “timely and much-needed step in the larger interest of the state and its people”. Earlier, the BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) announced their tie-up for the upcoming Punjab Assembly polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah making it clear that the CM post will go to the SAD as it would be the “big brother” in the alliance. Welcoming the alliance, Sodhi said it was not about political gains, positions or ministerial ambitions but about Punjab and its people. “At a critical juncture, the state needs collective resolve, a shared vision and decisive action to address the challenges confronting it. This alliance is the need of the hour to put Punjab back on the path of peace, progress and prosperity,” Sodhi said in a statement. Highlighting the pressing concerns facing Punjab, Sodhi said tackling the drug menace, addressing unemployment, creating opportunities for the youth, safeguarding farmers’ interests, improving law and order and reviving Punjab’s economy must be among the foremost priorities. “Our youth deserve opportunities, our farmers deserve security and dignity, and every Punjabi deserves a future filled with hope and possibilities. We cannot afford to let another generation suffer because of drugs, unemployment and lack of opportunities. Punjab needs focused leadership and a concrete roadmap for development,” he added.

headline: It's 'thaggjod', says Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on SAD-BJP reunion
content: Chandigarh: Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday called the reunion between the SAD and the BJP a 'thaggjod' (a pact of cheaters) and asked people not to trust them again. ."Do not trust them. This is not an 'gathjod', it is a 'thaggjod'. They are out to loot Punjab again," he alleged. .The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced their tie-up for the upcoming Punjab polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah making it clear that the chief ministerial post will go to the SAD as it would be the "elder brother" in the alliance. .BJP-Akali Dal alliance will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance: PM Modi.Slamming the previous Akali-BJP governments, Mann said from 2007 to 2017, this very alliance was in power and they ruled for 10 years. ."Drugs were introduced in Punjab during that time. 'Beadbi' (sacrilege incidents) happened during their rule in 2015," alleged Mann in a video statement. .With what face do they now say they have a 'nau-maas da rishta' (the bond between the nail and the flesh), he asked. ."Sometimes they break this nail-and-flesh bond, and sometimes they rejoin it," he said. .Mann said just recently, these parties were saying they would contest all 117 assembly seats. .Now they say, 'We have formed an alliance to save Punjab', he said. ."Are they saving Punjab's interests or whose interests? This is an alliance to save the family," Mann alleged. .He said the Aam Aadmi Party's alliance is with the 3.25 crore people of Punjab. ."We have alliance with the mothers of Punjab. It is with the farmers of Punjab who are getting electricity for farming and canal water. It is with the common people of Punjab, 90 per cent of whom get zero electricity bills. We gave over 70,000 jobs, he said adding that these jobs were given on merit. ."Our alliance is with those thousands of parents whose children we are giving a great education through schools like the schools of eminence. Children are clearing the NEET exam and moving ahead by passing big competitive exams. Our alliance is with them," he said.

headline: Rs 3.5 lakh bribe to settle case? Punjab and Haryana High Court rejects cop’s plea
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has denied anticipatory bail to a Special Police Officer (SPO) accused of demanding Rs 3.5 lakh to settle a criminal case, observing that custodial interrogation was necessary for an effective investigation and to unravel the truth. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the anticipatory bail plea of the accused, who had approached the High Court after the sessions court had rejected his plea. "It is imperative that every person in the Society can expect an atmosphere free from foreboding & fear of any transgression. At this stage, there is no material on record to hold that prima facie case is not made out against the petitioner. The material which has come on record and preliminary investigation appear to establish a reasonable basis for the accusations," the order read. Why did the court reject the plea? According to the prosecution, the petitioner had earlier registered an FIR in 2024 against three men under various provisions of the Indian Penal Code. In September that year, he allegedly demanded Rs 3.5 lakh from them to facilitate a compromise in the case. It was stated that the petitioner subsequently got a compromise affidavit prepared; however, he allegedly failed to appear before the court to honour the compromise. The prosecution stated that the petitioner returned Rs 2.3 lakh but allegedly retained the remaining Rs 1.2 lakh. The counsel for the petitioner said that the allegations were concocted and that no recovery of the alleged amount was effected. The counsel for the state however opposed the plea stating that considering the seriousness of the allegations, custodial interrogation of the petitioner was necessary for fair and effective investigation. Considering the seriousness of the allegations, the court said that the petitioner did not deserve the relief. The High Court said the petitioner's allegations of false implication and other disputed claims would have to be examined on the basis of evidence during the trial and could not be conclusively determined at the anticipatory bail stage. "No cause.has been shown, at this stage, from which it can be deciphered that the petitioner has been falsely implicated into the present FIR," it noted. The court said that while considering an anticipatory bail plea, it ought to consider the magnitude and nature of the offence; the role attributed to the accused; the need for fair and free investigation as also the deeper and wider impact of such alleged iniquities on the society. The court noted that the material on record and preliminary investigation appeared to establish a reasonable basis for the accusations. "In view of the seriousness of the allegations, this Court finds no compelling ground to extend the benefit of discretionary relief to the petitioner. Moreover, custodial interrogation of the petitioner is necessary for an effective investigation & to unravel the truth. The petition is, thus, devoid of merits and is hereby dismissed," the order read.

headline: Modi, Badal meeting in August gave first indication of reunion between SAD, BJP
content: Chandigarh: It was a meeting between Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal and Prime Minister Narendra Modi in August that gave the first indication of a possible reunion between the former allies for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls. .Though both the parties sought to downplay the meeting between Modi and Badal at that time, there was buzz in political circles that both the estranged allies were on a path to a reunion. .Badal had met Modi at his office in Parliament House. .'NDA’s oldest ally is returning': BJP, Akali Dal join hands for 2027 Punjab elections six years after parting ways.Neither of the parties publicly acknowledged talks for a possible re-stitching of an alliance that broke six years ago by the SAD over the three farm laws, which were later repealed. .Punjab BJP leaders consistently maintained that the party was preparing to fight all 117 Assembly segments in the state. .Talks of reunion again gained prominence when Union Home Minister Amit Shah, last month in Delhi, predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027. .He had then said that the people of Punjab had decided that there was going to be an NDA government there this time. .His remarks again fuelled speculation in the political circles about an imminent reunion between the SAD and the BJP. .Shah, when he came to Chandigarh on November 1, again said an NDA government will be formed in the border state. .His statement came months after he had said in his party's rally in Moga that the BJP would fight the 2027 elections to form its own government. .On November 2, when SAD president Badal was asked about the possibility of re-alliance, he gave a guarded response to speculation, saying, "You will come to know in a few days what will happen." .The leadership of both the parties reopened channels for talks for a possible reunion and held discussions over seat-sharing arrangements. .Ground surveys by both the parties indicated that it was better to join hands rather than fight the elections separately. .The BJP and the SAD, on Tuesday, being celebrated as Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, announced their tie-up for the upcoming Punjab Assembly polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years, with Shah making it clear that the chief minister's post will go to the SAD as it would be the "big brother" in the alliance. .This alliance was important to save Punjab, said an Akali leader. .A Punjab BJP leader said saving Punjab is a main agenda as he targeted the AAP government over the issues of deteriorating law and order and the drug menace. .Journey of SAD-BJP alliance | From 'nail and flesh bond' to rupture and then reunion.The SAD quit with the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in September 2020 over the three farm laws, which were later repealed. .The previous alliance between the SAD and the BJP was often seen as a symbol of Hindu-Sikh unity. Both the SAD and the BJP formed governments in Punjab in 1997, 2007 and 2012. .SAD patriarch and five-time chief minister late Parkash Singh Badal had described his party's relationship with the BJP as "nau-maas da rishta" (the bond between the nail and the flesh). .After both the parties parted ways, the SAD and the BJP fought the 2022 Punjab Assembly polls and the 2024 Lok Sabha polls separately, and their individual electoral performances remained dismal. .In the 2022 Assembly polls, the BJP won two seats and the SAD could register victories in three Assembly segments out of a total 117-member Assembly. .During the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the BJP failed to open an account, while the SAD won only one seat from Bathinda out of 13 parliamentary constituencies. .However, the vote share of BJP doubled to 18.56 per cent, as compared to 9.63 per cent in 2019. .With the Punjab BJP, leaders like former chief minister Amarinder Singh and former Punjab BJP chief Sunil Jakhar had been consistently advocating for the alliance with the SAD, stressing that it was important for communal harmony in the state. .Before ending the electoral alliance, both the Akalis and the BJP used to fight together. .According to the previous pact in the Assembly polls, the BJP used to contest 23 seats and the SAD 94 Assembly seats. In parliamentary polls, the SAD used to contest 10 seats and the BJP the remaining three.

headline: ‘Thug pact’ to save own families, seats: Bhagwant Mann slams SAD-BJP alliance | India News
content: Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann on Tuesday hit out at the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the BJP over their alliance ahead of polls in Punjab, calling it a ‘thug pact’ and alleging that the tie-up was aimed at protecting their political interests rather than serving the people of Punjab. Mann claimed the alliance was an attempt by the two parties to safeguard their families and electoral seats.“This alliance between the Akali Dal and the BJP is not for Punjab, but a 'thug pact' to save their own families and seats... Those who, until yesterday, were cursing each other over the three farm laws, Punjab's water, Chandigarh and Sikh institutions have today come together again, lured by the temptation of power,” Mann posted on X.Earlier on Tuesday, BJP and SAD revived their alliance for the upcoming Punjab assembly polls six years after the Akali Dal broke away from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).Also Read | ‘Natural alliance’: PM Modi says BJP-SAD reunion will ensure pro-people governance in PunjabContinuing his attack on the alliance, Mann said traditional political leaders who had spent 20 years engaging in ‘Nura Kushti’ (a staged fight) with one another had now come together on the same platform. Mann said that the people of Punjab would not forget the drug menace that prevailed in the state between 2007 and 2017. Also Read | BJP-SAD reunion: Can the alliance alter Punjab's political landscape?The chief minister said that the Aam Aadmi Party's (AAP) alliance was only with Punjab's 3.25 crore people. Highlighting his government's initiatives, he cited free electricity, canal water, mohalla clinics, Schools of Eminence and government jobs without bribes as examples of its positive politics. The chief minister added that the Aam Aadmi Party's (AAP) alliance was only with Punjab's 3.25 crore people. Highlighting his government's initiatives, he cited free electricity, canal water, mohalla clinics, Schools of Eminence and government jobs without bribes as examples of its positive politics.Mann said Punjabis would never accept what he described as the SAD-BJP's ‘thug pact’.

headline: BJP-Akali Dal alliance will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance: PM Modi
content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday said that he was extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) returned to the NDA and was confident that the coalition will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab. .The BJP and SAD on Tuesday announced their alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections, describing it as a "national and emotional" pact. ."Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji," Modi said in a post on 'X'. .'Directionless alliance': Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for assembly polls.The prime minister said the BJP and the Akali Dal have a natural alliance which will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress. ."Nurtured by Atal Ji, Advani Ji and Sardar Parkash Singh Badal Ji, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. I am confident that our Alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab," he said.

headline: After SAD-BJP reunion, Kejriwal says AAP’s alliance with Punjab’s people | Hindustan Times
content: Chandigarh: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday slammed the BJP over its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the upcoming assembly elections in Punjab, accusing it of joining hands with anyone for the sake of power.Reacting to the SAD-BJP reunion announced by Union home minister Amit Shah and SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, Kejriwal said the two parties had repeatedly come together and separated for political interests. “They come together, they part ways and then again come together,” he said. He said his party’s alliance was with the people. “Our alliance is with the women, farmers, Scheduled Caste community and traders of Punjab,” he added.Defending the Bhagwant Mann government’s record, Kejriwal said the people of Punjab had witnessed the work his government undertook over the past five years to address problems that plagued the state for several decades. Taking a swipe at the alliance, he referred to the farmers’ protests against the farm laws during which more than 700 farmers had “lost their lives”.Another AAP leader, finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema, described the renewed SAD-BJP partnership as an unprincipled alliance. He said the people of Punjab, particularly farmers, know how the BJP had enacted the three “black farm laws” with the SAD as its alliance partner, resulting in the deaths of 750 farmers during the protests. “The two parties have come together once again for the sake of power. It was during their rule from 2007-17 that the scourge of chitta and other drugs spread in Punjab. Now, the Mann government is waging a war against drugs,” he claimed. He also alleged that incidents of sacrilege (beadbi) of Guru Granth Sahib occurred on a large scale during the SAD-BJP regime. “People of Punjab have not been able to forget the Behbal Kalan and Bargari incidents. They will never accept this unholy alliance,” he said.

headline: 'Big brother' Akali Dal will have CM post: Amit Shah on Punjab Assembly elections
content: Announcing BJP's alliance with Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the upcoming Assembly elections in Punjab, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday said the chief minister post will go to the SAD as it would be the "big brother" in the alliance. Shah said the two parties would contest all 117 seats in Punjab. Announcing the alliance at a press conference in New Delhi along with Shah and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, BJP chief Nitin Nabin said the two parties will work together to make Punjab a developed state. Badal exuded confidence that the alliance will win more than 100 seats in the polls and that the AAP's seat tally in Punjab will drop to single digits. .'Directionless alliance': Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for assembly polls."BJP-SAD will resolve all issues in Punjab, including drug menace," Badal said while describing the tie-up as an "emotional alliance". Shah said a detailed manifesto would be finalised soon by the two parties for the Assembly elections, but eradicating the drug menace from Punjab and working together for the welfare of farmers and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity would be among the key focus areas. "The BJP's promise of resolving farmer issues and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity will get a boost with SAD joining hands with us," he said. "BJP's oldest ally Shiromani Akali Dal is back in NDA; we wholeheartedly welcome their return," Shah said, adding that Prime Minister Modi is very happy with the SAD's return to the NDA. He said the NDA is now complete with the Akali Dal coming back to its fold. Nabin said it is a "natural" alliance for the benefit of the people of Punjab and for Hindu-Sikh unity. "BJP-SAD alliance will work together to make Punjab a developed state, seat-sharing talks will take place soon," he said.

headline: Kejriwal slams BJP-SAD alliance, says AAP's ties are with Punjab's people
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday hit out at the BJP over its alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) for the Punjab Assembly polls early next year, saying the BJP could join hands with any party out of greed for power.He also asserted that the AAP's alliance was with the women, Scheduled Caste community, farmers and traders of Punjab.Reacting to the announcement of the SAD-BJP alliance, Kejriwal said the two parties had repeatedly come together and parted ways for political interests."Sometimes they come together, sometimes they separate and then come together again. Our alliance is with the people of Punjab. We are working for the development of the state," Kejriwal said.He said the people of Punjab have witnessed the work done by the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government over the past five years. Kejriwal said the AAP government has been trying to address the problems affecting the state for several decades.People of Punjab have not forgotten the farmers' protest against the three farm laws, during which "more than 700 farmers had died", Kejriwal alleged.He also referred to sacrilege incidents during the SAD government's tenure and alleged that Punjab had witnessed a period of drug abuse under its rule.Delhi AAP MLA Jarnail Singh said the SAD-BJP alliance would have no impact in Punjab, comparing the two parties to zeroes that added up to zero.He said the AAP was the only party in the country that sought votes on the basis of its work, adding that people should vote for it if they were satisfied with its performance.Kejriwal also extended greetings to people on the birth anniversary of Sikhism founder Guru Nanak Dev, saying his life and teachings offer guidance in difficult times."His life itself was a message for the entire world. We must follow the path shown by him. Whenever we face difficulties, his life and struggles offer us solutions," he said.

headline: SAD-BJP reunion ‘desperate marriage of convenience’: Punjab Congress | Hindustan Times
content: Chandigarh: Punjab Congress leaders on Tuesday dismissed the reunion of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) as an exercise in “opportunistic politics” and political survival, asserting that the alliance would have no impact on the Congress’s prospects in the 2027 assembly elections.Pradesh Congress Committee (PCC) chief Pargat Singh dismissed the tie-up as “directionless and opportunistic politics,” stating that core issues concerning farmers and the Badal family’s role in the state remained unresolved.“I would like to wish both of them good luck, but the issues remain exactly the same—what happened to the farmers, what was done to Punjab, and what the Badal family did,” he said, alleging that the BJP-led Centre had weakened democratic institutions over the past decade.Describing the tie-up as a “desperate exercise in political survival,” Leader of the Opposition (LoP) in the Punjab Vidhan Sabha Partap Singh Bajwa said both parties had lost public confidence and could not independently regain lost ground. “This is nothing but a marriage of political convenience between two rejected political forces. They may have come together hoping to revive their fortunes, but Punjab’s political arithmetic is clear: Zero plus zero equals zero. No amount of political manoeuvring can manufacture public support that does not exist,” Bajwa said. Former PPCC chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring termed the alliance “the most opportunistic,” arguing that the two parties had effectively remained aligned even without a formal arrangement. Accusing SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal of shifting his stance out of desperation, Warring alleged that Badal had betrayed Punjabis by aligning with what he called the RSS’s “sinister designs over Punjab.”Asserting that the reunion would make no difference to the Congress, Warring pointed to the party’s assembly election victories in 2002 and 2017—both won when the SAD and BJP contested together—and said the Congress was ready to take on the alliance in 2027.Echoing concerns over the agricultural policy, Bajwa questioned the ideological credibility of the alliance, recalling that the SAD had quit the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in September 2020 over the Centre’s three farm laws, with Sukhbir citing the lack of a statutory guarantee for minimum support price (MSP) and Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigning from the Union cabinet.“At that time, Sukhbir Badal told Punjabis that he was leaving the NDA to defend the interests of farmers. Today, he is sitting alongside the very same BJP leadership. What has changed? Have the farmers’ concerns been resolved? Has a legal guarantee for MSP been enacted?” Bajwa asked, adding that the repeal of the farm laws did not settle all issues raised during the farmers’ agitation.The LoP also challenged the SAD chief to clarify whether he would press Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah to scrap the Agnipath military recruitment scheme and restore regular army recruitment, as well as reopen cross-border trade routes—including trade suspended in 2019 and commercial connectivity via the Kartarpur Corridor.On the issue of narcotics, Bajwa said the BJP-led central government must explain what concrete steps it has taken to dismantle interstate and international drug supply chains and their financial networks, adding that neither party could absolve itself of its past record through a fresh electoral tie-up.“The people of Punjab are not looking for partnerships designed to save political careers. They are looking for accountability and a credible vision for their future. In Punjab, zero plus zero will remain zero,” Bajwa added.

headline: Punjab BJP describes reunion with SAD as a historic step
content: Chandigarh, Nov 24 (PTI) Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon and other senior leaders on Tuesday described the party’s reunion with SAD as a historic step for the state’s future, peace and prosperity. The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) announced their tie-up for the upcoming Punjab Assembly polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years, with Union Home Minister Amit Shah making it clear that the CM post will go to the SAD as it would be the “big brother” in the alliance. “The announcement of the alliance between the Bharatiya Janata Party and the Shiromani Akali Dal is a historic step for Punjab’s future, peace and prosperity,” Dhillon said in a post on X in Punjabi. Dhillon said the formation of this alliance on the occasion of the ‘Prakash Purab’ of Guru Nanak Dev also reflects a commitment to further strengthening Punjab’s communal harmony. Dhillon lashed out at the ruling Aam Aadmi Party in Punjab, alleging that under their promise of ‘false badlav (change)’, Punjab is struggling with drugs, gangsterism, extortion and unemployment. “Our first priority will be restoring peace and the rule of law and eliminating drugs (if SAD-BJP come to power),” he said.

headline: 'Directionless alliance': Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for assembly polls
content: Chandigarh: Punjab Congress President Pargat Singh on Tuesday slammed the BJP-SAD tie-up for the state assembly polls, saying the two parties re-stitched the alliance owing to their "greed" for power. .Both the parties, he claimed, lacked any development agenda or roadmap for taking the border state on the path of progress and prosperity. ."It is a directionless alliance," Singh told PTI while reacting to the SAD and BJP coming together for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls. ."The reunion between the SAD and the BJP is only for the greed for power," he alleged. .'NDA’s oldest ally is returning': BJP, Akali Dal join hands for 2027 Punjab elections six years after parting ways."They have no development agenda for Punjab or roadmap for the state's progress. They have joined hands merely for their own development. They have joined hands again with a single motive to capture power in Punjab," he said, while asserting that both the parties do not have any chance of forming the next government in Punjab. .Singh asked SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal to explain to the people why he quit the NDA earlier. .Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP President Nitin Nabin and the SAD chief made the alliance announcement ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls. .The Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal had snapped its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the now-scrapped three farm laws. .Earlier, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, who was also part of the Modi government as a minister with Cabinet rank, had also resigned.

headline: Journey of SAD-BJP alliance | From 'nail and flesh bond' to rupture and then reunion
content: New Delhi: For years, Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) patriarch Parkash Singh Badal described his party's relationship with the BJP as "nau-maas da rishta" (the bond between the nail and the flesh), projecting the alliance as much as a guarantor of communal harmony in Punjab. .The partnership, which saw the two parties govern Punjab for 15 years across three five-year terms, came apart in September 2020 when the Akalis walked out of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the Centre's three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. .On Tuesday, as the two parties announced the revival of their alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls, SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal invoked his late father's description of the relationship at a joint press conference with Union Home Minister Amit Shah and BJP national president Nitin Nabin at the BJP headquarters here. .Punjab BJP forms state election committee for 2027 Assembly polls.Shah welcomed the return of the NDA's "oldest ally", while Nabin described the partnership as a "natural alliance". .The announcement, coinciding with the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev, capped months of negotiations between the two parties, which have suffered successive electoral setbacks in Punjab after parting ways. .The association predates the formation of the BJP in 1980. Its predecessor, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, was part of coalition governments with the Akalis in 1967 and 1969 following Punjab's reorganisation. .The partnership in its modern form took shape in 1996, when the SAD, through its Moga Declaration, sought to broaden its appeal beyond its traditional Panthic constituency by embracing the idea of "Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat". .Coming in the aftermath of militancy in Punjab, the alliance brought together the predominantly rural Sikh constituency of the Akalis and the BJP's largely urban Hindu support base. .Under their longstanding seat-sharing arrangement, the SAD contested 94 of the 117 assembly seats, leaving 23 for the BJP. In Lok Sabha polls, the corresponding figures were 10 and three. The alliance won 93 seats in the 1997 assembly polls -- the SAD bagging 75 and the BJP 18. .After losing power to the Congress in 2002, the combine returned to office in 2007 with 68 seats and retained power in 2012 with an identical tally, bucking Punjab's trend of voting out incumbent governments. However, the emergence of the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), coupled with public anger over incidents of sacrilege and the drug menace, reduced the SAD to 15 seats and the BJP to three in 2017. .Three years later, the farmers' agitation against the Centre's agricultural reform measures brought differences between the two parties to a head. On September 17, 2020, Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned as Union food processing industries minister. Nine days later, the SAD snapped its 24-year-old electoral partnership with the BJP. .'NDA’s oldest ally is returning': BJP, Akali Dal join hands for 2027 Punjab elections six years after parting ways.Sukhbir Badal linked the deterioration in ties to the BJP's growing numerical strength in Parliament, accusing it of not taking allies into confidence on major policy decisions. In subsequent years, the Akalis accused the BJP of interfering in Sikh religious affairs, even as several senior SAD leaders crossed over to the saffron party. .The BJP, meanwhile, sought to shed its image as the junior partner, with its leaders arguing that the alliance had restricted its organisational expansion in rural Punjab. The repeal of the farm laws in November 2021 did not immediately pave the way for a rapprochement, but electoral compulsions made it inevitable after a point. .In the 2022 assembly polls, the SAD, contesting in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), won just three seats, with its vote share falling from 25.24 per cent in 2017 to 18.38 per cent. The BJP, which tied up with Amarinder Singh's Punjab Lok Congress and Sukhdev Singh Dhindsa-led SAD (Sanyukt), won two seats. The AAP swept Punjab, winning 92 seats. .Efforts to revive the alliance ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls failed amid renewed farmers' protests. In 2019, the SAD and the BJP had won two Lok Sabha seats each, polling a combined 37.08 per cent of the votes. Five years later, the BJP's vote share rose from 9.63 per cent to 18.56 per cent as it contested all 13 seats, while the SAD's fell from 27.45 per cent to 13.42 per cent. .The BJP drew a blank, while the SAD retained Bathinda. Their combined vote share of nearly 32 per cent was, however, higher than that of either the Congress or the AAP. This strengthened the proponents of reviving the alliance. .The signals became more pronounced this year. On August 7, Sukhbir Badal called on Prime Minister Narendra Modi at Parliament House, fuelling speculation over a reunion. Harsimrat Kaur Badal, whose resignation had set the separation in motion, publicly recalled the developmental benefits of the alliance. Her brother and senior SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia also advocated a reunion. .Punjab Assembly elections 2027: Six years after split, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance.In October, Shah predicted that an NDA government would assume office in Punjab in 2027, reiterating it in Chandigarh on November 1. Asked about an alliance on November 2, Badal said, "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen." .While the BJP has spent the last six years making efforts to expand its organisational footprint in Punjab, the SAD is fighting to reclaim lost political ground.

headline: 'NDA’s oldest ally is returning': BJP, Akali Dal join hands for 2027 Punjab elections six years after parting ways
content: New Delhi: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced a pre-poll alliance for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, bringing the two former allies together six years after their relationship ended over the Centre’s three farm laws. The SAD, however, will continue to be the “senior” partner in the alliance. The announcement was made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah at a joint press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, attended by BJP President Nitin Nabin and SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal. “It is a matter of great happiness that NDA’s oldest ally, the Shiromani Akali Dal, is returning to the NDA once again today,” Shah said. “Both the BJP and the Akali Dal have decided to fight the Punjab Assembly elections together,” Shah said. Badal said that the alliance reflects the mood of the people. .It's 'thaggjod', says Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann on SAD-BJP reunion.Seat-sharing arrangements are being talked out by the two parties, and a final announcement is to be expected soon. Previously, the SAD contested 94 seats and the BJP 23. Responding to a question on which party the chief minister be from, Shah said that SAD will choose one. “We will fight on all the 117 seats, but SAD will play the big brother’s role, and the big brother is the chief minister,” Shah said, putting an end to speculations. Shah said the prime minister had described it as a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood. “Badal Sahab has shared a deep, long-standing relationship with us, just as there has been a profound bond between the BJP and the Akali Dal. I believe that this alliance will serve as a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood — not just in Punjab, but across the nation and the world,” Shah said. Shah also made the eradication of drugs a key electoral promise, asserting that the NDA would work towards making Punjab drug-free by December 2029. He accused successive AAP and Congress governments of failing to tackle the drug menace, and said the alliance would also focus on addressing corruption and restoring Punjab’s security and prosperity. .BJP-Akali Dal alliance will ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance: PM Modi.BJP President Nitin Nabin described the partnership as a “natural alliance” and expressed confidence that the two parties would emerge victorious in the 2027 elections. The reunion marks the revival of a political alliance that lasted for 24 years before the SAD walked out of the NDA in September 2020 over the three contentious farm laws, which were subsequently repealed. The two parties had shared power in Punjab for three consecutive terms, forming governments in 1997, 2007 and 2012 under the leadership of Parkash Singh Badal. In the 2022 Assembly elections, fought separately, the BJP won two seats while the SAD managed three in the 117-member House. The Aam Aadmi Party swept the election with 92 seats.

headline: NAREP Real Estate Summit 2026 to Convene India's Leading Regulatory and Industry Voices
content: NewsVoirNew Delhi [India], November 24: The National Association of Real Estate Professionals (NAREP) will host the NAREP Real Estate Summit 2026 on November 25 at The Park, New Delhi. Bringing together policymakers, regulatory authorities, developers and industry leaders, the summit will explore the opportunities and challenges shaping India's real estate sector.The summit's theme, "The Next Billion Square Feet," will guide discussions on regulatory reform, sustainable urbanisation, emerging residential formats, commercial real estate and evolving investment and development priorities.Among the distinguished participants will be Shri N. Saravana Kumar, Vice Chairman, Delhi Development Authority (DDA), and serving and former RERA chairpersons: Dr. Anand Kumar, IAS (Retd.), Former Secretary to the Government of India and Chairman, RERA, Delhi & Chandigarh; Mr. Parneet Sachdev, IRS, Chairman, RERA, Haryana; Mr. Ajoy Mehta, IAS (Retd.), Former Chairman, Maharashtra RERA; and Mr. Rakesh Kumar Goyal, Chairperson, RERA, Punjab. India's largest PR and communications firm for Real Estate sector, ICCPL Group, is managing the media strategy for NAREP's maiden event in Delhi.Mr. Lokesh Yadav, HCS, SDM, Manesar, will participate as Guest of Honour, bringing an administrative perspective to discussions on urban governance, infrastructure development and regional growth.The summit will feature four thematic panel discussions. The inaugural session, "Policy to Progress: Enabling Real Estate's Next Growth Story," will examine regulatory reforms, transparency, policy frameworks and responsible development. It will be moderated by Mr. Santhosh Kumar, Group Vice Chairman, ANAROCK."Women Who Build: Redefining Leadership and the Future of Real Estate" will focus on the growing role of women in the industry. Panelists will include Dr. Reena Sharma Kher, Founder, NAREP and Head - Training & Development, Central Park; Ms. Chitra Jain, Architect and Director, Samyak Properties and Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd.; and Ms. Surabhi Gupta, Executive Director & Regional Head - North, Corporate Leasing & Advisory, ANAROCK.Changing consumer preferences and new residential formats will be the focus of "Beyond Four Walls: Branded Residences, Hospitality and Senior Living." The panel will feature Mr. Rakesh Bohra, Pioneer Urban; Mr. Sahil Agarwal, Nimbus Group; Mr. Sudeep Bhatt, Whiteland Corporation; Mr. Kulmeet Singh Dhari, ACPL; and a representative from BPTP. The session will be moderated by Mr. Shalin Raina, Managing Director & Head - Residential Services, Cushman & Wakefield.The commercial real estate discussion, "Cubicles to Clouds: The New Commercial Real Estate Playbook," will feature Mr. Varun Sharma, DLF, and examine changing workplace needs, corporate real estate strategies and the future of commercial spaces in India.Mr. Rishabh Periwal, Promoter, Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Limited, will deliver a keynote address on the next phase of real estate development and emerging opportunities across the sector.Founded by Mr. Vishal Sikarwal and Dr. Reena Sharma Kher, NAREP aims to provide an inclusive platform for real estate professionals and encourage collaboration among regulators, developers and other industry stakeholders.Through initiatives such as the NAREP Real Estate Summit, the association seeks to promote knowledge exchange, professional development and constructive dialogue between policymakers and market participants. The 2026 summit is designed to support meaningful discussion, strengthen industry connections and contribute to a more transparent, progressive and sustainable real estate ecosystem.As India enters its next phase of urban and infrastructure development, "The Next Billion Square Feet" calls attention to more than the scale of construction. It also highlights the importance of quality, sustainability, transparency and long-term value in the built environment.The National Association of Real Estate Professionals (NAREP) is an industry platform founded by Mr. Vishal Sikarwal and Dr. Reena Sharma Kher. It brings together real estate professionals, developers, regulatory authorities and allied stakeholders, with a focus on professional excellence, knowledge sharing, industry collaboration and responsible growth across India's real estate sector.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by NewsVoir. headline: BJP-SAD to contest Punjab polls together, but ghost of farm laws persists
content: After going their separate ways in the 2022 Assembly and 2024 Lok Sabha polls in Punjab, where both parties lost badly, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced plans to contest the upcoming Punjab Assembly elections in an alliance once again. Assembly elections in Punjab are due early next year. It marked SAD’s return to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) after six years. SAD exited the NDA, severing its 24-year-long alliance with the BJP in Punjab, in September 2020 after three Central farm laws sparked widespread farmers’ agitation. The Centre scrapped the contentious laws in November 2021. As was evident at Tuesday’s press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, addressed by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP national president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal on the occasion of Gurpurab, the ghost of the farm laws continues to haunt the two parties. When asked about the three laws, Shah said it was a non-issue as they had been repealed. But the three leaders repeatedly stressed that the SAD-BJP alliance would address the problems faced by Punjab’s farmers. They said the alliance would soon unveil a “roadmap” focused on ending Punjab’s drug menace, curbing corruption, creating jobs for its youth and ensuring farmers’ welfare. Shah declared that Punjab would be completely drug-free by December 31, 2029. Later in the day, Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said the Centre would do its utmost to ensure prosperity for Punjab’s farmers. Sukhbir Singh Badal said the SAD-BJP alliance “is not merely a political alliance, but an emotional one”, and recalled the friendship between his father — five-time Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal — the late Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee and former Home Minister L K Advani. The SAD chief said Prime Minister Narendra Modi would attend the centenary celebrations of Parkash Singh Badal on his birth anniversary on December 8 in Moga. Shah said Sukhbir Singh Badal and Nabin had been talking for the last three months to give shape to the alliance and finalise its agenda for the people of Punjab. The SAD chief met the PM in August. Sukhbir said his father had described his party’s relationship with the BJP as “nau-maas da rishta” (the bond between the nail and the flesh). Shah did not disclose the number of seats the two parties would contest, but said SAD would take the role of the “elder brother” and also get the CM post if they were voted to power. Asked who would get the chief ministership if the alliance won, he replied, “The elder brother is the one who becomes the chief minister.” After the formal announcement of the alliance, Modi said in a social media post that the BJP and SAD have a natural alliance which would ensure Punjab gets pro-people governance that takes the state to new heights of progress. The alliance’s earlier formula was for the BJP to contest around 23 of the 117 seats, mostly in Hindu-dominated urban areas, and SAD to contest around 94. Shah, Nabin and Badal said the alliance remained a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood. Sources said the BJP could contest double the number of seats, around 46-47, given its better performance than SAD in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls. However, SAD’s vote share has eroded ever since the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) entered Punjab politics, making electoral contests in the state three-cornered fights. The SAD-BJP alliance ran governments in Punjab for 15 years: 1997-2002 and 2007-2017. After parting ways, they performed dismally. In the 2022 Assembly polls, the BJP won two seats and SAD three. In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, SAD won only one of the 13 seats — Bathinda, which was taken by Sukhbir Singh Badal’s wife, Harsimrat Kaur Badal, on a mere 13.48 per cent vote share. The BJP couldn’t win any, but doubled its vote share to 18.56 per cent from 9.63 per cent in 2019, since it contested all 13 seats. Since 2017, SAD has been reduced to the third or fourth party in Punjab. At the press conference, Sukhbir Singh Badal termed the situation in Punjab a “tidal wave” against the AAP government, which he said would be reduced to a single-digit tally in the Assembly polls, suggesting that the contest would be between the SAD-BJP alliance and the Congress. The SAD-BJP alliance increases the NDA’s Lok Sabha tally by one — Harsimrat Kaur Badal, a former Union minister. In April, she opposed population-based delimitation and favoured a flat 50 per cent increase in the number of seats each state currently sends to the Lok Sabha. AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh said the two parties had re-stitched the alliance owing to their “greed” for power. headline: Directionless alliance: Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for state polls
content: Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh on Tuesday slammed the BJP-SAD tie-up for the state Assembly polls, saying the two parties re-stitched the alliance owing to their “greed” for power.Both the parties, he claimed, lacked any development agenda or roadmap for taking the border state on the path of progress and prosperity.“It is a directionless alliance,” Singh told PTI while reacting to the SAD and BJP coming together for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls.“The reunion between the SAD and the BJP is only for the greed for power,” he alleged.“They have no development agenda for Punjab or roadmap for the state's progress. They have joined hands merely for their own development. They have joined hands again with a single motive to capture power in Punjab,” he said, while asserting that both the parties do not have any chance of forming the next government in Punjab.Singh asked SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal to explain to the people why he quit the NDA earlier.Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and the SAD chief made the alliance announcement ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls.The Sukhbir Singh Badal-led Shiromani Akali Dal had snapped its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the now-scrapped three farm laws.Earlier, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, who was also part of the Modi government as a minister with Cabinet rank, had also resigned.

headline: 'Bada bhai will be CM': Amit Shah after BJP-SAD announce alliance in Punjab
content: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday sounded the poll bugle in Punjab, announcing an alliance for the 2027 assembly elections and reviving their partnership after a six-year break. The two parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, with the Akali Dal taking the lead in the alliance."Big brother will be Akali Dal. We will contest all 117 seats. Bada bhai hi chief minister hota hai (The elder brother becomes the chief minister)," Union home minister Amit Shah said at a joint press conference attended by BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal.Also Read | 'Will make Punjab drug free by 2029': BJP-Akali Dal announce alliance on Gurpurab six years after split"Naturally, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) will play the role of the elder brother. The Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) will contest together. Both parties will jointly contest all 117 seats, while the Akali Dal will be in the role of the elder brother," he added.Shah said tackling drugs, corruption and law and order would be the alliance's key priorities in Punjab, a border state."The biggest hallmark of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) is that wherever there is an NDA government, law and order has remained sound. Both of our parties have discussed several issues concerning Punjab, and we have a consensus on them," he said.Also Read | 'Akali Dal-BJP alliance stood the test of time': PM Modi welcomes SAD's return to NDA"Our topmost priority will be a drug-free Punjab, fixing law and order to provide security in this border state, and eliminating these gangs. This is our topmost priority, and it will be the foremost issue in the manifestos of both parties," he added.Shah further stated that a detailed manifesto would be finalised soon by the two parties for the elections, but eradicating the drug menace from Punjab and promoting Hindu-Sikh unity would be among the key focus areas."BJP, the Akali Dal, and the NDA will contest in Punjab, and we will announce several key points in our manifesto. But, I want to make one thing very clear: eliminating drugs from Punjab will be our primary goal, eliminating corruption in Punjab will be our primary goal, and strengthening nationalist forces in Punjab will also be our primary goal. The current government in the state, led by Kejriwal Ji, had come to power promising to eliminate drugs within three months. They promised to eliminate drugs, but the problem has not been eradicated; it has increased. In 2017, Rahul Gandhi Ji had promised that drugs would be eliminated within one term. He made that promise, but his party also did nothing to address the drug problem. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free," he added.Sukhbir Singh Badal to be CM face: SirsaDelhi minister and BJP leader Manjinder Singh Sirsa said Sukhbir Singh Badal would be the chief ministerial face of the BJP-SAD alliance in Punjab.Speaking to ANI, Sirsa said the alliance was formed with a broader vision of addressing Punjab's problems rather than merely capturing political power. He said its priorities included making the state free of drugs, gangsters and debt, besides resolving farmers' issues.Also Read | ‘Zero plus zero equals zero’: AAP, Congress react to BJP-SAD alliance in PunjabHe also congratulated Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Shah, Nitin Nabin and Badal on the alliance, and welcomed the SAD's return to NDA.The announcement, made on Gurpurab, comes with a symbolic connection to the events that led to the breakdown of the alliance.The alliance marks a revival of ties between the BJP and SAD, which parted ways in 2020 after the Akali Dal withdrew from the NDA over its opposition to the now-repealed farm laws.Under their previous seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 assembly seats, while the SAD fought the remaining constituencies.The two parties had jointly governed Punjab for 10 years before losing the 2017 assembly elections. Congress returned to power under Captain Amarinder Singh.In 2022, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) swept the state, while the BJP and SAD, which contested separately, were pushed to the margins.Meanwhile, the Punjab BJP on Monday announced its 16-member state election committee for the 2027 assembly elections, with state president Kewal Singh Dhillon heading the panel.The committee comprises senior party leaders and former state presidents and has been tasked with preparing the party's electoral roadmap and framing a comprehensive chargesheet against the incumbent government.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Punjab Government Notifies Physicswallah Digital University in Patiala, PW Enters Formal Higher Education
content: Physicswallah Limited (PW) is expanding its presence in the education sector with the establishment of Physicswallah Digital University in Patiala, Punjab. The move marks the company's entry into formal higher education, extending its offerings beyond K-12 education and competitive examination preparation to undergraduate, postgraduate and career-oriented programmes through a digital learning model.The Punjab Government notified the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, on October 29, 2026, following the Governor's assent on October 23, 2026. Nextseed Foundation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Physicswallah Limited, will serve as the sponsoring body of the university. Headquartered in Patiala, Punjab, the university will operate on a self-financed model in accordance with the provisions of the Act.AI-Enabled Learning to Drive Digital EducationThe university will adopt an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approach to online and distance learning, integrating technology into teaching, assessments, student engagement and academic support. Its learning model will also include live sessions, faculty mentoring and global faculty connect programmes, bringing diverse academic perspectives and international expertise to students.The combined approach aims to equip learners with academic knowledge, practical skills and capabilities relevant to the global workforce. The university's digital infrastructure will also support mobile-first access and low-bandwidth connectivity, making higher education more accessible to students in smaller towns and remote locations.Five Academic Schools Planned for July 2027 LaunchWith its first academic session targeted for July 2027, Physicswallah Digital University plans to offer programmes through five academic schools: Business and Management; Computer and Information Technology; Humanities and Social Sciences; Journalism and Media Communication and Skills and Vocational Studies.Its proposed academic portfolio will include undergraduate and postgraduate degree programmes, along with certifications in areas such as Banking and Financial Services and Digital Marketing with AI and Social Media Marketing. These programmes will be offered subject to University Grants Commission (UGC) recognition and other applicable regulatory approvals.Alakh Pandey on PW's Entry into Higher EducationCommenting on the development, Alakh Pandey, Founder and Educator at Physicswallah, said, "Since its inception, PW has been focused on providing students across the country with accessible quality learning at affordable costs and equal opportunity for all students irrespective of geography or economic status. The Digital University will help us take this vision into formal higher education. We want students to access good teachers, the right guidance, and learning opportunities that prepare them for robust careers. We are grateful to the Punjab Government for its support and hope to make a meaningful difference in the lives of students."University Established Under Punjab's Private Digital Open Universities PolicyThe university has been established under the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, based on the Punjab Private Digital Open Universities Policy, 2026. Its regulatory framework provides for credit mobility through distance and online courses, as well as micro-credentials, subject to applicable regulations. It also provides for an independent ombudsman to address student grievances.The university will be required to comply with applicable UGC regulations, including those governing online education and Open and Distance Learning (ODL) programmes. These provisions are intended to establish an academic and administrative framework for delivering higher education through digital platforms.PW Aims to Expand Its Education EcosystemThrough this initiative, PW aims to expand its role in the education sector beyond K-12 offerings and competitive examination preparation. The digital university will create opportunities for learners to pursue formal higher education while developing skills aligned with their academic interests and professional aspirations.The development comes at a time when aligning higher education with changing industry requirements and career aspirations is receiving greater attention. NITI Aayog's report, Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047, citing the Economic Survey 2024–25, notes that 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications.This highlights the growing importance of education models that combine academic learning with practical skills and industry-oriented knowledge. Through its digital university, PW aims to contribute to this evolving education landscape by expanding access to degree-based learning and career-focused programmes.

headline: As BJP-Akali Dal join hands for polls, Amit Shah says ending Punjab’s drug menace will be key goal
content: New Delhi: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Tuesday expressed confidence that the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) would form the government in Punjab in the upcoming elections, following the BJP’s alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD). He said the alliance would work towards addressing farmers’ concerns, strengthening the state’s economy, creating employment opportunities for youth and eliminating the drug menace and corruption. Addressing the alliance announcement, Shah said that extensive discussions had taken place over the past three months between BJP leader Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal on issues concerning Punjab. “Over the past three months, extensive discussions have taken place between Nitin Nabin and Sukhbir Singh Badal regarding the challenges faced by Punjab’s farmers, concerns over the state’s economic development, and the employment issues confronting its youth,” Shah said. He added that the discussions had resulted in the preparation of a roadmap that would guide the proposed NDA government in the state. “These deliberations have culminated in a roadmap, which will serve as the guiding framework for the NDA government that we intend to form,” he said. Shah also identified the eradication of drugs and corruption as key priorities for the alliance, while emphasising the need to strengthen nationalist forces in Punjab. “I wish to state one thing very clearly: the eradication of the drug menace from Punjab will be our primary objective. Eliminating corruption from Punjab will be a key goal, and strengthening nationalist forces within the state will also be a top priority for us,” he said. Targeting the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab, Shah alleged that it had betrayed public trust and failed to fulfil its promises. “The current Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government has effectively betrayed the public trust; it has failed to fulfil any of its promises,” he said. He further said that the people of Punjab would no longer tolerate a government or individuals who had shown disrespect towards the Gurus. “The people of Punjab have firmly decided that they will no longer tolerate a government—or the individuals within it—that has shown disrespect toward the Gurus,” Shah said. Referring to the BJP’s alliance with the Akali Dal, Shah expressed confidence that the coming together of the two parties would strengthen the people’s resolve for change in the state. “With the BJP and the Akali Dal now joining forces, I am confident that this resolve among the people of Punjab will only grow stronger, paving the way for meaningful change,” he said. Shah also expressed confidence in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership, saying that the people of Punjab would give the NDA a resounding majority in the upcoming elections. “I am certain that, under the leadership of PM Modi, the people of Punjab will grant the NDA a resounding majority. We will undoubtedly form an NDA government in the upcoming elections and restore prosperity to Punjab once again,” he added.

headline: Arvind Kejriwal takes a jibe at BJP-SAD alliance, AAP’s tie-up is with people of Punjab | India News
content: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal on Tuesday took a swipe at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) over their renewed partnesrhip ahead of the 2027 Punjab assembly elections, saying his party's alliance was with the people of the state and not for power.“Our alliance is with the people of Punjab, not for power,” Kejriwal said, according to news agency ANI. He said the AAP's alliance was with Punjab's Scheduled Caste (SC) community, farmers and traders, accusing the BJP and SAD of repeatedly joining hands and parting ways for political gains.“These parties come together and part ways repeatedly for the sake of power,” he said. Kejriwal also defended the AAP government's performance in Punjab, saying it was working to develop the state and reverse decades of damage. He credited chief minister Bhagwant Mann with working hard over the past five years to undo the damage caused to Punjab over the last 70-75 years. His remarks came after the BJP and SAD announced the revival of their alliance, ending a six-year separation ahead of the Punjab assembly polls. The two parties parted ways in September 2020 after the SAD quit the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the Centre's three farm laws. ALSO READ | Six years after split, BJP, Akali Dal revive alliance for 2027 Punjab electionsAAP national media in-charge Anurag Dhanda accused the two parties of bringing back the drug menace that plagued the state during their previous tenure in power.“Those who pushed Punjab into the grip of the drug menace are back together,” Dhanda told PTI, adding that the alliance had reopened “old wounds” for the people of Punjab.Referring to the BJP-SAD government's 2007-2017 tenure, he alleged that “drugs had reached every village and household in Punjab”. He also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's promise to eradicate drugs in the state while joining hands with SAD leader Bikram Singh Majithia.“Today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi says he will eradicate drugs in Punjab in alliance with Bikram Singh Majithia,” Dhanda said.He alleged that Majithia's name had become synonymous with the drug 'chitta' in Punjab and accused him of using official vehicles to smuggle drugs while serving as a minister. Dhanda also alleged that Majithia had hosted international drug smugglers at his residence and referred to cases involving the alleged circulation of drug money worth ₹750 crore to ₹850 crore to acquire additional properties.“This is not an attempt to eliminate drugs but a sinister and shameful plan to bring back the era of drug abuse in Punjab,” he said.Claiming that the Bhagwant Mann-led AAP government had brought the drug trade under considerable control over the past four to four-and-a-half years, Dhanda alleged that the BJP and SAD had joined hands because they could not tolerate the government's action against the drug menace. “That is why they have hatched this conspiracy to ruin Punjab once again,” he said. The reunion brings back a political partnership that lasted nearly 24 years and saw the two parties govern Punjab together for 15 years, between 1997 and 2002 and again from 2007 to 2017.The alliance had collapsed after SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in protest against the farm laws. The SAD subsequently announced its exit from the NDA, citing the Centre's failure to address farmers' concerns.The renewed BJP-SAD partnership could change the political equation in Punjab, where the AAP will seek a second consecutive term in the 2027 assembly elections. The party had won a sweeping 92 of the state's 117 seats in the 2022 polls.The Congress had won 18 seats, while the SAD secured three and the BJP two.How AAP fared in recent electionsThe AAP swept the 2022 Punjab assembly elections, winning 92 of the state's 117 seats and forming the government under Bhagwant Mann. However, its performance weakened in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The party's vote share fell from 42.3% in the 2022 assembly polls to 26.2% in 2024. It also led in just 33 of Punjab's 117 assembly segments, HT reported earlier.ALSO READ | BJP-SAD alliance: The rise, split and reunion of Punjab's decades-old partnersThe party subsequently recovered in assembly bypolls, winning six of the seven seats contested between July 2024 and November 2025. It also won the Tarn Taran bypoll in November 2025, defeating the SAD by more than 12,000 votes.AAP registered a strong performance in the May civic elections, winning 958 of 1,977 wards and securing victories in five of the state's eight municipal corporations.BJP-SAD alliance: A historyThe BJP and SAD shared power in Punjab for 15 years, from 1997 to 2002 and again from 2007 to 2017. Their nearly 24-year formal alliance ended in September 2020 after SAD leader Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in protest against the farm laws.The SAD subsequently quit the NDA, citing the Centre's failure to address farmers' concerns. Although the Centre repealed the three laws in November 2021, the two parties remained separate.

headline: BJP-SAD alliance: The rise, split and reunion of Punjab's decades-old partners | India News
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have reunited, reviving a political partnership that lasted nearly 24 years before falling apart over the Centre's farm laws in 2020. The two parties announced the revival of their alliance on Tuesday, ending a six-year break and coming together for the 2027 Punjab assembly elections.Union home minister Amit Shah, BJP president Nitin Nabin and SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal made the announcement at a joint press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi. The announcement coincided with Guru Nanak Jayanti, marking the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.Thirty years after they first fought an assembly election together, the SAD and BJP will contest the Punjab polls together for the sixth time. They fought together in 1997, 2002, 2007, 2012 and 2017, winning three of those five elections and governing Punjab for 15 years.ALSO READ | Six years after split, BJP, Akali Dal revive alliance for 2027 Punjab electionsThe only assembly election they did not contest together during the past three decades was in 2022, when both parties fought separately and were reduced to the margins. Leaders from both sides have described the reunion as an effort to restore a partnership built around Punjab's peace and stability, rather than merely an alliance for power. The reunion could reshape the contest in Punjab, where the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Congress and BJP are preparing for the next assembly elections.A history of the BJP-SAD allianceThe BJP and the SAD's formal pre-poll alliance took shape ahead of the 1997 Punjab assembly elections. The partnership was forged in the mid-1990s, after decades of militancy and political instability in Punjab.At the SAD's Moga convention in February 1996, the party broadened its political identity from one centred on the Sikh community and the Panth to an inclusive regional force representing all Punjabis. The declaration was framed around the slogan 'Punjab, Punjabi and Punjabiyat'.The Moga Declaration projected Punjabiyat, rather than religion or caste, as the basis of the party's political identity. It also laid the foundation for the SAD's partnership with the BJP, which was aimed at challenging Congress in the state.ALSO READ | AAP to launch Punjab 2027 poll campaign with Moga rally on November 26Former chief minister Parkash Singh Badal, the key architect of the alliance, would often describe the relationship as 'Nau-Maas da Rishta', or a relationship akin to that between a mother and her child.The alliance delivered its first major electoral success a year later. In the 1997 Punjab assembly election, it won 93 seats, with the SAD securing 75 and the BJP 18. Congress was reduced to 14 seats, and Parkash Singh Badal became chief minister again.In the 1998 Lok Sabha election, the two parties won all 11 Punjab seats they contested, with the SAD winning eight and the BJP three. The SAD became one of the oldest members of the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).The alliance lost the 2002 state election to Congress but returned to power in 2007, winning 67 seats. It won again in 2012, marking the first time a government in Punjab was re-elected to office after the state's 1966 reorganisation.The alliance's fortunes declined in 2017, when Congress won 77 seats under Captain Amarinder Singh. AAP won 20 seats and became the main opposition party. The SAD fell to 15 seats and the BJP to three.ALSO READ | Punjab polls: AAP drops minister, 6 other MLAs in second list of 31 candidatesIn the 2019 Lok Sabha election, the two parties agreed to divide Punjab's 13 seats, with 10 allocated to the SAD and three to the BJP. Each party won two seats, while Congress won eight.There were strains in the alliance, though. In January 2020, the SAD briefly sat out the Delhi election after a dispute over the citizenship law, before backing the BJP days later.How the BJP-SAD alliance fared Why the alliance brokeThe relationship ended in September 2020 over the three farm laws introduced by the Narendra Modi government. The legislation triggered protests by farmers, particularly in Punjab and Haryana. Farmers' organisations argued that the laws threatened the existing agricultural marketing system and minimum support price (MSP) protections, HT reported earlier.The SAD, which had initially supported the legislation, came under growing pressure in Punjab to oppose it. On September 17, 2020, SAD leader and Union minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet in protest against the farm bills.Nine days later, on September 26, the SAD announced that it was quitting the NDA. Sukhbir Singh Badal said the decision was taken over the Centre's refusal to provide statutory guarantees for MSP and its alleged insensitivity towards farmers and Punjab's interests.The government withdrew the laws in November 2021, but the parties remained apart.BJP-SAD alliance: A look at the numbersThe alliance's strongest electoral performances came in 2007 and 2012, when it won consecutive assembly elections. The SAD secured 48 seats and the BJP 19 in 2007. In 2012, their tallies stood at 56 and 12, respectively.Their fortunes declined sharply in 2017 and worsened after the split. By the 2022 elections, the SAD was down to three seats and the BJP to two.The 2022 election saw AAP sweep Punjab, winning 92 of 117 seats. The SAD, which contested in alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), won three seats. The BJP, which fought alongside the Punjab Lok Congress and SAD (Sanyukt), won two.In the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the parties contested separately again. The BJP fought all 13 seats on its own, significantly increasing its vote share but failing to win any. The SAD also contested all 13 seats independently and won only Bathinda.Together, the BJP and SAD secured a combined vote share of 31.98% in 2024, higher than Congress's 26.30% and AAP's 26.02%. Yet, separately, they managed to win only one seat between them.That gap between their combined vote share and their individual electoral performance is among the key arguments for the reunion. Both parties hope that a renewed alliance will help convert votes into seats in the 2027 assembly election.The first test without Parkash Singh BadalThe 2027 assembly election will be the first joint contest without Parkash Singh Badal, who died in April 2023.All five previous joint assembly elections were fought under his influence, whether as SAD president, chief ministerial face or the key link between the Akali Dal and BJP leaders such as Atal Bihari Vajpayee and LK Advani.The next election will be led on the SAD side by Sukhbir Singh Badal. The BJP, meanwhile, is expected to have a greater say in the alliance's seat-sharing arrangement and power structure than it did in the past.A new seat-sharing formulaFor much of the alliance's history between 1997 and 2017, the SAD was the senior partner, contesting the larger share of seats, while the BJP remained the junior partner with a stronger presence in urban constituencies.The traditional arrangement was based on the SAD contesting 94 seats and the BJP 23 in Punjab's 117-member assembly. The SAD primarily contested rural constituencies, while the BJP focused on urban seats.That balance is now expected to change. Sources in both parties said the BJP is likely to contest 47-48 seats in the 2027 Punjab assembly election, nearly double its previous share. The broad division of constituencies is expected to remain the same, with the BJP focusing on urban seats and the SAD on rural areas.The proposed change reflects the BJP's increased vote share in Punjab and the altered political realities since the alliance broke up in 2020.Why GurpurabThe announcement of the alliance revival came on Guru Nanak Jayanti, the 557th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak Dev Ji.In Punjab, Gurpurab has often been a significant occasion for political outreach to the Sikh community by the Centre, particularly during periods of strained relations.The Kartarpur Corridor was inaugurated on November 9, 2019, on the eve of the 550th birth anniversary of Guru Nanak. The project fulfilled a long-pending demand for visa-free access to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib at Kartarpur in Pakistan.Two years later, on November 19, 2021, also on Gurpurab, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the three farm laws in a televised address and urged protesting farmers to return home.

headline: Shiromani Akali Dal back in NDA fold, to fight Punjab polls with BJP
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) have decided to join hands again ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, bringing an end to their six-year break after a disagreement over the Centre's farm laws. Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced the alliance on Tuesday at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, with SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal and BJP National President Nitin Nabin present. The two parties were long-time political partners in Punjab but ended their alliance in September 2020 after the SAD withdrew its support for the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over three farm laws introduced by the Centre. Drug menace, corruption among key priorities, says Amit Shah Addressing the joint press conference, Shah described the BJP and the SAD as long-standing allies and said their partnership had remained strong despite electoral victories and defeats. "Under the leadership of Sukhbir Badal, the Akali Dal has been our oldest ally. We have contested many elections together -- experiencing both victories and defeats -- yet our bond has remained unbreakable. Today, this partnership is being renewed, and it brings us great joy," Shah said. He said tackling drug abuse and corruption in Punjab would be among the key priorities of the alliance. Shah also said the BJP and SAD would jointly contest all 117 Assembly seats in Punjab, adding that the Akali Dal would have the role of the senior brother. SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal said, "This is not just a political alliance, this is an emotional bond. This is an alliance for the interest of Punjab, for the interest of the country and for the interest of the Sikh community." Why did the BJP and SAD part ways in 2020? The BJP and SAD had shared a political alliance for nearly 24 years before their relationship broke down over the farm laws passed by Parliament in September 2020. The laws -- the Farmers' Produce Trade and Commerce (Promotion and Facilitation) Act, the Farmers (Empowerment and Protection) Agreement on Price Assurance and Farm Services Act, and the Essential Commodities (Amendment) Act -- triggered widespread protests by farmers, particularly in Punjab and Haryana. The SAD, which had initially supported the legislation, faced growing opposition from farmers in its home state. Party leader and then Union Food Processing Industries Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal resigned from the Union Cabinet on September 17, 2020, in protest against the laws. A few days later, on September 26, the SAD announced its decision to quit the NDA, ending its long-standing alliance with the BJP. The party said the Centre had failed to address farmers' concerns and had not taken the interests of Punjab into account. The farmers' protests continued for more than a year, with the Centre eventually announcing the repeal of all three laws in November 2021. BJP-SAD alliance in Punjab: A brief history The BJP and the SAD remained political allies from November 1996 to September 2020. Under their seat-sharing arrangement, the BJP contested 23 of Punjab's 117 Assembly seats, while the SAD fielded candidates in the remaining 94. The alliance was formed ahead of the 1997 Assembly elections. The two parties governed Punjab together for 10 years, from 2007 to 2017, with SAD leader Parkash Singh Badal serving as chief minister. However, the alliance lost the 2017 Assembly elections to the Congress, which formed the government under Captain Amarinder Singh. Their relationship broke down in September 2020 when the SAD withdrew from the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) over the Centre's three farm laws. The legislation had faced strong opposition from farmers, particularly in Punjab. The Centre repealed the laws in November 2021, following more than a year of protests by farmers After ending their alliance, the BJP and SAD contested the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections separately. The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) won a decisive mandate, securing 92 of the state's 117 Assembly seats and forming the government under Bhagwant Mann. Both former allies suffered major setbacks. The SAD won just three seats, while the BJP secured two.
