headline: Punjab Assembly elections 2027: Six years after split, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance
content: The BJP and Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced their alliance for the upcoming Punjab Assembly polls. The announcement was made by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, BJP National President Nitin Nabin and SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi. “The senior leaders of both the Shiromani Akali Dal and the Bharatiya Janata Party made a decision that we would contest the next Punjab Assembly elections jointly," said Shah during the press briefing. He said that the alliance would make Punjab completely free from drugs by December 31, 2029 and added that they would unveil a manifesto for Punjab, addressing several key issues. .Talks over seat-sharing underway between Shiromani Akali Dal, BJP: Sources.Describing SAD as the NDA's oldest ally, Shah said, "I heartily welcome all colleagues of the Akali Dal and Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji into the NDA. Yesterday, when I spoke with the prime minister about the expansion of the NDA, he also called Sukhbir ji and our president and expressed the sentiment that the NDA is now complete, after the inclusion of Badal Sahab's party." "I believe that in Punjab, across the entire country, and in the world, this alliance will become a symbol of Hindu-Sikh brotherhood, and both parties will move forward together in this direction," he said. SAD President Sukhbir Singh Badal asserted that the alliance will win more than 100 seats in the Punjab Assembly polls. "As my late father used to say, the Akali Dal-BJP relationship is like a bond between two brothers born of the same mother. This alliance is for the welfare of Punjab, the welfare of the country, and the welfare of the Sikh community. I have spoken about the issues of farmers, Sikh community and others with PM Modi ji, Amit Shah ji, Nitin ji and they have assured to resolve all the issues together," he added Negotiations on seat-sharing between the BJP and the SAD for the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls are also underway. "I believe that this alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal is a natural alliance. We will discuss seat-sharing later," said Nabin. However, Shah clarified that the BJP-SAD alliance will fight on all 117 seats in Punjab Assembly polls and that SAD will get the chief minister post. The SAD had snapped its 24-year-old alliance with the BJP in September 2020 over the now-scrapped three farm laws. .BJP forms 16-member panel for 2027 Punjab Assembly elections.Earlier, Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal was also part of the Modi government as a minister with Cabinet rank. Last month in Delhi, Shah had predicted an NDA government in Punjab in 2027. When he came to Chandigarh on November 1, he again said an NDA government will be formed in the border state. The statement reignited the buzz about a possible SAD-BJP alliance. On November 2, when SAD president Badal was asked about the possibility of a re-alliance, he gave a guarded response to speculation, saying, "You will come to know in a few days as to what will happen". He reiterated that, except for the Congress and the AAP, he is open to an alliance with other parties which accept his party's philosophy. In the 2022 Assembly polls, the BJP won two seats, and the SAD could register victories in three Assembly segments out of a total of 117. Prior to the end of the electoral alliance, both the Akalis and the BJP used to contest together. As per the previous pact in the Assembly polls, the BJP used to contest 23 seats and the SAD 94 assembly seats. In parliamentary polls, the SAD used to fight for 10 seats and the BJP the remaining three.

headline: Six years after split, BJP, Akali Dal revive alliance for 2027 Punjab elections | India News
content: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) on Tuesday announced they would contest the 2027 Punjab assembly elections together, reviving their alliance after six years when the Akali Dal broke away from the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) in 2020.The two parties didn’t share details of a seat-sharing agreement but people aware of developments said the BJP may contest 40-45 seats. If this holds, it’ll be the largest share of seats contested by the BJP in alliance in the state. The two parties aim to dislodge the Aam Aadmi Party from power in a contest where the Congress is also hoping to win power.Union home minister Amit Shah, who along with SAD chief Sukhbir Singh Badal, announced the alliance at the BJP headquarters, also ended speculation about the chief ministerial candidate.“Akali Dal will remain in the role of elder brother. Akali Dal and BJP will fight together. Both the parties will contest together on all 117 seats. But Akali Dal will take the role of elder brother,” Shah said.“The elder brother is the one who becomes the chief minister,” he added.He said that after Prime Minister Narendra Modi was apprised about the “NDA’s expansion”, he called Badal with great joy. The PM also called Nabin and expressed his sentiments, saying the NDA was “now complete with Badal saheb’s party,” the home minister added. After the formal announcement, Modi said he was confident that the coalition will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab.“Putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first! I am extremely delighted that the Shiromani Akali Dal returns to the NDA family and that too on the Parkash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji,” Modi said on X.“Nurtured by Atal Ji, Advani Ji and Sardar Parkash Singh Badal Ji, the Akali Dal-BJP Alliance has stood the test of time. I am confident that our alliance will emerge as the preferred choice of the people of Punjab,” he added. The SAD is one of the BJP’s oldest allies. The two parties joined hands in 1996 when the party patriarch Parkash Singh Badal announced support for the BJP after the 1996 general elections, and a formal alliance was announced ahead of the 1997 Punjab assembly polls.The two parties, which contested the 2022 assembly elections separately, ended with the SAD winning just three seats and the BJP two, in the 117-member assembly. The alliance fell apart in September 2020 after the SAD withdrew from the NDA. Lok Sabha MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal also resigned from the Union cabinet in opposition to the Centre’s three farm laws, which were subsequently repealed.The AAP, Congress and farm unions criticised the alliance.Shah, credited with working out the contours of the reunion, referred to the alliance as a favourable partnership and said it would be a “symbol of Hindu-Sikh bhaichara” (amity). He also asserted that unlike the Congress and the AAP, the NDA will crack down on drugs and corruption in the state.“Our priority will be eradicating drugs, ending corruption and improving security in this border state… Kejriwal had promised drug abuse would be eradicated in three months, nothing happened. Rahul Gandhi also made a similar promise but did not do anything. We have a roadmap for jobs and employment of the youth. The AAP government has not fulfilled any promise. Now, I want to reiterate a promise that I made there: by December 31, 2029, we will make Punjab completely drug-free,” he said.Shah said a detailed manifesto – which will pave the way for the development of every section including farmers, businessmen and young people – will be finalised soon. Responding to a question about apprehensions regarding Hindu-Sikh amity in the state, Shah said there was no problem and a strong NDA will ensure no scope for “any party to create a rift”.BJP chief Nitin Nabin said the two parties were “natural allies” and reiterated Shah’s statement that the alliance will “promote Hindu Sikh Ekta (unity)...”Badal – whose meeting with Modi during the monsoon session of Parliament had sparked speculation about the merger – said the “relationship that was forged” by his father Parkash Singh Badal and Vajpayee and Advani was revived.“First the Congress and then the AAP destroyed the state. Gangsters are ruling, I have never seen such chaos anywhere else. We need to save the farmers, the businesses and all this can be done by a double engine government,” he said.According to party leaders, the reunion was preceded by discussions within the BJP about the merit of joining hands with the SAD.“We conducted extensive surveys to assess the mood on the ground… Initially our cadre was not in favour of SAD being back in the NDA, there were some voices against the BJP assuming the role of the junior partner, but eventually it was decided that for the benefit of the state and its people, the BJP will let the SAD play big brother,” said a senior party leader.The leader said issues of national security prevailed to a large extent in deciding the contours of the alliance. “The home minister was emphatic that we cannot allow politics to overshadow national concerns. Punjab is a border state, grappling with corruption, drug mafia, lawlessness and joblessness. In the best interest of the people it was necessary that the state get a stable government and parties that put the nation first come together,” the leader said.Asked whether the BJP found it difficult to gain a foothold in the state after the prolonged protest over the farm laws, the leader said, “In the 2024 Lok Sabha polls the BJP’s vote percentage grew from 9.63% (in 2019) to 18.5%. It is true we did not convert the votes into seats, but it will be wrong to assume that there is no acceptance [for the BJP].”In 2019, the BJP won two of the 13 Lok Sabha seats but zero in 2024. The SAD won two in 2019 and one in 2024.The two parties had also explored the possibility of joining hands before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, but talks fell through due to disagreements over the proposed alliance terms. Discussions about a reunion gathered pace again in recent months, particularly after Shah repeatedly said the NDA would form the next government in Punjab. The partnership, which saw the two parties govern Punjab for 15 years across three five-year terms, came apart in September 2020 when the Akalis walked out of the NDA.The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and Congress leaders hit out at the move, calling it an “opportunistic” bid for power.“This alliance...is not for Punjab, but a ‘thug pact’ to save their own families and seats,” CM Bhagwant Mann said.AAP national convener Arvind Kejriwal said, “They come together for the sake of power, then they part ways, and then they come together again.”Punjab Congress President Pargat Singh said the “biggest lie” told on Gurpurab concerned the alliance. Congress’s Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot called it a prime example of “opportunism.”“It existed all along, but has only been announced today,” he said, adding that the BJP and SAD had now “joined AAP in the same category of politics of deception.”He also called it a “compromise alliance, an alliance born of necessity, because neither party has explained why they split six years ago.”

headline: Physicswallah enters higher education with Digital University in Patiala, classes to begin in July 2027
content: Physicswallah (PW) has established Physicswallah Digital University in Patiala, Punjab, marking its entry into formal higher education beyond K-12 and competitive exam preparation. The proposed university will offer undergraduate, postgraduate and career-oriented programmes through an online model, with its first academic session targeted to commence in July 2027. The Punjab government notified the Physicswallah Digital University, Patiala Act, 2026, on October 29, following the Governor's assent on October 23. Nextseed Foundation, a wholly owned subsidiary of Physicswallah Limited, is the sponsoring body of the university. Headquartered in Patiala, the university will operate on a self-financed model in accordance with the provisions of the Act. AI-Driven Learning The university will adopt an artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled approach to online and distance learning, integrating technology across teaching, assessments, student engagement and academic support. This will be complemented by live sessions, faculty mentoring and global faculty connect initiatives, bringing diverse academic perspectives and international expertise to students. These initiatives aim to equip learners with academic knowledge, practical skills and capabilities required by the global workforce. Its digital infrastructure will also enable mobile-first access and low-bandwidth connectivity, with the aim of making higher education more accessible to learners in smaller towns and remote locations. Academic Offerings The university plans to offer programmes across five academic schools: Business and Management; Computer and Information Technology; Humanities and Social Sciences; Journalism and Media Communication; and Skills and Vocational Studies. Its proposed portfolio will include undergraduate and postgraduate degrees, along with certifications in areas such as Banking and Financial Services, Digital Marketing with AI, and Social Media Marketing. These programmes will be subject to University Grants Commission (UGC) recognition and other applicable regulatory approvals. Alakh Pandey, founder and educator, Physicswallah, said, “Since its inception, PW has been focused on providing students across the country with accessible quality learning at affordable costs and equal opportunity for all students irrespective of geography or economic status. The Digital University will help us take this vision into formal higher education. We want students to access good teachers, the right guidance, and learning opportunities that prepare them for robust careers. ”

headline: Punjab Assembly polls: BJP-SAD to hold joint presser today

The alliance’s goal was to make Punjab drug-free by December 31, 2029, and make sure that law and order, development, and issues pertaining to farmers were addressed, the Home Minister also said. Directionless alliance: Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for State polls Directionless alliance: Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for State polls Both the parties, the Punjab Congress chief claimed, lacked any development agenda or roadmap for taking the border state on the path of progress and prosperity Directionless alliance: Punjab Congress chief slams BJP-SAD pact for State polls storyline 1 Mr. Badal hailed the long history and personal equations between senior leaders of the BJP, the late former PM Atal Behari Vajpayee and L.K. headline: Punjab Congress chief urges PM to reopen Kartarpur Corridor, resume Attari-Wagah trade
content: Punjab Congress chief Pargat Singh has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging him to reopen the Kartarpur Corridor and resume trade through the Attari-Wagah border.In a letter to the Prime Minister on Monday, Singh said the Kartarpur Corridor represents the deepest spiritual sentiments of the Sikh community.“Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur, is closely associated with the life and teachings of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji. For millions of devotees, the opportunity to visit this sacred place is not merely a journey across a border; it is a matter of faith, heritage and spiritual connection,” he wrote.“The suspension of the corridor has caused deep disappointment among devotees who have been unable to pay obeisance at this historic shrine,” said Singh.The Jalandhar Cantt MLA urged the Centre to initiate appropriate diplomatic engagement with Pakistan and explore a safe, secure and mutually acceptable mechanism to reopen the corridor at the earliest.The Kartarpur Corridor connects Gurdwara Darbar Sahib in Pakistan, where Sikhism founder Guru Nanak Dev spent the last years of his life, with the Dera Baba Nanak shrine in Punjab's Gurdaspur district.The corridor has remained shut since May 7 last year, when the Indian armed forces carried out pre-dawn missile strikes on nine terror targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir.On resuming trade through the Attari-Wagah border, the Punjab Congress chief said the route had historically been important trade for Punjab and the wider region.“Cross-border trade supported traders, transporters, farmers, labourers and several other sections of the local economy. Its closure has affected economic activity, employment opportunities and the livelihoods of people, particularly in border districts,” he said.Punjab has a strong stake in regional trade and connectivity, he said, urging the Centre to examine the possibility of resuming trade through the Attari-Wagah Integrated Check Post, subject to appropriate security arrangements, safeguards and regulatory mechanisms.Singh said Punjab has always borne a significant human, social and economic burden because of tensions along the international border.“Our people deeply value national security, but the interests, religious sentiments and economic well-being of Punjab must also receive due consideration,” he said.Both issues deserve a constructive approach that balances national security with religious freedom, regional economic development and the aspirations of the people, he said.“I respectfully request your personal intervention and urge the government of India to initiate the necessary steps for the early reopening of the Sri Kartarpur Sahib Corridor and the resumption of trade through the Attari-Wagah border,” he said.

headline: High Court raps officials for poor case handling
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rapped Punjab Government officials for a lackadaisical approach and failure to properly defend land acquisition compensation cases. The Bench observed that inadequate evidence, failure to verify sale deeds and selective filing of appeals were creating financial liabilities for the state.Taking note of the pattern during the preceding four months, Justice Jagmohan Bansal directed the high court registry to send the order’s copy to the state chief secretary and the principal/additional chief secretary (law and justice) for bringing the concerns to the attention of the state’s senior-most administrative and legal authorities.Justice Bansal observed: “During the last four months, I have noticed that in most of the cases, the state does not lead requisite evidence before the reference court and as per evidence led by landowners, state’s huge fiscal liability is created.”The Bench was hearing a batch of 55 petitions filed by landlords against different awards passed by reference court/additional district judge, Ropar. They were seeking enhancement of compensation following acquisition of land in nine villages for the construction of the Ropar bypass, while the state was claiming otherwise.A reference court in land acquisition cases is the judicial forum that adjudicates objections raised by an interested person who does not accept the compensation or terms awarded by the land acquisition collector/officer.Flagging the failure to scrutinise transactions relied upon for determining compensation, Justice Bansal observed: “No effort is made to find out genuineness of sale deeds comprising small pieces of land and that too executed just few months before the initiation of acquisition process.”Justice Bansal also questioned the state’s approach to challenging compensation awards. Referring to the matters placed before the Bench, Justice Bansal observed: “Appeals have been filed in a few cases and no appeal has been filed where a higher amount was awarded.”Justice Bansal noted that even specific judicial directions had not ensured production of essential documentary evidence. “Despite specific orders of this court, the state does not produce a site plan disclosing the location of the acquired land as well as exemplar sale deeds,” the court observed.“A very casual and lackadaisical approach is adopted by all officials dealing with the matters,”Justice Bansal said.

headline: Punjab govt’s HUNAR portal helping youth land industrial job offers, says Arora | Hindustan Times
content: The Punjab government’s Hunar portal is providing direct hiring opportunities for students with leading industries in the state, with over 200 recruitment applications already sent to ITIs, polytechnics, colleges and universities.According to Punjab industries and commerce minister Aman Arora, over 1,100 industries have used the platform to connect with educational institutions, a validation of the Bhagwant Mann-led government’s initiative to connect the state youth with industry giants and jobs.Major firms such as Tata Steel, Kansai Nerolac, LT Foods, and Happy Forgings are actively hiring across the steel and engineering, food processing, paints and chemicals, construction, and hospitality sectors.Sharing the portal’s early success, Arora said campus drives were also underway and students were already receiving job offers.He said HUNAR (Hub for Upskilling, Networking and Access to Rozgar), launched by chief minister Bhagwant Mann on October 8, was a unified digital platform to connect Punjab’s youth with employment opportunities and help industry access skilled, industry-ready talent.Arora said HUNAR was integrated with “Fast-track Punjab”, the state’s investment facilitation platform and in future, the platform will also offer internships, industrial training and structured partnerships between industry and institutions — including support in curriculum development, faculty development, guest lectures and technology.

headline: If voted to power, SAD will free Punjab from scourge of gangsters, says Sukhbir | Hindustan Times
content: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal on Monday said if his party forms the next government in Punjab, it would free the state from the scourge of gangsters once and for all.Interacting with traders and industrialists in Zira, Sukhbir made the announcement after business representatives highlighted the growing menace of ransom threats and extortion, claiming that it had become difficult to operate in Punjab.He assured the trade and industry that gangsters would be dealt with firmly if his party comes to power. “This is essential to provide a congenial atmosphere to the industry and attract new investment into the state. The only gangsters who will remain will either be in jail or hospitals,” he said.He also took on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) after it recently inducted gangster-turned-politician Gurpreet Singh Sekhon from Zira. Sekhon had joined the AAP along with his supporters at a rally in Zira in Ferozepur in September.To offer relief to small traders, he stated that if his party forms the next government, they will bring back a previous relief scheme. Under this programme, shopkeepers would pay a flat ₹1,000 per year, removing the requirement to maintain detailed account books or undergo inspections by government officials.He added that big businesses would also be allowed to file self-declarations on taxes, emphasising that citizens must be trusted rather than subjected to unnecessary official interference.Balwant Singh of the Zira Arhtiya Association raised concerns over the poor condition of mandis and demanded an increase in commission to 2.5%. Responding to that, Sukhbir promised repairs and reconstruction of market huts and an increase in commission.Darbara Singh Malhi of the Kiln Owners Association highlighted alleged harassment by the mining, labour and provident fund departments.In response, Sukhbir assured the kiln owners that their grievances would be resolved and that they would be exempted from the Mining Act.

headline: Anti-sacrilege law: Akal Takht panel skips second meet, Punjab govt renews talks appeal | Hindustan Times
content: The Punjab government-appointed coordination committee has renewed its appeal to the expert committee constituted by the Akal Takht to hold discussions on the objections raised to the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026, and work towards resolving them through mutual consultation.The panel has proposed November 27 for a fresh round of talks, after two earlier attempts to hold a joint meeting, including one on Monday, failed to materialise.The Akal Takht panel skipped the meeting called by the Punjab government’s committee at the Circuit House in Amritsar, sticking to its stand that it will not participate in any deliberations over the legislation unless the government first puts a stay on it.The Takht panel has sent three letters to the government panel so far, pushing for a stay on the Act in compliance with the Takht’s decree.Releasing a statement on Monday, the government-appointed coordination committee said it had sought a meeting with the Akal Takht-appointed expert panel in Amritsar on November 18.A fresh request was made on Monday for a joint meeting to discuss the contentious provisions and find an acceptable solution. However, no representative of the expert committee attended either meeting, it said.Describing the matter as highly sensitive and closely linked to Sikh religious sentiments, the coordination committee stressed that the concerns needed to be addressed through dialogue, mutual understanding and consensus rather than confrontation.It urged the expert committee to come forward for discussions and share its recommendations so that both panels could deliberate on the objections raised by the Akal Takht and finalise the necessary amendments to the legislation through mutual agreement.“The objective is not to create any confrontation but to arrive at an amicable and unanimous resolution, keeping the sanctity of Guru Granth Sahib and the sentiments of the Sikh sangat paramount,” the committee said.As part of its renewed efforts, the coordination committee has proposed November 27 for a meeting with the Takht panel, also inviting the members to suggest a convenient date, time and venue at the earliest.The coordination committee said it was willing to travel to any venue chosen by the expert panel and participate in meaningful deliberations to resolve the issue.

headline: ED summons 20 Punjab bureaucrats in three separate investigations, AAP cries foul | Hindustan Times
content: The recent Enforcement Directorate (ED) action, which has seen 20 Punjab bureaucrats, including 10 IAS, eight PCS and an IPS and a PPS officer each, summoned and questioned in three separate investigations over the past two months, has brought the state’s bureaucracy under unprecedented federal scrutiny.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has snapped back, accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre of misusing central agencies to target the Punjab government, alleging that the summons are politically motivated and aimed at disrupting its functioning.The high-profile list includes chief secretary KAP Sinha and two principal secretaries. Of the 10 IAS officers, two are retired.The investigations span alleged irregularities in land dealings involving the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), real estate transactions linked to Ritesh Properties and Industries Ltd (RPIL), later renamed Hampton Sky Realty Limited, and the bribery and disproportionate assets case against suspended DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar.Also read: Punjab: IAS, IPS officers among seven summoned by ED in PMLA probe linked to Bhullar graft caseGMADA land deal probeNearly two months after conducting searches at the Punjab Urban Planning and Development Authority (PUDA) headquarters, the ED has intensified its probe into alleged irregularities in GMADA land dealings, summoning several serving and former officials of the housing and urban development department.Those summoned include GMADA chief administrator Sandeep Rishi (IAS); principal secretary, housing and urban development, Vikas Garg (IAS); and former chief administrator Sakshi Sawhney (IAS).Among the PCS officers are land acquisition officer Rohit Jindal, estate officer Aman Gupta, former additional chief administrator Rakesh Kumar Popli, additional chief administrator Amarinder Singh Mali, and former land acquisition officer Hardeep Singh.The agency has also summoned chief secretary KAP Sinha and principal secretary, finance, Alok Shekhar, to appear on November 26 in the money-laundering investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).Also read: ED summons two Punjab AAP MLAs in land fraud, money-laundering probeED examines alleged manipulation of land prices and auction conditionsOn September 22, the ED conducted searches at 26 premises across Delhi, Mohali, Chandigarh, Panchkula and Ludhiana, including the GMADA headquarters at PUDA Bhawan and offices of the housing and urban development department. The probe concerns alleged bank fraud and subsequent money laundering involving real estate developer Tirupati Infraprojects and its associated entities.The agency is examining whether changes in land-use policies, reserve prices, auction conditions and master plans benefited select private entities. It alleged that manipulation of reserve prices of unsold GMADA land could have caused a potential loss of nearly ₹10,000 crore to the authority and the Punjab government.Earlier, former chief secretary Anurag Verma, who headed the housing and urban development department in 2024, was questioned in September in a separate probe involving Mohali-based Suntec City and Altus Space Builders Private Limited over a Change of Land Use (CLU) issue. Director, town and country planning, Kanwal Preet Brar was also questioned in the same case.The investigations have also affected routine administrative work. A senior department officer said officials were spending considerable time compiling records and preparing replies to the agency.AAP MP and party spokesperson Malwinder Singh Kang accused the BJP-led Centre of misusing central agencies to target the state government, alleging the summons were aimed at derailing its functioning.Also read: GMADA land deals probe: ED summons Punjab chief secy, finance secy on Nov 26Real estate transactions under scannerIn the second case, the ED questioned Vikas Hira (PCS), chief administrator of the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA), in August and September in connection with a real estate and money-laundering probe.The agency is examining land and property transactions, including records related to RPIL, subsequently renamed Hampton Sky Realty Limited and linked to AAP minister Sanjeev Arora.Bhullar graft caseIn the third case, the ED has summoned serving and retired officials in a money-laundering investigation stemming from the corruption case against suspended DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar and his alleged associates.Those summoned include health and family welfare administrative secretary Kumar Rahul (IAS), special secretary, general administration, Neeru Katyal Gupta (IAS), and Anand Sagar Sharma (PCS), staff officer to the commissioner, Faridkot division.Also read: Punjab: Bhullar’s aide acted as middleman for several officials, says EDLudhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma (IPS) and Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh (PPS) have also been summoned.Two retired IAS officers, former Jalandhar commissioner Gurpreet Kaur Sapra and former divisional commissioner Arun Sekhri, are also among those called. They have been asked to appear on November 26 and 25, respectively.The PMLA probe stems from two CBI FIRs against Bhullar and his associates on charges of bribery and alleged possession of disproportionate assets. Bhullar, then DIG, Ropar Range, was arrested by the CBI in October 2025.

headline: Sports Can Be Punjab’s Strongest Weapon Against Drugs, Muktsar Police Show the Way
content: In a refreshing approach to tackling Punjab's drug problem, the Muktsar police have demonstrated how sports and community participation can become powerful instruments of social change. On Saturday, police personnel joined local youngsters for a volleyball match in Ward 29 on Kotkapura Road, transforming a previously identified drug hotspot into a space for physical activity and positive engagement. As part of the initiative, the police cleaned the area and installed a volleyball net, encouraging young residents to spend their time playing sports rather than becoming vulnerable to substance abuse. Several police personnel, including women officers, participated in the match, sending a message that the fight against drugs requires cooperation between law enforcement agencies and local communities. The initiative coincided with a wider crackdown under the Punjab government's Yudh Nashian Virudh campaign. More than 400 police personnel participated in cordon-and-search operations across the district, targeting suspected drug trafficking and criminal activities. However, the volleyball initiative represents an equally important dimension of the anti-drug campaign: prevention through meaningful engagement.

headline: 3rd Punjab Hockey League: Government Academy beat Surjit Hockey 6-5 in penalty shootout
content: Government Hockey Academy, Sonepat, edged past Surjit Hockey Academy 6-5 in a penalty shootout to earn a bonus point during the 3rd Punjab Hockey League at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium.The match ended in a 1-1 draw after regulation time. Both teams maintained a compact defensive structure during a goalless first half. However, Surjit Academy broke the deadlock three minutes into the third quarter when Rohit converted a field goal in the 33rd minute.Sonepat responded in the final quarter, with Gurdyal Singh scoring a field goal in the 48th minute to restore parity and force a shootout. With the teams tied at 3-3 after the first five rounds, the contest went into sudden death. Ashish converted the decisive eighth-round attempt, while goalkeeper Love Kumar denied Jasanpreet Singh to secure the bonus point for Sonepat.Meanwhile, Roundglass Hockey Academy secured its third consecutive victory with a comfortable 3-1 win over Namdhari XI to move to the top of the points table. The academy team recorded a goalless two quarters, but scored two goals after halftime. Jarman Singh struck twice in quick succession with field goals in the 31st and 35th minutes to give his side a 2-0 advantage. Namdhari XI pulled one back early in the final quarter when Gurman Singh converted a penalty corner in the 48th minute.However, the hosts restored their two-goal cushion in the 55th minute through a field goal by Anurag to seal all three points and move to the top of the standings.Ghumanhera Risers Academy, Delhi, registered a commanding 4-0 victory over Republican Sports Club, Mumbai. The deadlock was broken in the 20th minute when Pankaj Phalswal converted a penalty corner to give his side a 1-0 lead at half-time.The Delhi team took complete control in the third quarter with a clinical scoring burst. Phalswal struck twice more through penalty corners in the 44th and 45th minutes to complete his hat-trick, before Sukhdev Singh added a fourth goal with a field goal in the 45th minute.Republican Sports Club tried to fight back in the final quarter, but Ghumanhera Risers Academy maintained its defensive discipline to preserve its clean sheet and register its third win of the league.

headline: In a first, EC wants officials who served in 2022 Punjab Assembly poll shifted out of district
content: In a first, the Election Commission of India has ordered that officers involved in the last Assembly polls will be shifted out and kept away from the exercise in the same constituency or district during the 2027 elections.“In a major policy revision to ensure a level playing field for all parties, while implementing the said instructions / transferring officers, the departments concerned should take care that they are not posted to their home districts,” the recent EC order stated.“It shall also be ensured that no DEO/RO/ARO or police inspector/sub-inspector or above is posted back or allowed to continue in the constituency or district where he/she was posted during the last Assembly election/any bypoll held thereafter,” it added.Notably, the EC routinely orders the transfer of officials involved in election-related duties to ensure free and fair polls. Senior Punjab government officers, however, noted that until the last Assembly elections, the EC would only shift officers from the districts or constituencies that they were in for the last Lok Sabha elections or a bypoll.The rule change has left hundreds of officers in the civil and police administration across Punjab running from pillar to post to at least secure a posting in a nearby district. Queued up outside their seniors’ offices, many of them rued that they would now have to spend at least six more months away from home.“The new rules have left a majority of officers hopeful of returning home dejected,” said an IPS officer. “There are hundreds of such officials from the rank of sub-inspector and above who will be shifted and are now trying to manage non-election related postings,” the officer added.“After the 2022 Assembly polls, I served two years in Patiala and then took an out-of-city posting with a hope that I can come back ahead of 2027. However, the EC has now directed officers who were in a particular district even during the last Assembly polls to be shifted out,” a police inspector lamented.Last month, the EC had directed Goa, Manipur, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand authorities to transfer officers from certain categories directly involved in election-related work. The new directive comes after the poll body recently ordered a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states, including the five headed for polls next year.Those set to be affected by the new rules are district election officers, returning officers, additional district magistrates, sub-divisional magistrates, tehsildars and block development officers, divisional and municipal commissioners. Police officers from sub-inspector up to range additional directors general, inspectors general and excise and transport department officers of sub-inspector rank and above are also covered.Officers posted at state headquarters are exempted, as are non-election staff such as are doctors, engineers and teachers.

headline: Akal Takht panel skips meeting on anti-sacrilege law again
content: The standoff between the Punjab Government and the Akal Takht over the Jaagat Jot Sri Guru Granth Sahib Satkar (Amendment) Act, 2026, continued on Monday, with the government’s coordination committee making a fourth appeal to the expert panel appointed by the Akal Takht to join discussions on the legislation.The government committee reached the Circuit House in Amritsar on Monday for a meeting with the expert panel, but no representative of the latter turned up. Committee members said they had invited the panel for discussions on three earlier occasions, but it had not participated so far.The committee has now invited the expert panel for another meeting on November 27 at 12 noon. Its members said they were willing to hold discussions at any place and time convenient to the panel.They said efforts to initiate dialogue began after an interim meeting on November 13. Subsequent invitations were sent for meetings on November 18 and November 23 through email and personally by the government’s nodal officer. However, the panel did not attend any of these meetings.Those present at the Circuit House included Bhupinder Singh, representative of Baba Sewa Singh of Gurdwara Rampur Khera; Giani Sahib Singh, representative of Damdami Taksal; AG Preet Inderpal Singh from the Advocate General’s office; and retired Justice Jaspal Singh.Former Akal Takht Jathedar Giani Raghbir Singh, retired Justice Gurbir Singh and Jatinder Singh Aulakh joined the meeting through video conferencing.Meanwhile, Lakhbir Singh, SGPC secretary and coordinator of the Akal Takht-appointed expert panel, said the committee had already conveyed its position to the government in writing.He said the government should put the implementation of the Satkar Act on hold in compliance with the Akal Takht’s directives before holding any discussions. The expert panel would participate in the dialogue only after the directives were implemented, including putting the Act in abeyance.

headline: Haryana CM Saini reviews development works in Gurugram
content: Gurugram, Nov 24 (PTI) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini on Tuesday reviewed development works, including sanitation, waste management, drinking water supply and sewerage networks at a meeting with officials of the Gurugram Metropolitan Development Authority and the municipal corporation. According to an official statement, Saini directed officers to ensure visible improvements in civic infrastructure and services across Gurugram. Stating that there is no shortage of funds for development works, Saini asked the officials to implement government schemes and development projects on the ground with utmost integrity, responsibility and commitment. He emphasised that he wanted to see tangible results rather than merely progress reports. The chief minister asked them to adopt a micro-management approach to improve sanitation and ensure proper and “scientific” disposal of construction and demolition (C&D) waste in the city. He directed the officials to fix accountability and ensure that waste disposal is carried out in accordance with the prescribed standards.

headline: Kirodi Meena rules out leadership change in Rajasthan, day after invoking Haryana example
content: Jaipur, Nov 24 (PTI) Rajasthan Agriculture Minister Kirodi Lal Meena on Tuesday dismissed speculation about a possible leadership change in Rajasthan following the BJP’s poor performance in the recent panchayat elections, contradicting his remark a day ago, when he cited a similar change in Haryana as an example of the party’s electoral comeback there. On Monday, reacting to the BJP’s electoral setback, Meena said the party had not anticipated such a poor performance and would undertake a detailed review to identify the reasons. Responding to the Congress’ description of the election results as a litmus test for the BJP government, he said the opposition was under a misconception. He then cited Haryana, where Nayab Singh Saini replaced Manohar Lal Khattar as chief minister before the BJP returned to power with a strong majority. Meena said the party would accept the defeat and correct its mistakes to regain public confidence. He acknowledged that a failure to fully activate the administrative machinery at the grassroots had contributed to discontent in rural areas. However, on Tuesday, he rejected speculation about a change in the BJP’s state leadership. He said the central leadership was adept at formulating strategies and would ensure the party’s success in Rajasthan. He cited the BJP’s electoral performances in West Bengal, Bihar and Haryana as examples of its ability to make a strong comeback.

headline: Data Centres, REITs and Real Estate IPOs to Take Centre Stage at NAREDCO NextGen Leadership Conclave
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 24: NAREDCO NextGen, the youth wing of the National Real Estate Development Council (NAREDCO), is set to organise the NAREDCO NextGen Leadership Conclave 2026 on 2 December 2026 in Gurugram, Haryana, with the support of the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India. Presented by Adani Cement, the Conclave will bring together young leaders from the real estate sector, developers, next-generation representatives of family-owned businesses, investors, policymakers and industry experts on a common platform to deliberate on emerging opportunities and significant developments shaping India's real estate sector.The Conclave will feature discussions around key themes: Data Centres, REITs & REIT IPOs, and Family Offices - Fundamentals & Structure. The sessions will explore the growing role of institutional capital in real estate, opportunities in India's expanding data centre ecosystem, professionalisation of family-run enterprises, succession planning and the importance of structured wealth management.Dr. Niranjan Hiranandani, Chairman, NAREDCO, said, "India's real estate sector is continuously evolving with the emergence of new investment avenues and asset classes. Institutional capital, REITs and digital infrastructure are creating new opportunities for the sector's expansion and diversification. At the same time, professional governance and leadership development will be essential for building strong and sustainable real estate businesses."As India's real estate sector continues to mature, the focus is expanding beyond traditional residential and commercial development towards a more diverse range of business and investment opportunities. Growing participation from institutional investors, emerging asset classes such as data centres and evolving capital market instruments are opening new avenues for developers and investors. Meanwhile, the importance of professional management and succession planning in family-owned real estate businesses is also gaining prominence.Mr. Parveen Jain, President, NAREDCO, said, "For the real estate sector to move into its next phase of growth, businesses must prepare themselves to adapt to changing investment trends, emerging asset classes and evolving market requirements. REITs can provide new opportunities for capital mobilisation, while data centres present promising avenues for investment and development. Equally important is the need to establish strong governance frameworks and ensure leadership continuity in family-owned businesses. Platforms such as NAREDCO NextGen can play a significant role in preparing emerging leaders to understand and capitalise on these opportunities."Speaking about the upcoming conclave, Mr. Jay Morzaria, Chairman, NAREDCO NextGen said, "It is becoming increasingly important for the next generation of real estate leaders to understand emerging asset classes, evolving investment structures and professional business practices. The objective of this conclave is to bring young entrepreneurs and experienced industry leaders onto a common platform, enabling them to exchange ideas and explore opportunities that will shape the future direction of the sector."Mr. Ravi Reddy, President, NAREDCO NextGen, said, "The real estate sector is moving towards greater institutional participation, emerging asset classes and more structured business models. Data centres and REITs are creating new opportunities for developers, while professional management, governance and succession planning are becoming increasingly important for family-owned businesses. This conclave will provide an important platform to discuss these developments and their wider implications for the industry."Mr. Siddharth Jain, President, NAREDCO NextGen NCR, said, "Delhi-NCR's real estate market is entering a new growth phase, driven by residential and commercial development, technology-led infrastructure and emerging investment opportunities. With rising demand for AI, cloud computing and digital services, data centres are becoming an important asset class, while REITs offer structured investment opportunities by connecting real estate with capital markets. The next generation of developers must look beyond conventional development and embrace technology, institutional investment and professional business management to drive sustainable growth."The conclave will provide emerging entrepreneurs, real estate investors, financial institutions, technology innovators and other industry stakeholders with an opportunity to exchange ideas, explore new partnerships and gain insights into the evolving dynamics of India's real estate sector.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: Guru Nanak Dev’s teachings a source of inspiration for all humanity: Haryana CM
content: Yamunanagar, Nov 24 (PTI) Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini said the teachings of Sikhism’s founder, Guru Nanak Dev, transcend religion, society and time and continue to inspire all humanity. He was addressing a state-level ceremony organised on the eve of Guru Nanak Dev’s ‘Prakash Parv’ at the sacred Kapal Mochan in Yamunanagar late Monday evening, an official statement on Tuesday said. “Guru Sahib gave society the message of truth, service, equality and harmony, challenging the barriers of caste, social hierarchy and discrimination and emphasising that every human being is equal in the world,” Saini said. A spectacular drone, light and sound show brought Haryana’s glorious heritage to life in the night sky, depicting Guru Nanak Dev’s message of truth, service and equality, Guru Gobind Singh’s 52-day stay at Kapal Mochan and the valour of Baba Banda Singh Bahadur. Saini said the revered pilgrimage site of Kapal Mochan is a remarkable symbol of shared faith and cultural heritage. The sacred site finds mention in the traditions of the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

headline: CAQM report in Supreme Court shows huge gap between policy and groundwork in curbing vehicular emissions
content: New Delhi A chasm exists between the effectiveness of strategies devised by policymakers to control vehicular pollution in Delhi and the National Capital Region (NCR) States through a transition to e-mobility, and the actual ground reality now. The gap between planning for a cleaner tomorrow on paper and the actual grime and dust on the streets of the capital emerges even as the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) confirmed in its latest status report to the Supreme Court that “vehicular pollution is one of the most significant contributing sectors to the generally poor air quality in Delhi-NCR”. For one, the report said there is hardly any infrastructure to provide basic support to e-mobility. Why has the Centre extended PUCC validity to three years for newer vehicles? Why has the Centre extended PUCC validity to three years for newer vehicles? Amendments to sub-rule (7) of Rule 115 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, were notified on November 13, 2026, and came into effect from the date of notification Why has the Centre extended PUCC validity to three years for newer vehicles? storyline 1 For a total 12.94 lakh electric vehicles (EVs) in Delhi and the three NCR States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan, the number of charging points or stations are only 16,785. Uttar Pradesh has only 565 charging points to support 3,47,587 EVs. Haryana has 1,285 charging points to top up 2,18,530 EVs, while Rajasthan has only 22 charging points to fill up 44,987 EVs. On the other hand, Delhi, with 6,83,251 EVs, had 14,913 operational charging points as on October 31, 2026. This means that Delhi has an overwhelming 88.85% of the total 16,785 charging stations/points among the four States, revealing a regional divide in the accessibility to EV support infrastructure. This is significant as the Supreme Court has recently observed that a large part of the pollution in the national capital is caused by vehicles crossing into Delhi from the neighbouring NCR States of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan. How is Delhi implementing restrictions to reduce air pollution? How is Delhi implementing restrictions to reduce air pollution? From Automatic Number Plate Recognition cameras to AI-enabled Integrated Control and Command Centres ICCC and manual checking, the authorities have adopted a mixed approach to impose the restrictions with varying degrees of success How is Delhi implementing restrictions to reduce air pollution? storyline 1 The statistics also reveal that registered electrical vehicles are operating on a fraction of the required grid support, raising questions about the “progress on e-mobility”. However, the dearth in infrastructure continues despite an aggressive push by the Delhi government and NCR States to actuate their medium-term and long-term targeted EV policies. In fact, the Union Ministry of Finance had asked the Ministries and Departments of the Union government to switch over to EVs way back in December 2018. The CAQM, represented by Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, too had issued an advisory in May 2025 to procure or hire cleaner mode vehicles by governments, public undertakings and institutions in NCR to encourage the transformation to non-polluting technology in the transport sector. The Delhi government had notified the Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 on June 30, 2026. The policy, meant to “curb air pollution”, has been effective since July 1 this year. The policy mandates new registration of only electric L5 three-wheelers from January 2027, electric two-wheelers from April 1, 2028 and phased targets for electrification by commercial fleet operators, logistics aggregators, and private schools. While Delhi provides incentives for the purchase of EV vehicles, other NCR States, the CAQM reports, have been “advised” to revise their EV policies to accelerate transition to clean mode of transport. The CAQM reports acknowledges in court that the promotion of e-mobility would require a robust supporting infrastructure, including battery charging stations, battery swapping points, and mechanisms for the disposal of large volumes of spent batteries expected in the coming years. The CAQM report brings to the fore the urgent need to combat vehicular emissions and change to EV mode. The report also showed the formidable presence of end-of-life vehicles plying in the Delhi-NCR region, adding to the pollution problem. Of a total 1,71,76,234 vehicles plying in Delhi NCR, 60.55 lakh adhere to emissions standards of the BS-1 to BS-IV eras. That is, these vehicles had a “much higher polluting potential”. Enforcement measures against end-of-life vehicles were “far from satisfactory” in Delhi and NCR States, the report said. The CAQM noted that efforts by the States and the Delhi government to keep petrol and diesel vehicles more than 15 and 10 years old, respectively, out of the capital’s roads, had yielded results. In this context, the Commission pointed out that the apex court had barred authorities from taking coercive actions against the owners of these over-aged vehicles. The Commission pointed out that out of 25,43,679 end-of-life vehicles reported active in Delhi, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan, as few as nearly 1.86 lakh — a little over 7% — were either scrapped or moved out of the region between January and October 2026.

headline: Are these Haryana locations the next big bet for homebuyers?
content: The proposed Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor could give a fresh push to real estate development in North Haryana, with improved connectivity expected to make cities such as Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal more attractive to homebuyers, working professionals and property developers.The 136.3-km corridor, which will connect Delhi with key cities in Haryana, is expected to reduce travel time significantly and improve access to major economic centres. The project, being developed by the National Capital Region Transport Corporation (NCRTC) at an estimated cost of Rs 33,051 crore, is targeted for completion by 2030.Real estate experts believe faster regional connectivity could encourage people to look beyond established residential markets in Delhi and other parts of the National Capital Region (NCR), while creating opportunities for residential, commercial and mixed-use developments along the route.Abhay Kumar Mishra, President and CEO of Jindal Realty, said the corridor would give a new dimension to connectivity between the NCR and Haryana.“The Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor will give a new dimension to connectivity between the NCR and Haryana. It will shorten the distance between Delhi and cities such as Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal, and help these areas connect better with major economic centres,” he said.Mishra added that improved public transport could unlock the potential of areas that have so far struggled to attract development because of inadequate connectivity.“With fast, convenient public transport, the potential for residential, commercial and mixed-use development in these cities will grow. Growth could pick up especially in areas that have so far been unable to realise their full potential for lack of good connectivity. The corridor can play an important role in balanced urban development in Haryana and in the emergence of new real estate hubs,” he said.SONIPAT, PANIPAT TO ATTRACT HOMEBUYERSThe improved connectivity could make emerging locations along the corridor more viable residential options for people working in Delhi and other NCR business centres.Yashank Wason, Managing Director of Royal Green Realty, said the corridor could create fresh opportunities for homebuyers in Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal, particularly families and working professionals looking for more affordable housing with better connectivity.“With fast and easy access to Delhi, people will take these cities more seriously as places to live. The impact could be felt especially by families and working professionals looking for affordable, convenient housing with better connectivity,” he said.Wason also expects the development to support demand for everyday amenities around the stations.“Demand for retail, schools, healthcare and other everyday amenities around the stations will also grow. In the coming years, the corridor will give the real estate markets of these cities fresh momentum and open up new investment opportunities,” he said.Vinod Kumar, Director and Founder of Sky Byte Developers, said stations at Kundli, Bahalgarh Chowk and Rajiv Gandhi Education City could make daily commuting easier for people living in surrounding areas.“Working professionals will be able to enjoy a better work-life balance by living in these emerging locations while remaining connected to their workplaces in Delhi,” he said.Kumar added that faster connectivity could drive demand for both residential and commercial real estate along the corridor, with the project expected to bring lasting changes to the region's property market.Robin Mangla, President, M3M India, said, "For homebuyers, improved connectivity translates into greater flexibility in commuting, better access to employment hubs and enhanced convenience in everyday living.""For developers, it creates opportunities to explore residential destinations aligned with evolving buyer preferences, particularly in the premium and luxury segments, where location, accessibility, quality and lifestyle offerings play a significant role in purchase decisions. Such infrastructure developments can further strengthen the region's appeal as a residential and investment destination," he added. TOD POLICY COULD SUPPORT ORGANISED DEVELOPMENTThe Haryana government's inclusion of the corridor in its Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) policy could further support real estate activity around stations.Under the policy, high-rise residential buildings, offices, retail spaces and commercial complexes are expected to expand around transit stations, encouraging development closer to public transport networks.Santosh Agarwal, Executive Director & CFO, Alpha Corp Development Limited, said that the Namo Bharat corridor is creating greater opportunities for residential development beyond established urban pockets, particularly around transit nodes and emerging industrial and logistics hubs."As employment opportunities deepen, we expect both end-user and investor demand to strengthen across these corridors. In the coming years, continued infrastructure development is likely to reshape Haryana's residential landscape, unlocking new growth corridors and investment opportunities," he said.The corridor is expected to have 22 stations, most of which will be elevated. Trains will have a maximum design speed of 180 kmph and an operating speed of 160 kmph, with services expected every five to 10 minutes.The project could significantly reduce travel times between Delhi and the Haryana cities along the route. The journey from Delhi to Panipat, which currently takes around two to two-and-a-half hours by road or regular train, is expected to come down to about an hour. Travel time to Karnal could fall from three-and-a-half to four hours to around an hour and a half.With improved connectivity and development planned around transit stations, the corridor could gradually change how homebuyers and developers view the emerging property markets of North Haryana.(Disclaimer: The views, opinions, recommendations, and suggestions expressed by expertsbrokerages in this article are their own and do not reflect the views of the India Today Group. It is advisable to consult a qualified broker or financial advisor before making any actual investment or trading choices.)- EndsMust Watch

headline: Criminal having previous conviction can't be given bail only on strength of right to speedy trial: Supreme Court
content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court has said that a criminal, having antecedents and a previous conviction, cannot be released on bail merely on the strength of his right to a speedy trial. .A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar made the observation while setting aside an order of the Punjab and Haryana High Court granting bail to an accused in a murder case. ."The right to speedy trial is always considered to be a facet of Article 21 of the Constitution of India but, at the same time, when the accused is involved in committing a heinous offence, the right of the accused and the interest of the society, including the interest of the victim and his family, is also required to be seen," the bench said. .The bench said it appeared that neither the previous conviction of the accused was ever brought to the notice of the high court nor his involvement in other criminal cases was placed before the high court at the time of hearing of the bail petition. ."A criminal, having antecedents and previous conviction, cannot be released on bail merely on the strength of his/her right to speedy trial," the top court said in its November 18 order. ."It is the duty of the court to maintain balance between the two facets, i.e., right to speedy trial and the societal interest, by releasing a person on bail while he is involved in a series of offences and particularly when the bail order has been secured by making an incorrect statement before the high court," it said. .The apex court passed the order while hearing an appeal filed by the complainant, who is the father of the deceased, challenging a January 2026 order of the high court granting bail to the accused. .Supreme Court to hear on Wednesday pleas of Sharjeel Imam, Umar Khalid seeking bail in UAPA case.The bench noted that the high court had granted bail on the grounds that the accused was in jail for over five years. .The complainant had argued that the high court ought to have considered all relevant aspects of the matter, including the criminal antecedents of the accused and particularly the fact that he was earlier convicted in an attempt to murder case. .The counsel appearing for the accused said he had mentioned his criminal antecedents in his bail application filed before the high court. .The top court noted that while preferring the bail petition before the high court, the accused made a statement at two places that he was not involved in any other case except the present one. .It said he had concealed his conviction in the previous case in which he was convicted and sentenced for attempting to take the life of the same person, who is the deceased in this case. .The bench said the present crime was committed while the accused was on bail in the case where he stood convicted for committing the offence of attempt to murder. .It said the high court ought not have released the accused on bail pending trial. .While allowing the appeal, the bench set aside the high court order and directed the accused to surrender before the court concerned within a week.

headline: Haryana to stock 2 lakh fish fingerlings in suitable water bodies and waterlogged areas
content: Chandigarh: The Haryana government will stock two lakh fish fingerlings using various waterlogged areas and suitable water bodies in each district of the state to boost fish production and create livelihood opportunities for fishermen and entrepreneurs. .Shyam Singh Rana, Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare, Animal Husbandry and Dairying and Fisheries Minister, said that the initiative was launched at Jal Sagar in Budh Majra village of Yamunanagar district. .According to the minister, the initiative would not only boost fish production but also help conserve aquatic biodiversity and create new livelihood opportunities for local fishermen and entrepreneurs. .Last year, 2 lakh fish fingerlings were stocked in Ballewala village. .A twist in genes turns fish into better fathers.The state government's objective is to make better use of available water resources, strengthen the fisheries sector and enhance the income of fish farmers, Rana said. .So far, 49,034 acres of water areas have been brought under fish farming, resulting in a fish production of 1.47 lakh metric tonnes. Additionally, 4,953 acres of saline-affected water area have been brought under white shrimp farming, he said, according to an official statement. .Rana further said that cold chain facilities with a combined capacity of approximately 4,300 tonnes and 18 fish feed mills have been established in the state. This year, three mobile water-testing laboratory vans have also been deployed to provide farmers with on-site soil and water testing facilities at their ponds. .He said that the government would establish two processing units in Karnal and Sirsa and construct two fish markets in Hisar and Faridabad. Centres of excellence would also be set up in Bhiwani and Sirsa districts. .The minister further stated that the Fisheries Department's budget has increased from approximately Rs 6.99 crore in 2014-15 to Rs 242.40 crore in 2026-27, reflecting the BJP government's commitment to the welfare of farmers. .He appealed to farmers across the state to pledge to conserve water and aquatic resources so that Haryana can achieve new milestones in the fisheries sector.

headline: EEMA North in Focus: Meet the Team Leading the 2026-2028 Tenure
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 24: Event and Entertainment Management Association (EEMA) introduced the North Zone Team for the 2026-2028 tenure at EEMA North SAMVAAD 2026, held at Kosmos Conventions, Gurugram, reaffirming its commitment to strengthening regional representation, fostering industry collaboration and building a more connected events fraternity.Deepak Choudhary, President, EEMA, added: "EEMA's strength lies in its people and the collective spirit of the fraternity. The formation of the new EEMA North Team is an important step towards strengthening our regional presence, encouraging greater member participation and creating meaningful opportunities for collaboration. I am confident that the new team will play a significant role in advancing our vision of a more organised, recognised and future-ready industry."Mahavir Pratap Sharma, Executive Vice President, EEMA, added: "Strong regional leadership is fundamental to building a stronger national association. EEMA North has an important role to play in bringing members together, fostering relationships and creating a platform where ideas translate into meaningful action. We look forward to greater engagement, stronger industry representation and initiatives that create lasting value for the fraternity."Vipul Pandhi, Vice President - North, EEMA, added: "Our vision is to build a more connected and engaged fraternity where every member feels represented, heard and involved. Through meaningful conversations, knowledge sharing and collaborative initiatives, we aim to create real value for our members and strengthen EEMA's presence across North India."EEMA North Team for the 2026-2028 tenure is led Vipul Pandhi (Vice President - North), Naveen Gupta (Joint Secretary - North), Karan Mehta and Alok Nagpal (Committee Members), supported by Vanessa Williams (State Head - Delhi), Shaleen Kapur (State Head - Punjab), Suman Raina (State Head - Rajasthan), Atul Chabra (State Head - Haryana) and Mohd. The team will focus on creating opportunities for meaningful dialogue, professional development and collaboration among event and experiential industry stakeholders.Through initiatives such as EEMA North SAMVAAD, the association seeks to build stronger connections between members, address regional industry priorities and facilitate conversations that translate into collective progress.The 2026-2028 tenure reflects EEMA's continued commitment to empowering regional leadership, strengthening industry representation and building a more inclusive, organised and future-ready events fraternity.About EEMAEvent and Entertainment Management Association (EEMA) is India's apex body representing the events, experiential marketing and entertainment industry. It brings together event management companies, wedding planners, MICE professionals, experiential agencies and allied industry stakeholders, working towards the growth, recognition and professional development of the sector.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL.
