headline: Kirori’s ‘Haryana model’ remark stirs up spectre of leadership change in Raj
content: Jaipur: Amid introspection and stocktaking in the BJP camp after Congress’ decisive sweep in the recently concluded panchayat polls, cabinet minister Kirori Lal Meena stirred up controversy Monday after invoking BJP’s “Haryana model” as a possible template for Rajasthan.The reference was to BJP replacing Haryana chief minister Manohar Lal Khattar with Nayab Singh Saini in a move that Meena implied was responsible for powering the party back into office in the 2024 assembly polls.Meena was responding to questions over Congress’s claim that BJP’s loss in the panchayat polls was a “litmus test” – a referendum on its popularity and performance – and a clear sign that the party would face ouster in the next assembly polls due in Dec 2028.While Meena neither named chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma nor criticised the state govt’s performance, he seemed to imply that a change in leadership may restore the public’s faith in the party in power.“Congress is mistaken in its perception. In Haryana, Khattar sahib was replaced by Nayab sahib, and BJP won by a huge majority,” Meena said while speaking to reporters at BJP state headquarters.BJP replaced Manohar Lal Khattar with Nayab Singh Saini as Haryana chief minister in March 2024, six months before state assembly polls. The party went on to win 48 of 90 seats and formed the govt for a third consecutive term.Meena, who holds charge as agriculture minister, had earlier offered to resign from the cabinet after BJP lost several Lok Sabha seats in eastern Rajasthan in 2024, taking “moral responsibility” for the setback. The party leadership, however, did not accept his resignation and he later resumed his ministerial duties.BJP’s recent drubbing at local body polls has elicited biting remarks from several corners within the party fold.Speaking in Chandigarh Saturday, Punjab Governor and former Rajasthan minister Gulab Chand Kataria called for a review of the party’s performance, saying the results were “not satisfactory” and required corrective action.“The current situation (in Rajasthan) is not ideal, and I say this having worked in this field for many years. It is simply not satisfactory,” Kataria said.“We must carefully examine the underlying reasons for this and take corrective action, because we exist to serve the public. If the people are unhappy with us, it indicates a shortcoming in our work,” he added.Echoing similar sentiments, Union minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat too acknowledged that Rajasthan’s panchayat poll outcomes fell short of expectations.After meeting BJP state president Madan Rathore and organisation general secretary Ajaey Kumar in Jaipur Sunday, Shekhawat said the party would review the results thoroughly, focusing on gaps in the implementation of govt schemes, delivery of benefits to beneficiaries and the communication of those benefits to the wider public.

headline: Namo Bharat Corridor: Could Delhi-Panipat Rail Link Drive Housing Demand In North Haryana?
content: Could the launch of the Namo Bharat Corridor result in a boost for housing demand in North Haryana? As per reports the connectivity plans put Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal in focus. While ANAROCK's data states residential prices in Sonipat are likely to be at Rs 3,500-6,000 per sq ft, compared with Rs 10,000-18,000 per sq ft in Gurugram, Knight Frank’s data highlights higher annual capital growth for Tier-II markets than Tier-I markets overall; this broader assessment is not for any specific city. The proposed 136.3-km Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor is expected to connect Delhi with Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal. Approved by the Haryana Cabinet in March 2026, the project has an estimated cost of Rs 33,051 crore and is targeted for completion by 2030. Once operational, travel to Panipat is expected to take about an hour and to Karnal around 90 minutes. Industry experts believe this corridor could give homebuyers' more choices, beyond the current established NCR areas and boost access to some employment and education centres. With 22 proposed stations and trains expected to operate every five to ten minutes, the project could make daily commuting more convenient for working professionals, students and business owners. Parvinder Singh, CEO, Trident Realty, said, "the Delhi-Panipat-Karnal Namo Bharat corridor could be a significant catalyst for transforming the residential landscape of North Haryana. Spanning approximately 136 km, the proposed corridor will connect key growth centres, including Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal, with Delhi through a faster regional transit network. Improved connectivity can expand homebuyers' choices beyond established NCR markets, while creating opportunities for planned residential developments and integrated townships. The inclusion of the corridor under Haryana's Transit-Oriented Development policy further strengthens the potential for organised urban growth around transit nodes. Over time, accessibility, social infrastructure and employment opportunities could drive demand for quality housing." Experts believe the proposed corridor could strengthen regional connectivity and improve access to key economic centres across NCR. Abhay Kumar Mishra, President and CEO of Jindal Realty said, "the Delhi–Panipat–Karnal Namo Bharat corridor will give a new dimension to connectivity between the NCR and Haryana. It will shorten the distance between Delhi and cities such as Sonipat, Panipat and Karnal, and help these areas connect better with major economic centres."

headline: Cyber attack puts Haryana’s digital payments under scanner | Hindustan Times
content: A suspected cyberattack on the enterprise resource planning (ERP) software of Haryana’s development and panchayats department involving an unauthorised payment of about ₹75 lakh to an unknown vendor prompted the state government on Monday to issue stringent cybersecurity and financial security instructions to departments.Officials said the ERP software has been operational in the department for four years. The suspected cyber hacking reportedly took place in November when an unauthorised transaction was allegedly initiated through the department’s digital financial system. The alleged fraudulent payment involved funds from the state finance commission (SFC) account maintained with Punjab National Bank (PNB). While gram panchayats submit requests for vendor payments through the system, an unauthorised payment of around ₹75 lakh to an unknown vendor reportedly came to light. The alleged transaction is suspected to have been carried out through instructions generated or processed through the ERP system. While the alleged instruction generated by the department to make the payment has been communicated by the bank to the department, the ERP logs available with the department do not show such a command, officials said. A first information report (FIR) has been registered at Panchkula and a special investigation team under DCP, crime, Panchkula Amarinder Singh was set up to probe the suspected cyber hacking.Also read: Haryana orders audit of government portals, digital payment systemsDepartments told to reconcile electronic transactions every dayMeanwhile, the finance department (FD) in its November 23 instructions, made four cybersecurity and financial safeguards mandatory for all departments, boards, corporations etc. The instructions issued by the additional chief secretary, finance, stated that automated reconciliation of electronic transactions should be done daily. Discrepancies between financial records of departments and bank statements should be resolved within 24 hours. Departments have been directed to prepare authenticated lists of authorised beneficiaries, vendors and payees and submit them directly to their respective banks. No payments should be routed to accounts outside the approved beneficiary list, the instructions said.The FD has also directed all public entities to initiate migration of their applications, databases and servers to approved government cloud infrastructure. Hosting public workloads on unverified third-party commercial platforms has been prohibited.Also read: ₹25.67 crore from Gurugram payments firm, two held">Hackers siphon off ₹25.67 crore from Gurugram payments firm, two heldMaker-checker system to prevent single-user payment approvalsAnother key measure put in place is the mandatory implementation of a maker-checker mechanism in financial systems operating through parent-child account structures. Under this arrangement, no single user or automated process at the child level will be permitted to independently initiate and finalise a payment.The finance department has directed departments to submit a compliance readiness report within 15 working days warning that failure to comply may result in temporary suspension of digital treasury disbursement windows.

headline: Haryana farmer leaders unite to protest against sugarcane prices | Hindustan Times
content: With the aim of intensifying the ongoing stir against the Nayab Singh Saini government over sugarcane prices, farmer leaders from various factions joined hands to form Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha on Monday. This is the first time since the 2020-21 agitation against the farm laws that farmer leaders from different ideologies met jointly at Neem Sahib Gurudwara, Kaithal to decide on a possible unity. At the meeting attended by senior farmer leaders Gurnam Singh Charuni and Ratan Mann from the Tikait group as well as their aides, the gathering decided to fight the ongoing movement demanding the sugarcane price of ₹600 per quintal.The meeting unanimously decided that the state’s farmer organisations would collectively participate in all programs of the ongoing movements at sugar mills, the agriculture minister’s residence and other places.Charuni said that at the meeting which was also attended by representatives of Sanyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) and Sanyukt Kisan Mazdoor Morcha (SKMM), it was decided that all organizations would extend their full support to the movement to close all sugar mills in the state. “It was also decided in the meeting that all farmer organisations from Haryana would actively participate in the protest outside the CM’s residence on December 2,” he added. Similarly, Mann said that in the future, all struggles and movements related to farmers’ interests will be fought with complete solidarity under the banner of the Haryana Sanjha Sangharsh Morcha.He said that unity among farmer organisations is the need of the hour to strongly raise farmers’ issues and demands. “Despite the existence of separate organisations, farmers’ interests are paramount. Now, the farmers’ struggle will be fought with mutual solidarity and collective strength as we showed during the 2020 agitation on Delhi borders,” Mann said. In the past few weeks, farmers have escalated their agitation in various parts of the state threatening to disrupt operations at cooperative and private mills, days after the government announced a hike of ₹15 for the season taking the state advised price (SAP) to ₹430 per quintal.The farmers have so far decided to stage protests at 14 sugar mills across the state, planning also to stop harvesting and lock the mills.A group of farmers from the Tikait group led by district president Subhash Gujjar, has staged a permanent sit-in outside the residence of agriculture minister Shyam Singh Rana in Radaur town of Yamunanagar.

headline: Haryana CM Saini calls for strengthening local governance | Hindustan Times
content: Gurugram: Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Monday called for strengthening panchayats and municipal bodies to transform them into effective local governments, while also emphasising on greater financial autonomy, administrative powers and accountability in delivering public services.Speaking at a two-day national conference on empowering panchayats and municipalities in Gurugram, the chief minister said, “The objective is to empower panchayats and municipalities and transform local bodies into local governments. This represents a change in our approach to governance and the way we work.”He said that panchayats and municipalities should evolve into institutions that listen to citizens, take timely decisions and remain accountable for their work.While stating that the subject of the conference had a direct bearing on the lives of citizens across the country, Saini also identified authority, financial stability and effective service delivery as the “three pillars of this transformation”.On boosting grassroots institutions, he said the government had undertaken steps to ensure that resources for development works were transferred directly to panchayats. He said that ₹1,056.75 crore was transferred directly into the accounts of Panchayati Raj institutions on June 9 when 350 Atal libraries were also inaugurated.Stating that the state government’s 2026-27 budget proposed to reserve 5% funds for the maintenance of community assets, he said, the government had also introduced provisions for representation of the Backward Classes-B category through the Haryana Panchayati Raj Amendment Act, 2024, while women had been given 50% representation in village water and sewerage committees.On municipal governance, Saini said the government had proposed a councillor emergency fund in the 2026-27 budget to help elected representatives address smaller but essential problems in their wards without unnecessary delays.He cited Haryana’s property tax collection of ₹709.51 crore in 2025-26 as an indicator of the capacity of municipal bodies to generate regular local revenue and strengthen their financial position.The CM also highlighted the government’s push towards digital governance, saying schemes and public services in Haryana had been brought onto digital platforms to improve accessibility and service delivery.Referring to the state’s infrastructure and environmental initiatives, Saini said memoranda of understanding were signed on August 29 to set up four integrated waste-to-energy plants for strengthening waste management and promoting resource recovery.Suggestions emerging from the discussions during the conference, he said, should be incorporated into Haryana Vision 2047 and linked with the Sustainable Development Goals through local-level plans.The two-day conference brought together elected representatives, policymakers, experts and officials from different parts of the country to discuss ways to strengthen local governance, improve financial resources and make grassroots institutions more responsive to citizens.

headline: Rural NCR areas exposed to higher levels of toxic air: Study
content: New Delhi: Rural areas outside the national capital are exposed to a much higher load of toxic air due to the continued practice of biomass burning mostly for cooking and heating twice a day, even though urban Delhi gets the maximum attention and resources for tackling air pollution, an Indo-US team reported on Monday. Carried out by a team led by scientists at the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi and University of California, Berkeley, the study challenges the common perception of urban areas being pollution hotspots. They showed that the level of PM2.5 - ultra-small particles that enter the lungs and bloodstream causing serious health damage - released by houses in rural Haryana consistently exceeded those in the megacity by around 20% in every month between July and November, 2024 when the study was conducted. .'We want only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi': SC amid air pollution crisis.Their analysis showed air pollution peaking in the morning between 6-10 AM and evening between 4-8 pm at rural sites, but such peaks were absent in urban sites. The spikes, according to the authors, are due to the use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry. "Anti-pollution measures being taken by the authorities are implemented in core urban areas. Rural areas are not targeted for mitigation. But we must take such measures in rural and peri-urban areas. Also we need to initiate pollution measurements in these areas for effective interventions," Sagnik Dey, scientist at IIT Delhi's Centre for Atmospheric Sciences and one of the team leaders told DH. Since Delhi is often considered the world's most polluted megacity, the national capital gets priority in data collection and air pollution mitigation measures. For instance, the Central Pollution Control Board runs 59 air pollution monitoring stations in Delhi as against three in Faridabad, nine in Ghaziabad, seven each in Noida and Greater Noida and four in Gurugram. The National Capital Region comprises 37 districts including 13 in Delhi. .Delhi air pollution: CAQM directs district-level action plans for 2027 to reduce AQI by 15-20% . To capture the ground realities, Dey, Joshua Apte from UC Berkeley and team members from other institutes used their own network of sensors connecting 32 rural and 17 urban sites. Since the rural sites were 80 km upwind of Delhi, they were free from the air pollution generated in the national capital. Still the data shows a consistent sharp rise in PM2.5 concentration in the morning and evening in rural sites. In the post-monsoon months (October, November), the difference between the rural and urban zones was larger. The overall pattern that emerges is that the peak component PM2.5 is consistently and substantially elevated for rural sites. "We attribute these events to widespread use of solid fuels for cooking, heating, and small-scale industry in suburban and rural settings," the team reported in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Dey said multiple studies and surveys in the past few years have shown people went back to solid fuels such as coal, dung and wood instead of LPG provided under Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana due to factors like high cost and availability. The scientists analysed five months of data in the present study, but monitored the sites for 16 months. "The data shows that the gap between urban and rural areas is increasing in terms of air pollution. The signals emerging from the NCR is that people are using solid fuels," he added.

headline: BJP govt has ruined the state’s healthcare system: Hooda
content: Jind: Leader of the opposition in Haryana assembly, Bhupinder Singh Hooda, said on Monday that the BJP govt had proven to be a “complete failure” in providing employment to youth, security to the general public, education to children, and quality healthcare services to patients.“This govt has devastated the state’s healthcare system. The situation is such that hospitals and medical colleges alike lack both doctors and other essential staff,” Hooda said.Hooda was in Jind city to express his condolences following the passing of Shamsher Singh, son of a former MLA. The former CM met the bereaved family and offered his sympathies. He remarked that the loss to the state’s politics caused by Shamsher Singh’s demise could never be filled.Later, while responding to questions from the media, Hooda expressed deep concern over the crumbling state of healthcare in the region. He pointed out that out of 1,064 sanctioned posts of pharmacists in govt hospitals, more than 450 remained vacant.Furthermore, there are 5,314 vacant positions for doctors and paramedical staff across govt medical colleges, comprising 2,572 posts for doctors and 2,742 for paramedical staff. Due to the absence of staff to dispense medication, long queues of patients are formed at the counters, he said.According to a report, in eight govt medical colleges across Haryana, 2,572 out of 3,843 sanctioned posts for doctors, approximately 67%, are vacant. More than half of the positions for paramedical staff are also unfilled. The situation in the newer medical colleges is even worse. At the Jind medical college, 555 out of 559 posts are vacant; in Mahendragarh, 492 out of 559 are vacant; and in Bhiwani, 477 out of 552 posts remain unoccupied, said the senior Congress functionary.Even at the state’s largest institution, PGIMS Rohtak, more than 40% of the positions for doctors and Group-A staff remain vacant, he added.“There is a severe shortage of specialist doctors, such as radiologists, gynaecologists, surgeons, and paediatricians at primary health centers, community health centers, and civil hospitals. Consequently, these institutions have effectively been reduced to mere referral centres,” Hooda said.“The primary reasons for doctors leaving their jobs include excessive work pressure, lack of timely promotions, limited career growth, shortage of adequate resources and equipment, and the prospect of better pay and working conditions in the private sector. Govt has failed to provide an environment conducive to the delivery of medical services, which is why doctors are choosing to leave,” the LoP explained.Hooda said this had a direct impact on ordinary patients. “Due to the unavailability of treatment at the primary and secondary levels, the entire burden has shifted onto larger hospitals and medical colleges. Patients are forced to endure long queues in OPDs, extended waiting periods for diagnostic tests, and a lack of timely access to specialist care. headline: ‘Have some shame’: Haryana minister raps officials over public grievances, warns of action
content: Hisar: Haryana minister Krishan Kumar Bedi on Monday came down heavily on district officials over alleged negligence in addressing public complaints during a meeting of the District Public Relations and Grievances Committee in Fatehabad.Warning officers against taking public issues lightly, Bedi made it clear that laxity would invite strict disciplinary action. Of the 12 grievances taken up during the session—eight fresh complaints and four pending from the previous meeting—six were resolved on the spot.For the remaining six, the minister ordered the constitution of inquiry committees and sought detailed reports at the next meeting.Tempers flared when a long-pending complaint regarding sewage discharge onto private land in the Ratia Chungi area came up for hearing. Pulled up over the prolonged inaction, the executive engineer (XEN) of the public health engineering department faced the minister’s ire. “Have some shame,” Bedi told the official, directing immediate resolution of the issue.In another matter concerning the dilapidated condition of a 33-foot-wide main street in Nahla village of the Bhuna block, the block development and panchayat officer (BDPO) informed the committee that the repair estimate had been prepared and work would commence once funds were released.Displeased with the response, Bedi remarked that officials would not be at peace if the public continued to suffer. “Relief has to be provided to the people—whether by the officials, the deputy commissioner, or by me personally. Satisfying the public is the responsibility of the administration,” he said.“Either you (BDPO) apologise or I will, but the public’s problem must be solved,” the minister said while ordering swift construction of the street and assured advance funding under D-Plan if required.Bedi also cautioned officials against attending future grievance meetings without thorough preparation, noting that the time of complainants, public representatives, and officers alike was valuable. He warned that if negligence persisted, officials risked arriving at the next meeting with suspension orders issued directly from Chandigarh.Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Bedi said action would also be taken if funds available with the municipal council were lying unutilised. Officials stalling development works due to vested interests or apathy will face stringent action, he warned.

headline: Haryana officers’ school visits to be linked to performance
content: Chandigarh: Haryana has decided to link school adoption and inspection duties of Class I and II officers to their annual confidential reports (ACRs), making school visits and follow-up reports part of their performance assessment.Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi on Monday directed that a dedicated column be added to the ACR format for the current reporting year to record the schools adopted by officers, visits undertaken and inspections conducted. Officers will also have to attach inspection reports to their annual self-appraisals.Reviewing the school adoption initiative, Rastogi said the move aimed to ensure greater administrative accountability and sustained involvement in improving govt schools. He directed all administrative secretaries and departments to issue instructions for incorporating the changes in the ACR format.He said officers should assess the academic environment, interact with students and teachers, examine infrastructure utilisation and identify gaps requiring corrective action. Inspections must follow the prescribed standard operating procedure, with observations documented for follow-up.“The ultimate idea is that all schools function to the best of their ability and capability,” he said.Principal secretary, school education, Vijay Dahiya said officers were required to visit their adopted schools at least thrice a year and upload inspection reports on the designated portal.

headline: Centre, Haryana push for financially self-reliant panchayats, civic bodies
content: Chandigarh: Union power, housing and urban affairs minister Manohar Lal Khattar and Haryana chief minister Nayab Singh Saini on Monday called for making panchayats and urban local bodies (ULBs) financially self-reliant by granting them greater powers, independent revenue sources, and accountability for civic service delivery.Addressing a two-day national summit on devolution of powers, financial sustainability, and effective service delivery at Gurugram University, the two leaders urged grassroots institutions to reduce their dependence on government grants and monetise local land, buildings, water bodies, and other assets.Khattar said stronger Panchayats and ULBs could better meet public expectations as sarpanches, councillors, mayors, and chairpersons were directly connected with residents, provided they had adequate funds, administrative authority, and manpower.To boost local revenues, the Union minister suggested leasing panchayat land through transparent procedures, using village ponds for fish farming, developing markets and buildings for regular rental income, and deploying funds lying in fixed deposits to build income-generating assets.Calling for community participation, he proposed designating one day every month for voluntary labour (shramdaan) in villages, with Gram Sabhas identifying tasks such as repairing and painting schools, cleaning streets and peripheral roads (phirni), maintaining ponds, and holding plantation drives.He also advocated a village caretaker system to maintain public properties. Citing a pilot in his Karnal parliamentary constituency, he said 15 village caretakers had been appointed alongside a dedicated portal where citizens report infrastructure damage via photographs for time-bound action by departments concerned.CM Saini said the vision of Viksit Bharat-2047 could be achieved only when villages and urban wards become empowered centres of development rather than the last link in the chain, adding that priorities identified by gram sabhas should anchor panchayat development plans.Highlighting Haryana’s grassroots reforms, Saini cited mandatory educational qualifications for panchayat representatives (2015), 50% reservation for women in panchayati raj institutions (2020), and the lal dora-free initiative that gave rural residents property ownership rights and was later adopted nationally as the SVAMITVA scheme.To strengthen panchayat finances, Saini said the state had decided to offer matching grants equivalent to the water bills collected by villages, while urging representatives to prioritise water conservation amid declining groundwater levels.Calling for healthy competition and recognition for high-performing wards and villages, the CM asked ULBs to explore new revenue avenues while ensuring sanitation, drinking water, roads, and sewerage services.Development and panchayats minister Krishan Lal Panwar, urban local bodies minister Vipul Goel, and SJHIFM director general Raj Nehru were among those attending the event, which has drawn panchayati raj and ULB representatives from Haryana and other states.

headline: Rise above party politics for Nov 26 session: Haryana speaker
content: Chandigarh: A special session of the Haryana assembly will be held on Nov 26 to deliberate on the state’s six decades of development, public participation in building a developed state, and the role of elected representatives in upholding constitutional values, speaker Harvinder Kalyan said on Monday.Urging MLAs across party lines to rise above politics, Kalyan called for active and constructive participation to strengthen democratic institutions and reinforce public trust.The session forms part of the ongoing Constitution Fortnight being observed by the assembly since Nov 2.Discussions on Nov 26 will focus on parliamentary functioning, democratic traditions, and the responsibility of legislators in raising public awareness about citizens’ constitutional rights and duties.Recalling the recent “Janpratinidhi Sammelan” held at Indradhanush Auditorium in Panchkula, which saw participation from sitting, former, and independent legislators across parties, Kalyan said the suggestions shared by senior public representatives offered valuable guidance for future generations and strengthened commitment to constitutional principles.

headline: BJP govt has ruined state healthcare system: Hooda
content: Former Chief Minister and Leader of the Opposition Bhupinder Singh Hooda today said the BJP government had been a complete failure in providing employment to the youth, security to the general public, education to children and quality healthcare services to patients.Interacting with mediapersons during his visit to Jind, the former CM said the government had devastated the state’s healthcare system. The situation was such that hospitals and medical colleges alike lacked both doctors and other essential staff. Hooda was in Jind to condole the demise of Shamsher Singh, son of former MLA Fateh Singh.Expressing concern over the crumbling state of healthcare in the region, he pointed out that of 1,064 sanctioned posts of pharmacists in government hospitals, more than 450 were vacant. Furthermore, there were 5,314 vacant positions for doctors and paramedical staff across government medical colleges, including 2,572 posts for doctors and 2,742 for paramedical staff.“There is a severe shortage of specialist doctors, such as radiologists, gynaecologists, surgeons and paediatricians, at primary health centres, community health centres and civil hospitals. Consequently, these institutions have effectively been reduced to mere referral centres,” he said.“The primary reasons for doctors leaving their jobs include excessive work pressure, lack of timely promotions, limited career growth, shortage of adequate resources and equipment, and the prospect of better pay and working conditions in the private sector. The government has failed to provide an environment conducive to the delivery of medical services, which is why doctors are choosing to leave,” he alleged.Hooda said due to the unavailability of treatment at the primary and secondary levels, the entire burden had shifted to larger hospitals and medical colleges.“Patients are forced to endure long queues in OPDs, extended waiting periods for diagnostic tests and a lack of timely access to specialist care. In many instances, patients lose their lives while waiting, never receiving the treatment they need,” Hooda said.

headline: Four untapped Haryana drains discharge 297 MLD wastewater into Yamuna, CPCB finds
content: NEW DELHI: Four major drains in Haryana remain untapped, discharging a combined 297.23 million litres per day (MLD) of wastewater into the Yamuna, carrying a daily biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) pollution load of 9.649 tonnes per day (TPD), according to a Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) reply to an RTI query.A joint inspection by CPCB and Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) between April 15 and 23, 2026, found that the drains -- Budhiya Nala and Alipur drain in Faridabad, Dhanaura Escape in Karnal and Drain no. 2 in Panipat -- were untapped.Budhiya Nala recorded the highest discharge -- 152.1 MLD -- that had a BOD load of 4.715 tonnes per day. Dhanaura Escape discharged 101 MLD, carrying a BOD load of 3.434 tonnes per day, while Alipur drain recorded 44.13 MLD and discharged a BOD load of 1.5 tonnes per day. Drain 2 in Panipat was blocked and had stagnant water.The inspection also documented municipal solid waste being dumped in and along Alipur drain. Photographs included in the CPCB annexure show garbage accumulated along the drain in Faridabad.Taking note of the findings, CPCB director (water quality management-II) Deenbandhu Gouda wrote to the HSPCB member secretary on Sept 15, directing authorities to identify the sources responsible for the high BOD and act against the polluters.The board also called for the removal of waste from the Alipur drain, enforcement of the Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026, and interim remediation measures until the drains are connected to sewage treatment plants (STPs).CPCB sought an action taken report (ATR) within 30 days of the communication.“The key questions now are whether Haryana authorities have submitted the ATR, what concrete steps have been taken to stop untreated wastewater from entering the Yamuna, and when these four drains will finally be connected to adequate sewage treatment infrastructure,” said Amit Gupta, environment and RTI activist.“The findings raise serious concerns about the continued discharge of untreated wastewater into the Yamuna despite official inspections and regulatory directions,” he added.

headline: 19 bites a day: Dog menace intensifies in Himachal's Hamirpur; nearly 6,000 bite cases reported in 2026
content: As many as 5,876 people were bitten by dogs in Himachal Pradesh’s Hamirpur district over 10 months in 2026, averaging 19 bite cases a day.The Health Department data shines a light on the canine crisis, which is not limited to stray dogs.Between January and October this year, stray dogs accounted for 3,863 bite cases, while pet dogs were involved in 2,013.The number of reported cases this year has already exceeded the total for the entire previous year by 1,551. On average, nearly 19 people have been targeted by dogs every day."Dog bite cases must be taken seriously. People should not be negligent if bitten or scratched by a dog and should immediately visit the nearest healthcare facility for treatment. It is essential to complete the full course of the anti-rabies vaccine as per medical advice," Hamirpur Chief Medical Officer Dr Satish Kumar said on Monday.Allowing pet dogs to roam freely in public spaces, failing to maintain proper control and negligence in their care are posing a risk to public safety too, he said.In Hamirpur town, the worst-hit areas are the Hirangar forest region and Anu zone, as stray dogs are found in great numbers on the Hamirpur-Sujanpur main road and near the Ano chowk. Students exercising here are targeted by the dogs, with residents alleging that the local municipal corporation is silent on this issue..Stray crisis: States need to fix a broken system.The number of people bitten by stray dogs in 2026 was 445 in January, 420 in February, 382 in March, 396 in April, 425 in May, 444 in June, 294 in July, 428 in August, 321 in September, and 308 in October.Meanwhile, regarding pet dogs, the number of people injured by them was 164 in January, 212 in February, 234 in March, 188 in April, 224 in May, 208 in June, 192 in July, 191 in August, 220 in September, and 180 in October.Treating a dog bite as a minor injury can prove costly. Rabies is a serious and life-threatening disease, but it can be prevented through timely treatment and vaccination. If bitten or scratched by a dog, immediately wash the wound thoroughly with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, health officials said.“Regardless of whether the wound is small or large, consult a doctor without delay. Complete the full course of the rabies vaccine as advised by the physician. Do not apply turmeric, chilli, soil, oil, or any other substances to the wound,” they added.(With inputs from PTI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Chandigarh apple trader's Rs 14.64 lakh claim rejected after truck accident over 3.31pm loading time, con
content: CHANDIGARH: The Chandigarh district consumer disputes redressal commission has directed SBI General Insurance Company to pay Rs 14.64 lakh to a Chandigarh-based apple trader whose insurance claim for damaged goods was rejected after a road accident.The commission also ordered the insurer to pay 9% annual interest along with Rs 30,000 as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The case concerns Jaswinder Singh, a 59-year-old apple merchant from Chandigarh, who had taken a Marine Open Insurance Policy from SBI General Insurance to cover apples and pears transported by road across India.According to the complaint, Singh already had an insurance policy valid from July 21, 2023, to March 31, 2024. On August 12, 2023, he paid an additional premium of Rs 24,780 through PhonePe to increase his insurance cover by Rs 1 crore.The insurer subsequently issued an enhanced policy showing a total insured amount of Rs 1 crore, with a maximum limit of Rs 20 lakh per vehicle.The dispute arose when a truck carrying Singh's apple consignment met with an accident on August 16, 2023, causing extensive damage to the goods. After a survey and inspection, the trader sought compensation for his losses.However, SBI General Insurance rejected the claim arguing that the consignment had been loaded and weighed at 3.31pm on August 12, while the enhanced policy became effective only at 7.03pm that day. The company maintained that the journey had started before the insurance cover came into force.The commission, however, found gaps in the insurer's argument. It noted that the insurer had failed to produce reliable evidence, including a fresh insurance proposal form, to establish that the August 12 transaction was for an entirely new policy rather than an enhancement of the existing cover.The commission also examined transport records.While one weighing receipt mentioned 3.31pm, another receipt showed the loaded truck was weighed at 7.38pm, after the policy became effective.A toll plaza record further showed that the vehicle crossed a toll point around 7.51pm, approximately two kilometres from the loading location.These records weakened the insurer's claim that the insured transit had begun before the policy started. The commission held that rejecting the claim on such a technical interpretation amounted to deficiency in service and an unfair trade practice.While the trader had claimed Rs 14.80 lakh, the commission accepted the surveyor's assessed loss of Rs 14.64 lakh.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: ‘Two brothers have reunited again’, says Chouhan on SAD-BJP reunion
content: Chandigarh, Nov 24 (PTI) “Brothers have reunited again”, Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said on Tuesday after BJP and SAD officially announced they would jointly contest the 2027 Punjab Assembly polls, marking the return of the oldest NDA ally after six years. Chouhan’s remarks came after interacting with farmers at a ‘Kisan Choupal’ in Booh Havelian village, Tarn Taran district, Punjab. Sitting amidst the fields and listening to their problems and suggestions, Chouhan congratulated farmers for shunning stubble burning. He also urged the Punjab government to implement the Prime Minister’s Crop Insurance Scheme in the interest of farmers and reiterated the Narendra Modi government’s commitment to farmer-friendly policies and record procurement at MSP. Speaking to reporters on the sidelines, Chouhan, who was asked about the reunion of SAD and BJP, said two brothers have reunited. “It is a very good thing. I believe two brothers have reunited again,” he told reporters.

headline: Punjab polls: SAD, BJP reunification puts both parties back in the reckoning
content: CHANDIGARH The reunification of the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) ahead of the crucial 2027 Punjab Assembly election has put both parties back in the reckoning, even as the State’s political landscape looks headed for a four-cornered fight, with the old partners joining hands to make it more competitive. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/shiromani-akali-dal/ https://www.thehindu.com/topic/bharatiya-janata-party/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/punjab/ In the run-up to the election, due in early 2027, the political positioning of the parties appeared increasingly vulnerable, and political observers felt that the logical way to overcome it was to forge an alliance. After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election Prime Minister Narendra Modi hails the move as ‘putting Punjab and the welfare of Punjabis first’ After six years apart, BJP and Akali Dal announce alliance for Punjab Assembly election storyline 1 The SAD and the BJP have been allies since the late 1990s. However, when farmers’ protests broke out over the Centre’s farm laws, the SAD decided to break away from the National Democratic Alliance in 2020. Later, on November 19, 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the repeal of the farm laws. “With the BJP-Akali re-alliance, both parties are in the reckoning now in the impending Assembly election. In the absence of an alliance, the division of votes would have gone to the advantage of the ruling Aam Aadmi Party. Now it’s unlikely,” said Pramod Kumar, director of the Institute for Development and Communication, Chandigarh. Pointing out that contesting separately, the SAD and the BJP would likely have split the same Opposition space, leaving the AAP and the Congress as the principal rivals, Mr. Kumar said, “With the two now united, the political equation would shift significantly, making them serious contenders.” He added, “Congress, which was appearing to enjoy the advantage of being the alternative to the AAP, will now have to share the anti-incumbency vote with the alliance. Earlier, it could have expected a major share of it.” Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement Former State Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring accuses SAD president Sukhbir Singh Badal, and his wife, former Union Minister Harsimrat Kaur Badal, of misleading people by publicly distancing themselves from the BJP while supporting it on key issues in Parliament Aam Aadmi Party and Congress attack SAD-BJP alliance, call it a political arrangement storyline 1 Ashutosh Kumar, a professor in the political science department of Punjab University in Chandigarh, points out that the alliance could make a difference in a multipolar contest. “In a multipolar contest, even if you get 25%, then you can actually win the seats as well; it can turn into a winnability. The BJP already got about 19% of the vote in the 2024 Lok Sabha poll,” he said. Combining the BJP’s urban vote base with a portion of the Akali Dal’s traditional Sikh support could push the alliance past the 25% threshold that could convert vote share into winnable seats. In Punjab, where ‘Panthic’ politics, a political mobilisation surrounding the Sikh community’s collective identity, continues to be the cornerstone of the electoral space, the re-stitching of the alliance could specifically work in favour of the SAD, which has been struggling to stage a political comeback in the State. A sense in the political circle is that if Akali Dal’s core support base sees a real chance of the party returning to power in 2027 through the BJP alliance, that perception itself could become a rallying point to draw voters back to the SAD led by Sukhbir Singh Badal. Over the past decade, the SAD witnessed a significant downfall in Punjab’s politics, where Sikh identity and its issues have long been central to political discourse, and different Akali groups have been fighting among themselves to capture the ‘Panthic’ space. SAD open to alliances for Chandigarh civic polls, sparks buzz over potential BJP re-alignment SAD open to alliances for Chandigarh civic polls, sparks buzz over potential BJP re-alignment The decision regarding any alliance lies with the central leadership. As of now, we are contesting alone across all 35 wards, says BJP’s Saurabh Joshi SAD open to alliances for Chandigarh civic polls, sparks buzz over potential BJP re-alignment storyline 1 In 2025, the SAD saw a virtual split following the rebel faction forming a new outfit – Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit). Separately, the outfit Waris Punjab De, led by independent Lok Sabha MP Amritpal Singh, a pro-Khalistan propagator who is currently in Dibrugarh jail in Assam under the National Security Act, has been steadily building support within the ‘Panthic’ space, a trend observers link to the weakening of the SAD.

headline: Dental health check-up camp organised at Chandigarh school
content: The DC Montessori Sr Sec (SMART) School, Chandigarh, organised a two-day dental health check-up camp on its premises for students from Pre-Nursery to Class XII, in collaboration with Clove Dental Clinic, Panchkula. A team of well-trained dental professionals visited the school and conducted comprehensive clinical examinations to assess the students’ oral health. During the check-up, the students were made aware of the importance of maintaining good oral hygiene and guided on essential dental care practices, including proper brushing techniques, regular dental check-ups and healthy eating habits. Based on individual assessments, the dental team also recommended appropriate treatments and further consultations wherever required. The initiative aimed to promote awareness about dental hygiene and encourage children to adopt healthy oral care habits from an early age.

headline: PB BJP PRINT MEDIA AT CHANDIGARH
content: Guru Nanak Dev Ji’s Teachings of ‘Kirat Karo, Vand Chhako, Naam Japo’ and ‘Sarbat Da Bhala’ Guide India’s Journey Toward a Developed Nation: PM Narendra Modi Prime Minister participates in sacred Shabad Kirtan on the Prakash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji in New Delhi alongside Delhi LG Taranjit Singh Sandhu and CM Rekha Gupta Chandigarh, November 24-Prime Minister Narendra Modi attended a sacred Shabad Kirtan in New Delhi on the auspicious occasion of the Prakash Purab of Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji, asserting that the timeless teachings of the Sikh Gurus serve as the guiding light for building a Developed India (Viksit Bharat) and fostering global peace through the spirit of Sarbat Da Bhala.Addressing the Saadh Sangat in the presence of revered Sikh saints, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, and Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, the Prime Minister extended greetings to countrymen across the globe. He noted that every word of Gurbani and Kirtan is a form of spiritual practice and recalled his deep personal bond with Sikh traditions, bowing at Sri Harmandir Sahib, partaking in Langar, and his memorable years spent working in Punjab. Honouring Sikh Heritage and Supreme SacrificesHighlighting that this year’s Prakash Purab coincides with the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji, PM Modi paid solemn tribute to Guru Sahib’s supreme sacrifice on the soil of Delhi to protect the nation’s faith, identity, and human values. He also remembered the martyrdom of Bhai Mati Das Ji, Bhai Sati Das Ji, and Bhai Dayala Ji, as well as Sardar Teja Singh Samundri Ji on the centenary of his martyrdom for his pivotal role in the Gurdwara Reform Movement. Outlining the central government’s sustained efforts over the past 12 years to honour Sikh heritage worldwide, the Prime Minister cited: * National and international commemorations of the 350th Prakash Purab of Guru Gobind Singh Ji, the 550th Prakash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev Ji, and the 400th Prakash Purab of Guru Tegh Bahadur Ji at the Red Fort, alongside the ongoing 350th martyrdom year observances.* The nationwide observance of Veer Baal Diwas on December 26 to inspire the younger generation with the unmatched courage of the Sahibzadas and Mata Gujri Ji* Support for the redevelopment of the historic Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara in the Philippines, which the Prime Minister visited recently.

headline: HMBCON 2026 Concludes at PGIMER Chandigarh with a Renewed National Commitment to Expand Human Milk Banking
content: CHANDIGARH, 24.11.26-The 12th Annual Conference of the Human Milk Banking Association of India (HMBAI), HMBCON 2026, organised by the Neonatal Unit, Department of Paediatrics, Postgraduate Institute of Medical Education and Research (PGIMER), Chandigarh, on November 21–22, 2026, concluded with a strong national resolve to expand Comprehensive Lactation Management Centres (CLMCs) and human milk banks across the country. The two-day conference brought together over 200 delegates, faculty members and experts from across India, providing an important platform for knowledge exchange, scientific deliberations and capacity building in human milk banking, breastfeeding support and lactation management. The conference was inaugurated by Prof. Vivek Lal, Director, PGIMER, Chandigarh, who appreciated the initiative and underscored the importance of strengthening human milk banking services to improve neonatal outcomes. Reaffirming the Institute's commitment to this vital cause, he assured the organisers and participating experts of all necessary support and assistance in taking the initiative forward. Emphasising the critical role of human milk banking in neonatal care, Prof. Vivek Lal, Director, PGIMER, said, “Every newborn deserves the best possible start in life, and human milk is among the most precious gifts we can offer to our babies. Strengthening human milk banking and lactation management services is not merely a healthcare initiative; it is an investment in the survival, health and future of our children. PGIMER will extend all possible support to advance this important cause and encourage its wider adoption.” A major highlight of the conference was the organisation of two hands-on workshops focusing on Comprehensive Lactation Management Centre (CLMC)/Human Milk Bank operations and Skills in Breastfeeding. These workshops provided delegates with practical exposure and training in the essential technical and clinical aspects of lactation support, human milk banking and breastfeeding management. A particularly inspiring moment was the 4th Armida Fernandez Oration, delivered by Dr. Sandhya Khadse from Maharashtra, who shared her remarkable 40-year journey and experience in establishing several human milk banks across Maharashtra.

content: Chandigarh: Resident doctors from PGI’s department of community medicine and School of Public Health won seven prizes at the 7th IAPSM Young Leaders’ National Conclave 2026, held at Armed Forces Medical College (AFMC), Pune.Dr Abdul Basith KM, senior resident, won the first prize in the e-poster presentation under the Disease Surveillance and Universal Health Coverage category and third prize in Visual Storytelling.Dr Aastha Sharma, junior resident, bagged the first prize for oral paper presentation in the Digital Health category. She also led her team to victory in the Young Leaders’ Parliament with the SAHAARA (Climate Change Affected Persons Health Security) Bill, 2026, and was adjudged Best Speaker.In the team events, Abdul Basith and Aastha, competing as Team Duodemiology, won the Public Health Hackathon. Team Hidayat, comprising Aastha and junior resident Dr Madhura Sarkar, secured first prize in the IAPSM Public Health Content Creation Challenge on mental health.Hosted by AFMC’s department of community medicine under the Indian Association of Preventive and Social Medicine (IAPSM), the conclave drew 380 delegates from across the country.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Chandigarh: Constitution a living document that must evolve with society, says ex-CJI
content: The Department of Laws, Panjab University (PU), organised the first Prof DN Jauhar annual lecture on Monday, with former Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Jagdish Singh Khehar delivering the inaugural address on the theme of constitutional morality and the evolving interpretation of the Constitution.Addressing law students, research scholars, faculty members and legal professionals at his alma mater, Justice Khehar emphasised that the constitution should not be interpreted merely in the context of its original drafting by the Constituent Assembly. Instead, it should be viewed as a living document that evolves with changing social realities.Referring to landmark Supreme Court judgments delivered in 2018, Justice Khehar discussed the complexities involved in interpreting morality in a diverse society.He observed that when a majority of people subscribe to a particular belief, it often comes to be accepted as the majoritarian understanding ofreality.On the debate surrounding the Uniform Civil Code (UCC), Justice Khehar emphasised the need to examine legislative and policy questions through the lens of constitutional morality.However, he cautioned against making constitutional morality the sole guiding principle for interpreting legislation, noting that its practical application could raise complex questions.The annual lecture has been instituted in memory of Prof DN Jauhar to commemorate his legacy and provide a platform for deliberations on contemporary issues relating to law and constitutional interpretation.The event was attended by Punjab and Haryana High Court Judges Justice Raj Bala, Justice Daya Chaudhury and Justice Aman Chaudhry; Vice-Chancellors Prof Jai Shankar and Prof Paramjeet Jaswal; PU Vice-Chancellor Prof Meenakshi Goyal; Registrar Prof YP Verma; Chairperson of the Department of Laws Prof Vandana Arora; former PU Vice-Chancellor Prof Renu Vig; and former Dean of University Instruction Prof Yojna Rawat. Serving and retired faculty members and university officials were also present.

headline: Chandigarh administration forms coordination committee to ensure leak-free NTA papers
content: The Chandigarh Administration has formed a state-level coordination committee to prevent paper leaks and ensure that entrance examinations conducted by the National Testing Agency (NTA) are transparent, fair and error-free.The committee was formed in compliance with directives issued by the Union Ministry’s Department of Higher Education and the Director General of the NTA on October 23, 2026. The notification was issued on Monday, superseding an earlier order dated February 28, 2025.Under the new system, an integrated strategy will be developed to strengthen examination security and dismantle paper-leak networks through continuous intelligence gathering on security threats and examination-related malpractice.A dedicated hotline is being established between the Chief Secretary of Chandigarh, the Director General of Police of the UT and the Director General of the NTA to facilitate emergency communication and immediate action.The Secretary of Technical Education will be the nodal officer of the committee, while the Inspector General of Police has been appointed as the nodal police officer. Other members include the nodal officer nominated by the NTA, the Director-Principal of Government Medical College and Hospital, Chandigarh (GMCH-32), the State Informatics Officer of the National Informatics Centre (NIC) Secretariat, the Chief Engineer of Chandigarh and a senior officer of the Subsidiary Intelligence Bureau.Panel's responsibilitiesIntegrated strategy against paper leaks: Formulate a coordinated strategy to break paper-leak syndicates through continuous intelligence gathering on examination-related malpractice and security threats.Exam-specific planning: Develop strategies to ensure that each examination is conducted in a fair, transparent and error-free manner, and brief the district-level committees accordingly.Reconstitution of district committees: Ensure that District Level Coordination Committees (DLCCs), headed by the District Magistrate/Collector and Superintendent of Police, are reconstituted and function smoothly.Review of DLCC performance: Assess the performance and functioning of district-level committees after every major examination.Submission of reports to the NTA: Compile observations and suggestions received from the district committees and submit reports to the NTA for necessary action.

headline: Dalai Lama allotted bungalow in Lutyens’ Delhi
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) The Central government has allotted a bungalow to Tibetan spiritual leader the Dalai Lama in Lutyens’ Delhi, sources said on Tuesday. Although there is no official word from the Union Housing and Urban Affairs Ministry, sources said that the Dalai Lama has been allotted the bungalow on Pandit Ravi Shankar Shukla Lane. They said the allotment to Gaden Phodrang Trust — the office of the Dalai Lama — has been made following a request from the Ministry of External Affairs. Such accommodation is generally transferred for three years, with provision for extension. According to the website of Gaden Phodrang, the Trust is dedicated to preserving and upholding the institution of the Dalai Lama and his spiritual work, while advancing his humanitarian vision. The website states that the Trust also supports His Holiness’s core commitments: promoting human values, fostering interfaith harmony, preserving Tibetan culture and identity, protecting the environment, and encouraging a deeper appreciation of ancient Indian wisdom. PTI BUN RUK

headline: TIME’s World’s Best Airports 2027 list: Delhi’s IGI Airport ranks 38th - Which are the top 10?
content: India has secured a spot in TIME magazine’s World’s Best Airports 2027 ranking, with Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International (IGI) Airport emerging as the country’s only entry in the World’s Best Major Airports category.IGI Airport ranked 38th among 47 major airports, with an overall score of 84.96. Singapore’s Changi Airport topped the list, followed by two airports in China.The rankings have been compiled by TIME in collaboration with Statista, taking into account passenger experience and airport operational performance.Despite its position among the 47 major airports featured in the ranking, IGI remains India’s sole representative in this category.The rankings have been compiled by TIME in collaboration with global data platform Statista. The airports have been categorised into four groups — major, large, mid-sized and smaller airports. The rankings also feature separate lists assessing specific services and experiences, including family-friendliness and transit facilities.How did Delhi’s IGI Airport perform in the ranking?Which airports secured the top three positions?Singapore’s Changi Airport was named the world’s best major airport for 2027, with a score of 91.74.China’s Guangzhou Baiyun International Airport secured the second position, while Beijing Daxing International Airport ranked third.World’s best major airports 2027What does TIME’s World’s Best Airports ranking consider?TIME’s 2027 ranking recognises airports that provide a strong passenger experience while maintaining efficient flight operations.The list is divided into four categories based on annual passenger traffic, allowing airports of different sizes to be assessed separately.Which other Indian airports are among the busiest in 2026?While Delhi is India’s only airport featured in TIME’s World’s Best Major Airports category, several other airports across the country handle millions of passengers every year.According to the Airports Authority of India (AAI) passenger traffic figures for FY 2025–26, the following are India’s 10 busiest airports.1. headline: Delhi to set up skill centre in Shalimar Bagh for youth, women
content: New Delhi: Delhi govt will set up an eight-acre skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh that will have 14 laboratories, smart classrooms, an entrepreneurship and incubation facility and a two-acre horticulture training field.The centre will offer technical and IT-related courses to Class XII passouts and specialised vocational training to women to secure jobs or start their own businesses.Chief minister Rekha Gupta unveiled the plan Tuesday. “Providing better employment opportunities to Delhi’s youth and empowering women economically are the priorities of our govt. The proposed centre in Shalimar Bagh is an important step towards fulfilling this vision. By aligning training programmes with market demand and industry requirements, the centre will prepare young people for modern workplaces. Women will have opportunities to acquire skills according to their interests, abilities and family circumstances, as well as explore avenues to start their own businesses,” Gupta said.The facility, being developed by Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC), near Desu Colony, will also have a library, a 250-seat auditorium, hostel accommodation, sports facilities and two crèches with a capacity for 25 children in each.The courses for women will include fashion designing, tailoring, embroidery, beauty and wellness, baking, food processing and handicrafts. These skills will help them find employment or establish small businesses such as boutiques, beauty salons, bakeries and tiffin services.The centre will offer flexible timings, weekend batches and online and offline classes to enable women with domestic responsibilities to pursue such training. A women’s entrepreneurship and incubation facility will provide mentorship, guidance and market linkages to help trainees establish their ventures, besides facilitating access to financial assistance.The chief minister’s office said that for young people, the centre will offer employment-oriented technical courses on the lines of ITI programmes, covering digital services, IT support, artificial intelligence, retail and hospitality.The programmes will focus on practical training and follow standards under the National Skills Qualifications Framework and Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana.The academic and technical operations will be managed by the skill development centre of Dr BR Ambedkar University, under Delhi’s Directorate of Higher Education. Trainees will receive certificates on completing their courses, along with guidance for employment, apprenticeships and entrepreneurship.The campus will also have specialised laboratories for training in IT and digital technology, fashion and textiles, healthcare, beauty and wellness and food processing. The adjoining horticulture field will provide hands-on training in plant care, plant health and landscaping.A medical sick bay will be there on the premises. Govt plans to link the initiative with Skill India, Mission Shakti and the National Education Policy, 2020, while also creating opportunities for trainees to pursue higher education.

headline: Nine of 10 women feel unsafe in Delhi’s public parks after dark, finds study
content: New Delhi: Nearly nine out of 10 women, girls and LGBTQ+ persons surveyed in Delhi do not feel safe in their neighbourhood parks after dark, while an overwhelming majority feel unsafe walking to the nearest bus stop or metro station at night, a study by the Centre for Equity and Inclusion (CEQUIN) has found.Titled ‘Everyday Journeys: Women’s and Girls’ Access to Footpaths and Public Parks in Delhi’, the study highlights how poor infrastructure, harassment and a lack of institutional accountability continue to restrict women’s access to public spaces.The survey received 1,882 responses, of which 1,588 were considered valid. It covered women, girls and LGBTQ+ persons and was conducted between Oct 15 and Nov 2, 2026. The findings were supplemented by two focus group discussions, one involving nine college students and another with 11 women from neighbourhoods that included Jamia Nagar, Seelampur, Seemapuri and Tehkhand.According to the report, 88.9% of respondents do not feel safe in the nearest public park after dark.This figure remains high even during daytime, when 54% said they feel unsafe in parks.Among the 1,114 respondents who answered a question on commuting, 87.5% said they did not feel safe walking to the nearest bus stop or metro station after dark.The study identified both infrastructure gaps and men’s behaviour as major contributors to this fear. While 76.4% reported poorly lit footpaths, 60% said the footpaths leading to public transport points were either broken or missing.As many as 79.5% said men’s behaviour — staring, making comments, whistling and following them — made their daily commutes unsafe.A significant finding was the lack of awareness about civic accountability.While 52.3% did not know where to complain about problems with footpaths or parks, 80.5% could not identify even one authority responsible for maintaining them.The report also flagged the absence of women in public parks as a factor reinforcing the insecurity. As many as 42.7% of respondents who said they saw hardly any women in their parks in the evening also felt unsafe there after dark.“Safety is not only about headline crimes. It is shaped by the everyday breakdown of lighting, footpaths, neighbourhood parks and institutional accountability,” Lora K. Prabhu, co-founder and managing director of CEQUIN, said.The organisation is set to submit the study and its recommendations to the Supreme Court in the ongoing suo motu cognisance taken on Sept 28following rape incidents in Delhi-NCR.The submission seeks the court’s consideration of four priority measures -- better-lit and repaired footpaths, clear accountability for civic agencies, more women police personnel on evening patrols, and binding minimum safety standards for public parks.CEQUIN will release the report Wednesday, marking the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women and Girls, at its annual Hain Haq Hamara Hissedari event in Vasant Vihar.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
