headline: Delhi Pollution Control Committee asks dairy farms to apply for pollution clearances within 15 days
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) The Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) has directed all dairy farms and gaushalas operating in the national capital to apply for mandatory pollution clearances within 15 days, warning of action in case of non-compliance. In a public notice, the DPCC directed owners, operators and occupiers of dairy farms and gaushalas to obtain Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO) under the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981, as applicable to their activities. The directions have been issued in compliance with a May 20, 2020, order of the National Green Tribunal (NGT). Following the NGT order, the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) had issued guidelines for environmental management of dairy farms and gaushalas, covering issues such as solid and liquid waste management and regulatory compliance, the notice said. The DPCC said dairy farms and gaushalas were categorised into different pollution categories by the CPCB on July 10, 2020, under Section 18(1)(b) of the Water Act and the Air Act. According to the categorisation, gaushalas have been placed in the green category with a Pollution Index of 41.5.

headline: Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile thanks Indian govt for allotting Delhi bungalow to Dalai Lama
content: Dharamshala (Himchal Pradesh) [India], November 24 (ANI): Members of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile on Tuesday expressed gratitude to the Indian government for allotting a Type 7 bungalow in Lutyens' Delhi to the 14th Dalai Lama and his personal office, Gaden Phodrang, describing the move as a significant gesture of support towards the Tibetan spiritual leader and the Tibetan community.Speaker of the Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile Dolma Tsering welcomed the allotment, describing it as "very welcome news" and conveying gratitude to the Indian government on behalf of the Tibetan Parliament.She said the accommodation would make the Dalai Lama's visits to the national capital more convenient and provide greater comfort during his stay in Delhi.Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile member and Standing Committee member Choedak Gyatso also thanked the Indian government, recalling the support extended to Tibetans after they were forced to leave their homeland."The Government of India has given us refuge when we had no country. We lost our country and gave us Dharamshala when we had no land and gave us schools and many institutions that can preserve our culture," Gyatso said.Recalling his recent official visit to Delhi, during which he met Indian MPs, Gyatso said he had personally visited the bungalow along with the Tibetan Deputy Speaker and described the opportunity as a great honour.Welcoming the allotment, Gyatso highlighted the bungalow's location, saying it was situated just three kilometres from the centre of power in the national capital and that the development sent a strong message to everyone concerned about Tibet.He said the allotment reflected India's continued support for the Tibetan people and their cause, adding that the Tibetan community remained deeply grateful to the Government and people of India. He also appealed for continued support in the future.Both Tibetan Parliament-in-Exile members described the allotment as an important gesture towards the Dalai Lama and the Tibetan community, particularly in facilitating the spiritual leader's visits to the national capital.The Gaden Phodrang, also known as the Office of His Holiness the Dalai Lama (OHHDL), is the personal office of the Tibetan spiritual leader. It provides secretarial assistance and handles matters related to the Dalai Lama, acting on his behalf. (ANI)(This content is sourced from a syndicated feed and is published as received. The Tribune assumes no responsibility or liability for its accuracy, completeness, or content.)

headline: K-Food Universe 2026 concludes in Delhi, highlighting growing appetite for Korean cuisine and culture in India
content: VMPLNew Delhi [India], November 24: The 10-day K-Food Universe 2026, a festival celebrating Korean food, music, beauty and culture, ended in New Delhi after bringing together food lovers, K-culture fans, families and young consumers for a full experience of South Korea's culinary and cultural landscape. The festival was organized by Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corporation (aT) and South Korea's Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs and held at Pacific Mall, Tagore Garden from November 13 to 22.The festival aimed at taking Korean cuisine to Indian consumers beyond its growing popularity through films, K-dramas and music and brought together food experiences, retail opportunities, live performances and interactive cultural activities under one roof. It also pointed out the increasing opportunities in the Indian market for Korean food companies looking to expand their footprint abroad.Food was the main focus of the experience with visitors able to explore Korean street food, live cooking demonstrations and product sampling opportunities. There were demonstrations in the open kitchen by Delhi-based Korean restaurant Kori's and free street-food tastings three times a day. The K-Market had vendors such as SEELA, Khuben, ARIH, K-Friends and Nongshim India, offering visitors the opportunity to explore and buy different Korean food products.Among the key attractions was an interactive Korean ramen preparation experience, which allowed visitors to customise their noodles. Popular Korean favourites, including instant noodles, tteokbokki, seaweed, snacks, sauces and beverages, introduced audiences to the diversity of Korean cuisine. The JUMAK zone, inspired by traditional Korean roadside taverns, further showcased Korean food and beverage experiences, with participation from Delhi-based restaurant GOONG.Beyond food, the festival featured a K-Pop Cover Dance Championship, K-Food Mask Singer competition, traditional Korean games, Hanbok experiences, Taekwondo demonstrations and K-Beauty activities, including personal colour analysis and Korean-style makeup. Performances and cultural showcases, including appearances by K-Pop girl group DIVA-X, added to the festival's entertainment programme.Commenting on the growing opportunities for Korean food in India, Mr. Kyoung-yong Byun, Managing Director of the Bangkok Office, Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corporation (aT), said, "India is an important strategic market for Korean food products, supported by its population of approximately 1.4 billion, young consumer base, and strong economic growth potential. The growing popularity of Korean culture and the rapid expansion of online retail have increased awareness and consumption of Korean food, creating significant opportunities for further market growth."Highlighting the changing consumption trends, Mr. Byun added, "We are seeing growing demand for a wide range of Korean food products in India, including instant noodles, tteokbokki, seaweed, sauces, snacks, and beverages. Korean instant noodle exports to India reached USD 20.85 million as of September 2026, representing a 48.2% increase compared to the same period last year."He further stated that adapting products to local tastes, particularly through vegetarian and vegan options, familiar flavor profiles and convenient ready-to-cook formats, would be important for Korean companies entering the Indian market.The festival also highlighted the rising combination of Korean entertainment and food consumption in India. As K-Pop and Korean dramas become popular with younger audiences, the knowledge of the culture is increasingly leading to curiosity about Korean cuisine and food products.Through programs like K-Food Universe 2026, aT and the South Korean government hope to raise consumer awareness, ease market access and create opportunities for Korean food companies, including small and medium-sized enterprises, to access India's evolving food market.(ADVERTORIAL DISCLAIMER: The above press release has been provided by VMPL. ANI will not be responsible in any way for the content of the same.)

headline: Datanomics: 1 in 4 vehicles registered in Delhi since FY18 is below BS-VI
content: The Supreme Court on Monday mooted allowing only Bharat Stage VI (BS-VI) vehicles into the national capital to curb air pollution. The move comes as the Delhi government has already barred vehicles registered outside the city that do not meet BS-VI norms from November 1 to January 31, 2027. BS-VI, India’s strictest emission norm, came into force on April 1, 2020. Delhi’s registrations over the decade since financial year 2017-18 (FY18) show that 26 per cent, or 1 in 4 vehicles, are below the norm. Among its neighbouring districts, Ghaziabad and Noida have the highest share of BS-VI registrations. However, vehicles are only part of the story. Delhi’s own sources accounted for 33.06 per cent of its fine particulate matter (PM2.5) in the first week of November, with the rest coming from NCR districts and stubble burning. Transport made up 52 per cent of the local share.

headline: Delhi to set up skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh for youth, women
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) The Delhi government will set up a skill development centre in Shalimar Bagh with 14 advanced laboratories, smart classrooms and an entrepreneurship facility to provide job-oriented training to young people and women, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said on Tuesday. The centre, spread across around eight acres, will offer technical and IT-related courses for Class 12 pass-outs, while women will be trained in skills such as fashion designing, tailoring, baking, beauty and wellness, and food processing, according to a statement. Gupta said providing employment opportunities to young people and making women economically self-reliant were among the key priorities of her government. The proposed centre would offer training based on industry requirements and market demand. The facility will have smart classrooms, 14 laboratories, a library and learning resource centre, a 250-seat multipurpose auditorium, and facilities for conferences and placements. It will be developed by the Delhi Tourism and Transportation Development Corporation (DTTDC) near Desu Colony, it stated. A horticulture training field spread over around two acres will also be developed adjoining the campus to provide practical training in plant care, plant health and landscaping, the Statement stated. The centre will offer flexible schedules, weekend batches and online and offline training facilities to enable women, including those with domestic responsibilities, to pursue skill development courses.

headline: Delhi records ‘poor’ air quality for 10 days in a row
content: New Delhi, Nov 24 (PTI) Delhi’s air quality remained in the ‘poor’ category on Tuesday for the 10th consecutive day, and PM2.5 remained the dominant pollutant. Of the 58 monitoring stations that recorded data on Tuesday, air quality was in the ‘poor’ category at 34, ‘moderate’ at 19 and ‘very poor’ at five. The Cantonment area recorded the worst air quality, with an AQI of 346. It also recorded its highest reading since May 8, according to the Sameer app. The Cantonment monitoring station, which has often recorded among the lowest pollution levels in the city this month, had also registered a day in the ‘satisfactory’ category. It recorded more than 10 days with ‘moderate’ air quality during the month. According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between zero and 50 is considered ‘good’, 51 and 100 ‘satisfactory’, 101 and 200 ‘moderate’, 201 and 300 ‘poor’, 301 and 400 ‘very poor’, and 401 and 500 ‘severe’. The city’s AQI stood at 280 on November 19, before falling to 270 on November 20, 265 on November 21 and 239 on November 22. It rose to 260 on November 23 before settling at 227 on Tuesday.

headline: No relief for DU’s first 4-yr UG batch as HC refuses to intervene, directs UGC to decide
content: In a major setback for students, the Delhi High Court on November 20 refused to direct authorities to allot additional seats to accommodate Delhi University's first four-year undergraduate programme (FYUP) students in the varsity’s one-year master's course. The court held that offering such relief "would fall beyond the permissible scope of judicial intervention." Instead, the court directed the University Grants Commission (UGC) to consider the students' grievances and take a decision within three weeks. Justice Jasmeet Singh was hearing eight pleas involving scores of students who graduated from DU as the first batch under the Four-Year Undergraduate Programme (FYUP), introduced in 2022 under the National Education Policy (NEP). Many of them had opted for the four-year course with the belief they would be able to transition to a one-year master's programme instead of the traditional two-year postgraduate course. Also Read | Consider admitting students who graduated under 4-yr UG course in PG 2nd year: HC to Delhi University DU introduced a one-year master's programme in the academic year 2026-27, the first such course under the NEP framework, alongside its traditional two-year PG programme. The students, however, challenged the admission criteria for the one-year course. While the two-year PG course admits students based on their CUET PG scores, the one-year master's programme used the cumulative grade obtained in undergraduate studies as its criterion, along with a university-defined priority order. As a result, students with a multidisciplinary undergraduate degree and a higher CGPA were considered after Honours graduates with lower scores for a one-year PG seat. Before the Delhi HC, the students argued that the admission criteria for the one-year Master's were "discriminatory". Why can't HC direct DU to create additional seats? In his November 20 order, Justice Singh observed that the HC "finds merit in the grievance raised" by the students "to the extent that, while opting for and undertaking the four-year undergraduate programme under UGCF-2022, they were acting under a bona fide belief and legitimate expectation that successful completion of the programme would facilitate their progression to a One-Year master's programme". However, the court said it could not grant the relief the students sought. The students had asked the court to set aside the admission criteria and direct that they be accommodated in the one-year master's programme this year. The court held that granting such relief "would fall beyond the permissible scope of judicial intervention." Justice Singh reasoned, "The creation of additional seats would involve consideration of several academic and administrative factors, including the sanctioned intake, availability of faculty and infrastructure, and other institutional requirements like space, resources, etc.Additionally, this Court neither possesses the requisite academic expertise nor is it equipped to undertake an evaluation of the comparative curricula, academic rigour and credit requirements of the four-year multidisciplinary undergraduate programme with a Major subject vis-à-vis the four-year Honours programme." "Such matters are primarily within the domain of the academic and regulatory authorities, and this Court would be circumspect in substituting its own assessment for that of the competent academic bodies," the court observed. Why did the HC defer the issue to the UGC? Considering the peculiar circumstances the students find themselves in, "particularly the fact that they constitute the first batch to have undertaken the four-year undergraduate programme under UGCF-2022," the court instructed the UGC, the parent regulatory body, "to consider the grievance of the petitioners." The eight pleas now stand disposed of. Directing that the petitions be treated as representations before the UGC, the court outlined, "The UGC shall examine whether seats are available in the One-Year master's programmes in other universities and colleges and, wherever feasible, endeavour to accommodate the petitioners.The aforesaid exercise shall be undertaken expeditiously and, in any event, not later than three weeks from today." Thousands of DU students who graduated under the FYUP have been stuck in limbo, with an academic year lost owing to fewer seats in the one-year master's programme. The students had alleged that DU delayed information on the admission criteria for the one-year master's programme.

headline: Delhi High Court says pending cases under Juvenile Justice Act must go to Children’s Courts
content: The Delhi High Court has ruled that all cases involving offences under the Juvenile Justice Act must be tried by Children’s Courts, even if the trials had already begun before magistrate court when the law was amended in 2022. A Bench of Justice Navin Chawla and Justice Arun Bhardwaj passed the ruling on November 23 while answering two legal questions referred to it by an Additional Sessions Judge at Saket Courts. The questions arose after the Parliament amended Section 86 of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, with effect from September 1, 2022. Before the amendment, cases under the Act were tried by different courts depending on the punishment prescribed for the offence. More serious offences were tried by Children’s Courts, while others could be heard by magistrates. The High Court was asked whether Section 86(4) of the JJ Act (which mandates that all offences under the Act be tried by a Children’s Court) be read with retrospective effect or with prospective effect. Answering in the affirmative, the Bench, “In our opinion, the answer to the above question of law raised by the Additional Sessions Judge lies in a well-accepted principle of interpretation of statutes, which is, that a change in the forum of a trial is a procedural matter and, therefore, a statute which brings about a change in the same is presumed to be retrospective in the absence of a contrary intention”. The second question concerned whether an ordinary criminal offence becomes an offence against children simply because one of the victims is a minor. However, the Bench clarified that every criminal case where one of the victims is a minor does not have to be transferred to a Children’s Court. “It is only for offences under the JJ Act, 2015, that the trial would now be conducted only by the Children’s Court. For general offences, even though one of the victims is a minor, there is no mandate in Section 86(4) of the JJ Act, 2015, to transfer such trials to the Children’s Court,” the court said. The court also examined whether shifting pending cases to Children’s Courts would affect the right of the accused and the State to appeal against the trial court’s decision. “It is again only the forum that changes and, instead of the appeal lying before the Court of Sessions, it would now lie before the High Court,” the court said. The court, additionally, noted that the view taken by it was in tune with the one canvassed by the counsels for the Centre and the Delhi government.

headline: Delhi Development Authority opens 17 parks, 8 amphitheatres for events; schools can book for Rs 1
content: NEW DELHI: To make its parks more accessible for organised public activities, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) has introduced a comprehensive booking policy, allowing citizens, institutions and community organisations to host cultural, educational, recreational and wellness events in designated green spaces across the city.The policy provides for a single-window online booking system, rationalised charges and special concessions, including bookings for schools at just Rs 1.Officials said the initiative follows several meetings chaired by Lieutenant Governor TS Sandhu, who directed the authority to rationalise and upgrade services offered at DDA parks, particularly during the ongoing festive season. Under the new policy, 17 identified park locations and designated facilities, including amphitheatres, will be opened for regulated bookings.eight amphitheaters will be part of the booking venues also.The proposed centralised booking portal, linked to the DDA website, will allow applicants to check available parks, designated spaces, capacities and applicable charges before submitting applications and making payments online. " The digital system is intended to streamline scrutiny, approvals and other booking-related processes while ensuring greater transparency and accountability," said officials.A key feature is the special provision for schools, which can book designated park spaces for Re 1 for educational and recreational activities such as picnics, painting, photography, debates and competitions. "Schools booking parks for other purposes will also get a 50% concession on applicable charges. The move is aimed at encouraging outdoor learning and giving students an opportunity to engage with nature beyond classrooms," stated the authority.The policy classifies open park spaces under Category A, depending on the expected gathering. Category A1 covers small gatherings of up to 200 people, A2 caters to gatherings of more than 200 and up to 500 people, while A3 is for events with more than 500 participants.Permitted activities include yoga, meditation, fitness programmes, nature and heritage walks, poetry readings, book launches, literary festivals, workshops, art and craft exhibitions, theatre, cultural performances, book fairs, craft bazaars and food festivals, subject to approval of the proposed event plan. Officials claim that scope of activities allowed at parks also been widen.The 17 identified locations include Swarna Jayanti Park and Chitragupta Park in Rohini, District Park in Paschim Vihar, Sandesh Vihar and Lake Park in Pitampura, District Parks in Dwarka, Indraprastha Park, Sanjay Lake, Asita-Yamuna River Front, Coronation Park, Astha Kunj, Hauz Khas Park, Baansera and Mehrauli Archaeological Park, among others.Designated amphitheatres at Indraprastha Park, Astha Kunj, Utsav Ground, Vasant Udyan, Tughlaqabad Recreational Park, Sanjay Lake and Coronation Park will also be available for half-day and full-day bookings, including ticketed and non-ticketed events.Recognised higher educational institutions, government departments, PSUs and autonomous bodies will be eligible for a 50% concession on booking charges. Applications will ordinarily have to be submitted at least five working days before the proposed event.The policy also lays down safeguards to protect the ecological character of parks and activities at sensitive locations such will be regulated.Organisers will be responsible for crowd management, safety, waste segregation, cleaning and restoration of the allotted area. headline: Chennai Regional Passport Office notice led to CJP’s Saurav Das being stopped at Delhi airport
content: New Delhi Saurav Das, co-convenor of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), was stopped from boarding a flight to London at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport (IGI) on Monday night (November 23, 2026) after failing to respond to a show-cause notice issued by the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, over alleged discrepancies between his passport and other identity documents, a senior government official told The Hindu. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/cockroach-janta-party/ CJP’s Saurav Das claims he was stopped at Delhi airport from travelling to U.K. storyline 1 His passport was issued in 2019 and the notice was served at 7.30 p.m. by email on November 23, hours before he was to board the flight at 1 a.m. on November 24. The government has issued no official statement on the reasons for stopping him at the airport. According to the notice, the RPO, Chennai, said that it has received inputs about Mr. Das’ passport application dated August 8, 2019, stating that “particulars (place of birth) furnished in it are incorrect” and his passport dated August 21, 2019 was “obtained by material suppression of facts.” CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government Addressing a protest named ‘Jantar Mantar @ Kochi’ demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), Abhijeet Dipke stresses that “Modi will go out in 2029.” CJP founder launches scathing attack on Central government storyline 1 “You are hereby called upon to provide a suitable clarification with respect to your place of birth along with supporting documents within seven days. Failure to produce a satisfactory response or a lack of response may result in impounding of your passport under Section 10(3)(b) of the Passports Act, 1967. You are advised not to use this passport till submission of response,” the notice seen by The Hindu said. Mr. Das said he saw the email with a show-cause notice about “discrepancies” in his passport only after he was stopped at the immigration counter at the Delhi airport. “I have no issue in providing any explanation. But I only received a show-cause notice five hours prior to my flight scheduled at 1 a.m. I did not see it before I was stopped at the airport. It says they have received an input over mismatch in my data. Can a citizen be stopped from travelling on such an input without disclosing any details of it?” He questioned why no issue was flagged in the verification process when an Indian passport was issued to him in 2019. “I have travelled abroad twice since without being stopped. The issue is being raised this time because I am associated with the CJP movement. My place of birth, my parents are being dragged into this. But we are not scared of cheap tactics.” CJP launches Cockroach Club to shift ‘youth movement beyond street protests’ CJP launches Cockroach Club to shift ‘youth movement beyond street protests’ Launched in Pune with over 300 participants, the initiative will combine political debates, lectures, film screenings, comedy and cultural performances as the party seeks to channelise youth energy into shaping India’s future CJP launches Cockroach Club to shift ‘youth movement beyond street protests’ storyline 1 The notice followed a September 30 order by the Madras High Court, which acted on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition seeking a probe by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) into the nationality of Mr. Das and sought to cancel his passport and Aadhaar card if he is not found to be an Indian. The First Division Bench of Chief Justice Sushrut Arvind Dharmadhikari and Justice G. Arul Murugan also ordered notice to Mr. Das on the PIL petition filed by R. Ganesh Kumar, a businessman from Chennai. Plea in Madras High Court seeks probe into nationality of Cockroach Janata Party co-convenor Saurav Das storyline 1 The official said that Mr. Das was asked to explain why his passport should not be impounded, as there is a mismatch in documents submitted to obtain his passport and Aadhaar. “There appears to be a mismatch regarding his date of birth, place of birth and name of father in various documents — Aadhaar, birth certificate and passport. He was asked by the RPO, Chennai to explain his stance but he did not, following which his passport was flagged and he was stopped by the immigration,” said the official. Addressing a press conference in Delhi, Mr. Das said, “Let alone being stopped from going abroad, we have not been allowed to speak inside the country. We were stopped from going to Jantar Mantar and then Ramlila Maidan. When we took to online spaces, attempts to stop were made even there.” He further said that Meta has taken down 60 lakh posts in the past few months, alleging “massive censorship” by the Indian Government. “They [government] tried to stop us by putting us in Tihar Jail for unfurling National Flag and by detaining the youth protestors. Now their excuse was some “discrepancy” in the passport,” Mr. Das said. “They are unable to find anything against Cockroach leaders or our supporters to put agencies like CBI, ED behind us or frame charges under UAPA so they are resorting to these cheap tactics,” he added. Mr. Das said he was scheduled to speak at Oxford Union, and attend multiple events organised by the students’ union at the London School of Economics, Cambridge University, Edinburgh University, and Queen Mary University, among others. “They [the government] have shown themselves as scared people. They are facing anxieties because of this movement. If I were Vijay Mallya, Nirav Modi, or Mehul Choksi, this government would have rolled out the red carpet and offered me VIP security. In that case, I would have taken off for London in three to four hours,” he said. Earlier on Monday night, he posted on X, “This coward government did not allow me to board my flight to London where I was invited by prestigious universities such as Oxford, Cambridge, LSE, Edinburgh to deliver talks on the cockroach movement. Indian students put their heart and soul to organise the events but this anti-intellectual govt was scared of me going to these prestigious institutions!”

headline: Delhi-NCR's toxic air may be doing more than triggering coughs and breathing trouble; years of exposure t
content: Every winter, Delhi-NCR residents brace for hazy skies, burning eyes, sore throats and persistent coughing. These symptoms often improve when the weather changes or pollution levels drop. But the health impact of polluted air may not end with the season.The bigger concern is what happens when the lungs breathe polluted air year after year. Research has linked long-term exposure to air pollution with lung cancer, including among people who have never smoked. This makes pollution more than a seasonal inconvenience. It is a long-term health concern that deserves attention.How polluted air can damage the lungs over timeDelhi-NCR's pollution comes from several sources, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, construction dust, waste burning and seasonal weather conditions that trap pollutants closer to the ground.Among these pollutants, PM2.5 deserves particular attention. These particles are so tiny that they can travel deep into the lungs. Repeated exposure can trigger inflammation, oxidative stress and cellular damage. Over time, this damage may affect how healthy cells function and potentially contribute to cancer development.Dr Kundan, Consultant Oncology, Manipal Hospital, Ghaziabad, explained that prolonged exposure to these particles can cause changes in lung cells that may eventually contribute to lung cancer, including in non-smokers.Is air pollution a proven cancer risk?Yes. The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), which is part of the World Health Organization, classified outdoor air pollution and particulate matter as Group 1 carcinogens in 2013. This means scientific evidence is sufficient to establish that they can cause cancer in humans.The strongest evidence is for lung cancer. Researchers have also observed a link with bladder cancer, although the evidence is less conclusive. This does not mean pollution causes every cancer or that every person exposed will develop the disease.Why non-smokers are also at riskSmoking remains one of the biggest risk factors for lung cancer. However, never having smoked does not eliminate the risk.Dr Jyoti Wadhwa, Principal Lead, Medical & Precision Oncology, Apollo Athenaa Women’s Cancer Centre, explained, “When we talk about air pollution and cancer, it is important to look beyond the immediate symptoms. A cough or breathing difficulty may be felt within days, but the concern around cancer is linked more closely with repeated exposure over a much longer period.”Age, genetics, tobacco exposure, lifestyle and the duration of exposure can all influence an individual's cancer risk. Pollution is one part of a larger picture, but it is a risk factor that cannot always be avoided.Symptoms that should not be ignoredA cough during a pollution-heavy winter does not automatically mean cancer. Throat irritation, congestion and breathlessness can also result from short-term exposure.However, a persistent cough, coughing up blood, unexplained weight loss, chest pain or continuing breathlessness need medical evaluation. These symptoms should not be dismissed as another consequence of Delhi's winter pollution.Can people reduce their exposure?While pollution cannot be controlled by individual choices alone, some precautions can help reduce exposure.Wear a well-fitted N95 mask when outdoor air quality is poor.Check AQI before planning outdoor exercise.Use a suitable indoor air purifier, especially in frequently occupied rooms.Avoid exercising near busy roads during high-pollution periods.Long-term protection, however, depends on cleaner transport, stricter emission controls, better waste management and reduced industrial pollution.The concern is not just one polluted winterCancer risk is rarely shaped by one day of exposure. It is the cumulative effect of several factors over time. Delhi-NCR's pollution may worsen during winter, but exposure continues throughout the year.The real concern is not simply waking up to a poor AQI. It is spending years breathing air that repeatedly exposes the lungs to harmful substances. Cleaner air is not just about breathing comfortably today. It is also about protecting health in the years ahead.

headline: 50 points for distance, 62 banned rules: How Delhi’s private schools are grading nursery admissions
content: Entry-level admissions for the next academic session in Delhi's private schools are set to begin, with some schools announcing their admission criteria, giving weightage to neighbourhood proximity, siblings of existing students and alumni parents, among other categories. The application process will cover nursery, kindergarten and Class 1 in private unaided recognised schools, with parents required to check the points allotted to different categories before applying. Also Read | Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28 schedule out, schools upload intake-criteria at edudel.nic.in Sudha Acharya, principal of ITL International School in Dwarka, said the school has to consider distance from the school, siblings of existing students, alumni parents and children of staff members under its admission criteria. Mallika Preman of Tagore International School in East of Kailash said the school has given distance, siblings of existing students, alumni parents and first-born children weightage under its admission criteria. Similarly, Vasant Valley School has allotted points to applicants living within a 10 to 15 km radius of the school, and to applicants whose father or mother is an alumnus. Siblings of existing students will also be considered under its admission criteria. Delhi Public School, RK Puram, has allotted 50 points to applicants residing within 6 km of the school, 40 points to those living beyond 6 km and up to 8 km, 30 points to those residing beyond 8 km and up to 15 km, and 20 points to applicants living beyond 15 km. The distance will be calculated on the basis of an aerial map and not road distance, according to the school's criteria. The school has allotted 26 points to applicants whose brother or sister is currently studying at DPS RK Puram, DPS Vasant Vihar or DPS East of Kailash. It has also allotted 12 points each to fathers and mothers who are alumni of DPS RK Puram, with Class 10 or 12 certificates required as proof. Shalimar Public School in Mahipalpur has allotted points to applicants residing within 1-3 km. The school has also included single-girl-child applicants in its admission criteria. The Directorate of Education, in its 59-page circular, has listed around 62 prohibited admission criteria, including parents' educational qualifications, interview-based assessments, management quota, gender and Delhi domicile by birth. Schools have been directed to upload their admission criteria and detailed point-wise break-up on their respective websites. The department has also prescribed age limits in accordance with the National Education Policy 2020. Children applying for nursery must be aged 3-4 years, kindergarten applicants four to five years and Class 1 applicants five to six years as on March 31, 2027. Registration for admission to nursery, lower KG, upper KG and class 1 in private schools in Delhi for the next academic session will begin on December 1, with December 28 set as the last date for submitting applications, according to a Directorate of Education circular. The first list of selected children, including the waiting list, will be published on January 20, followed by a second list on February 5. The admission process will conclude on March 12, the circular said. Schools have been directed to upload their admission criteria and the corresponding points on the Directorate's portal by November 26. They will also have to display the criteria and points on their respective websites.

headline: Sheikh Hasina seeks to return to Bangladesh on Victory Day, asks for Biman flight from Delhi
content: Sheikh Hasina, who was ousted as Bangladesh's Prime Minister in August 2024 and has been living in India since then, plans to return home on 16 December, her spokesperson told Reuters on Tuesday.The announcement marks the first time Hasina has publicly set a date for her return. The date coincides with Bangladesh's Victory Day, which commemorates the country's independence following the 1971 war with Pakistan. Hasina's planned return could heighten political and legal tensions in Bangladesh. Her party, the Awami League, remains banned, and unrest has intensified since she sought a new passport and other documents earlier this month.Hasina fled to India on 5 August 2024 after a student-led mass uprising brought an end to her 15-year rule.Sheikh Hasina seeks state aircraftHasina has urged the Bangladeshi government to arrange her return on the national flag carrier, Biman Bangladesh Airlines."Since Sheikh Hasina was flown to India on a Bangladesh aircraft on August 5th, 2024, she now calls upon the government to arrange for her air transport from Delhi back to Dhaka," the spokesperson, Syed Mozammel Ali, told Reuters."Having exiled her contrary to the Constitution under such circumstances, it is now the responsibility of the government to make possible her return to Bangladesh on Victory Day on December 16th," he reportedly added.Hasina has also sought a new passport and identity card ahead of a planned return in December, which the government had previously rejected.A Bangladeshi government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Sheikh Hasina will be 'arrested' as soon as she enters BangladeshHasina faces a death sentence in Bangladesh, and her Awami League party is banned following the 2024 uprising that ended her long rule.A Bangladeshi minister told Reuters on Sunday that Hasina would be arrested and jailed on return, and that there had been no official discussions with India about sending an aircraft to bring her back."As soon as she tries to enter Bangladesh, she will be arrested. And she will be taken to jail, and the law will take its course," Shama Obaed Islam, State Minister for Foreign Affairs, said in an interview on Sunday.While Hasina plans to return to Bangladesh in December, Dhaka is seeking her extradition from India, where she has lived since fleeing Bangladesh in 2024. The country expects New Delhi to comply with an existing extradition treaty, Obaed told Reuters."We would like India to honour the extradition treaty and return her as a convict, and the law will take its course. She will have to face the music," he was quoted as saying.India's Ministry of External Affairs did not immediately respond to Reuters' request for comment. In April, the ministry said it was examining Bangladesh's request to extradite Hasina.The United Nations said as many as 1,400 people were killed during the unrest that forced her out of power. Bangladesh's war crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile.Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity involving the uprising in which hundreds of protesters were killed. Hasina rejected the verdict and has said she is ready to fight the case once she is back.

headline: Delhi HC upholds 85-year-old man's right to live with dignity, says he need not prove harassment to evict
content: NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court has ruled that a senior citizen seeking eviction of his children from his self-acquired property does not necessarily have to prove harassment or ill-treatment. It observed that demonstrating the need to protect the property to ensure a peaceful and dignified life is sufficient.Justice Amit Mahajan set aside orders passed by the District Magistrate and the Divisional Commissioner, which had rejected an 85-year-old man's plea seeking eviction of his eldest son and daughter-in-law from his house in south Delhi's Masjid Moth.The court directed the couple to vacate the property within four weeks. It also directed the concerned Station House Officer (SHO) to provide all necessary assistance to the senior citizen to ensure compliance with the order, if required.“Further, a senior citizen cannot be compelled to share his own house with his children against his wishes, more so when the relationship between the parties has deteriorated to such an extent that the petitioner has been constrained to litigate against Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 since the year 2022 and to seek police assistance under the orders of this Court. At the age of 85 years, the petitioner is entitled to live in his own house peacefully and with dignity,” the court observed.The court noted that the petitioner was the absolute owner of the property, while his son and daughter-in-law had not claimed any ownership rights over it. Their occupation of the house was solely on account of their relationship with him.It held that the authorities had wrongly proceeded on the assumption that the senior citizen had to establish harassment through clear and cogent evidence before an eviction order could be passed.“No such requirement is contemplated under the Act or the 2009 Rules. By insisting on the same, the learned authorities below have imposed a condition which the statute does not contemplate, and have thereby committed an error of law,” Justice Mahajan held.The court further pointed out that harassment of senior citizens by their children often takes place within the confines of a house, making it difficult to establish through independent evidence.It said proceedings under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007, are summary in nature and authorities cannot insist on the standard of proof applicable in civil or criminal trials.The court also considered the multiple police complaints filed by the petitioner since 2022 and its earlier directions asking the police to provide him all possible assistance in addressing any threat allegedly posed by his son and daughter-in-law.It added that a business dispute between the petitioner's sons could not, by itself, be treated as a reason to doubt the senior citizen's grievance or deny him protection under the Act.The High Court also questioned the findings in the enquiry reports submitted by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM).It noted that the first report, dated February 25, 2023, merely stated that it could not be ascertained whether the senior citizen's complaint of harassment was genuine. The court said the report was inconclusive and could not have been treated as proof that the allegations were false.On the second enquiry report, dated September 17, 2025, the court observed that although the SDM had recorded the submissions of both parties, details of the house visit and the material produced by them, it did not analyse the evidence or specify what had been observed during the visit.“It proceeds to conclude, in a single line, that the allegation of harassment is not established, as no clear evidence of harassment has been observed. A conclusion bereft of reasons cannot be termed a finding,” the court observed.The High Court relied on the Supreme Court's August 2026 judgment in Ravi Kant Gupta v. State of Uttar Pradesh, which held that a Maintenance Tribunal has the power to order the eviction of children from a senior citizen's property when such a step is necessary and expedient for the person's maintenance and protection.It also referred to the Delhi High Court's judgment in Pritam Singh v. Government of NCT of Delhi, which held that a senior citizen seeking eviction only needs to demonstrate that the property requires protection and is not necessarily required to establish ill-treatment by his son or another legal heir.The petitioner had acquired the property from the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) in 1980 and converted it into freehold in 2000. He approached the authorities in 2022, seeking the eviction of his eldest son and daughter-in-law under the Senior Citizens Act.He alleged that despite being asked to arrange alternative accommodation, the couple refused to vacate the house and their behaviour towards him had deteriorated over the years.The District Magistrate rejected his plea in August 2023, observing that the allegations of harassment had not been established and that the dispute appeared to stem from a business disagreement between his sons.After the matter was remanded for fresh consideration, the District Magistrate dismissed the petition again in October 2025. The Divisional Commissioner upheld the decision on April 28, 2026, following which the senior citizen approached the High Court.The petitioner was represented by Senior Advocate Madhav Khurana, along with advocates Riya Arora, Ayush Kumar, Ananya Saxena, Garima Rai Singhania, Shashank Dewan, Uttam Kumar and Hardik Arora.Senior Advocate Anurag Ahluwalia appeared for the son, while Nitika Bhutani, Panel Counsel, represented the Delhi government. Puja S. Kalra, Central Government Standing Counsel, appeared for the Union of India.Allowing the petition, the High Court set aside the District Magistrate's October 28, 2025, order and the Divisional Commissioner's April 28, 2026, order, directing the son and daughter-in-law to vacate the property within four weeks.(With Agency Inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28 schedule out, schools upload intake-criteria at edudel.nic.in
content: Private schools in Delhi will start uploading their admission criteria and the points assigned to each criterion for entry-level classes from this week, on the official website, edudel.nic.in. The Directorate of Education (DoE) Delhi, earlier announced the admission schedule for entry-level classes in private unaided recognised schools. The application process will begin on December 1, and parents will have until December 28 to register and submit forms. This year’s admission cycle will also see the introduction of two additional pre-primary entry classes, lower kindergarten (LKG) and upper kindergarten (UKG), as Delhi moves towards a three-year foundational stage in line with the NEP 2020. The revised structure will operate alongside Nursery admissions, with different age requirements and admission provisions for each class. Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28: Important dates Admission event Date Uploading of admission criteria and points begins November 23, 2026 Admission process and availability of forms begins December 1, 2026 Last date to submit application forms December 28, 2026 Schools upload applicant details and points awarded January 4, 2027 Parents can raise queries or objections regarding points January 5 to 11, 2027 Display of final points after resolving objections January 12, 2027 First list of selected children, including waiting list January 20, 2027 Queries regarding the first selection list January 21 to 28, 2027 Second selection list, if applicable February 5, 2027 Queries regarding the second selection list February 6 to 12, 2027 Subsequent admission list, if required February 22, 2027 Closure of admission process March 12, 2027 Note that the above schedule applies only to open seats in private unaided recognised schools; admissions for EWS, DG, and CWSN others will be held separately. Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28: Age criteria explained One of the key aspects of this year's admission process is the phased implementation of the revised foundational-stage structure. The age requirements will be calculated as on March 31, 2027. Under the revised structure, the three pre-primary stages will be Nursery (Balvatika 1), Lower KG (Balvatika 2) and Upper KG (Balvatika 3), followed by Class 1. The age requirements for the 2027-28 session are: Class Minimum and maximum age as on March 31, 2027 Nursery (Balvatika 1 / Pre-School 1) 3+ years and up to 4 years (New Admissions) Lower KG (Balvatika 2 / Pre-School 2) 4+ years and up to 5 years Upper KG (Balvatika 3 / Pre-School 3) 5+ years and up to 6 years Class 1 5+ years and up to 6 years for students moving from KG under the existing structure For Nursery admission, a child must have completed three years of age by March 31, 2027. The age criteria will also apply to fresh admissions in the newly introduced Lower KG and Upper KG classes, where applicable. The Directorate has clarified that children enrolled in Nursery during the 2026-27 academic session will move to Lower KG in 2027-28. At the same time, schools can admit new students directly to Lower KG, provided they have completed four years of age by March 31, 2027. Similarly, Upper KG will be introduced as a new entry-level class in the 2027-28 session. Fresh admissions will be allowed for children who have completed five years of age by March 31, 2027. Students who were enrolled in KG during the last cycle will move to Class 1 in 2027-28 under the earlier structure. The transition is therefore being implemented in phases rather than requiring all existing students to move through the new three-year pre-primary structure at once. Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28: Where and how to check admission criteria? Parents will be able to check the criteria under the 'admission criteria (2027-28)' section in the 'What's New' section of the official DoE website. If schools don't upload their admission rules on time, their admissions might be put on hold, the DoE said in its notice. The Directorate has also reiterated that schools cannot use criteria previously prohibited by it and upheld by the Delhi High Court. These include parameters such as parents' educational qualifications, whether both parents are working, the child's first-born status, proficiency in music or sports, and other arbitrary or discriminatory considerations. Schools must also publish the criterion-wise break-up of points awarded to applicants. After applications close, schools will publish the names of applicants and the points awarded to each child on January 4. Parents will have seven days, from January 5 to 11, to raise queries or objections if they believe the points have been incorrectly assigned. Schools will have to respond to these queries and publish the final points on January 12. If two or more applicants secure identical points for the last available seats, schools will have to conduct a draw of lots. The process must be transparent and held in the presence of parents and the designated Education Department nominee. Schools must inform eligible parents at least five days before the draw, conduct the process under videography and retain the recording. Delhi Nursery Admissions 2027-28: Important documents required For admission-related verification, the Directorate has listed the following documents as valid proof of residence of the child or parents: -Ration card or smart card issued in the name of either parent, carrying the child's name. -Domicile certificate of the child or either parent. -Voter identity card (EPIC) of either parent. -Electricity, MTNL telephone or water bill in the name of either parent or the child. -Passport in the name of either parent or the child. -Aadhaar card or UID card issued in the name of either parent. Parents should check the individual school's admission instructions for any additional documents required during verification. The overall admission process for the 2027-28 academic session will conclude on March 12, 2027. The Directorate has also directed schools to publish the details of selected candidates and waiting lists, along with the points awarded, to ensure transparency in the admission process.

headline: Delhi government plans 8km elevated corridor with four flyovers on Mehrauli-Badarpur Road to tackle south Delhi congestion
content: The Delhi government is planning an 8 km elevated corridor comprising four flyovers along Mehrauli-Badarpur Road to address persistent traffic congestion in south Delhi. The Public Works Department has secured approval for two projects, for which the government sanctioned Rs 1,471.14 crore in March this year, whilst consultants have been appointed to study the remaining two stretches. The first stretch, measuring 2.41 km between Saket G and Sangam Vihar, has crossed the halfway mark in construction. The project, being executed by the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation, involves an integrated flyover built above an underground metro corridor. Work has also started on the 2.56 km section connecting Maa Anandmayee Marg with Pul Prahladpur, for which funds have been sanctioned. The remaining two sections include a 2.72 km flyover between Sangam Vihar and Maa Anandmayee Marg and a 450-metre flyover between Pul Prahladpur and Badarpur. Consultants have been appointed to examine these sections, and the required studies are currently in progress. Officials said the proposed corridor is expected to improve connectivity between Saket, Ambedkar Nagar, Khanpur, Sangam Vihar and Pul Prahladpur by reducing travel time and easing traffic movement. The PWD has approached the Delhi Development Authority seeking the transfer of land required for construction. headline: Nitin Nabin deepfake video: Case transferred to Delhi Police special cell's IFSO unit | India News
content: A day after the BJP Delhi filed a complaint alleging that the party's National President Nitin Nabin's speech was distorted using artificial intelligence (AI) and deepfakes, the Delhi Police said the case has been transferred to the Special Cell's Intelligence Fusion and Strategic Operations (IFSO) unit.On Monday, a complaint was filed with the central district in Delhi against unknown persons for AI-editing and using deepfakes to change the speech, and against a few social media handles for running the edited speech.A senior police officer on Tuesday said the complaint has been transferred to the IFSO unit, which has specialised teams dealing with deepfake cases.According to the BJP, Nitin Nabin addressed a public rally in Chandigarh on Sunday."The actual video recording of this address was tampered with, and a misleading and completely fabricated video was created using AI and Deepfake technology. The edited video shows extremely sensitive national issues such as India-China relations, Pakistan, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit, and India’s indigenous fighter aircraft Tejas MK-1," said a BJP spokesperson.In the viral 37-second footage, Nabin appears to say that China is pressuring India to invite Pakistan to the SCO summit in exchange for an agreement to reclaim 200 sq km of Indian territory occupied by China. The BJP national president also remarks in the video that although the Tejas aircraft lack engines, the airframes have been built, adding that the US would supply the engines whenever it chooses.However, in the original video, Nabin discusses the SIR of electoral rolls and other issues.The party also demanded an immediate FIR to identify the social media accounts involved and to take action against the accused.The senior officer added that the IFSO unit will probe the matter and notices have already been sent to Meta and X to remove all the fake videos. “We have noted names of social media handles and will soon identify the accused,” he added.

headline: An open jail, family detention centre: Delhi planning first detention centre for female foreign nationals | India News
content: Delhi will set up the national capital's first detention centre for female foreign nationals in Narela's Lampur near the Delhi-Haryana border, with a family detention centre and an open jail being planned, officials said.Lampur Detention Centre, which currently houses male foreign nationals held under immigration and other laws, is set to expand to accommodate female foreign nationals. According to officials, the Delhi government and the prisons department are working on a broader plan to address the growing number of foreign nationals awaiting deportation.Two jail officials told HT that the plan also includes setting up a family detention centre and an open jail in Narela. Security staff at the Lampur detention centre and Tihar jail have prepared expansion plans and shared them with the social welfare department, the home department, and the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), which is responsible for the security of the premises.The Lampur detentionThe Lampur detention centre is one of the oldest detention centres in Delhi, as its 50-year-old building is located in the Sewa Sadan complex in Lampur Village in northwest Delhi’s Narela area. The centre is managed by the Delhi government, the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), and the CRPF to hold foreign nationals awaiting deportation for visa violations or after completing prison sentences. Undocumented migrants, asylum seekers, and refugees are all placed at the 18.5-acre facility. As per jail officials, there are more than 280 male detainees at the centre.At present, the female foreign nationals, who have to be detained, are put at different community halls, homeless shelters and other temporary facilities. Officials said there is also Nirmal Chhaya, but it can only house 30 occupants.“Since repairs and major renovation works are also pending at Lampur, we have decided to also place the female detention centre there. That way, both the male and female detainees will be placed at one place. We have more than 70-80 female detainees at times and need a bigger space to accommodate them. We are now planning to expand the Lampur centre with multiple storeys and the adjacent property to be used for Delhi Prisons,” a senior jail officer from Tihar headquarters told HT.Most of the detainees at Lampur and other centres are Bangladeshis, followed by Nigerians and a few Pakistani nationals.Since 2025, the Delhi government has announced plans to renovate Lampur centre due to multiple complaints from inmates (in courts) and the NHRC alleging poor medical facilities, unhygienic conditions and overcrowding.Another jail officer said they are also planning to use the adjacent property to build an open jail in Delhi or a family detention centre.The Delhi government on Monday said they have already approached the Delhi Development Authority (DDA) to allocate an additional 27 acres of land in Narela for the new prison adjacent to the upcoming high-security jail, as part of a broader plan to decongest the overcrowded Tihar Jail complex, officials said.The government had earlier proposed a multi-storeyed prison at Narela but later dropped the plan. An official said a jail cannot be multi-storeyed as it could pose a security risk.

headline: Representative excluded from Delhi Medical Council, medical association seeks LG’s intervention | Latest News Delhi
content: The Delhi Medical Association (DMA) has written to Delhi lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu objecting to the non-inclusion of its elected representative in the newly constituted Delhi Medical Council (DMC).The reconstituted DMC was notified on November 18 with 24 members, including four nominated by the Delhi government, 10 representatives from medical colleges and institutions, eight elected members and two ex-officio members.In its letter to the LG, seen by HT, the DMC said, that the DMA had received a notification directing it to conduct the election for “one post to the DMC within one month and submit the result to the DMC”.Despite having completed the process, “It is surprising to note that the representation of the DMA has been omitted from the said notification.”The DMA also said it had not received any prior communication seeking clarification about the election or the omission. Its members felt “let down” by the absence of their elected representative, Dr Girish Tyagi, the letter said, seeking the LG’s intervention “on priority”.The DMA’s letter was also sent to the chief minister, health minister, chief secretary and principal secretary (health), according to the letter.The LG, health department, and the CM’s office did not respond queries send by HT.The DMC is the statutory regulator responsible for registration of medical practitioners and matters relating to professional conduct and ethics in Delhi. It also examines complaints of medical negligence and professional misconduct. It was dissolved in June 2025 amid allegations of financial irregularities.

headline: How a Delhi gang was minting fake coins worth ₹40 crore over 10 years | Latest News Delhi
content: A decade-long operation involving a former goldsmith, heavy machinery, specialised dies and makeshift factories spread across more than five states helped a gang manufacture counterfeit ₹20 coins with a face value of over ₹40 crore, Delhi Police said. The gang used scrap aluminium, nickel and copper, along with traditional coin-stamping techniques to produce thousands of fake coins every day, investigators found.Also Read | ₹20 coin racket busted, 4 held; coins worth ₹1 lakh seized">Delhi: Counterfeit ₹20 coin racket busted, 4 held; coins worth ₹1 lakh seizedHow a tip-off led police to the counterfeit coin networkThe counterfeit coin manufacturing racket, busted in a joint operation by the Delhi and Uttar Pradesh police in September, had been operating for more than 10 years, shifting its factories between cities to evade detection. Investigators have recovered more than 40 specialised dies, along with coin-polishing and other machines, from the accused.What began as a tip-off in early September about a man carrying more than four dozen packets of fake coins near Mundka Industrial Metro Station led the Delhi Police to a large-scale manufacturing and distribution network spread across Delhi and Sonipat. On September 9, the first accused, Paras Jain, 45, allegedly led police to counterfeit ₹20 coins with a face value of ₹1 lakh. The coins were recovered from a Toyota Etios car.Delhi Police’s Crime Branch said Jain subsequently revealed that he worked with Upkar Luthra, 58, who had been manufacturing counterfeit coins for more than a decade and had been named as an accused in six cases, including four related to counterfeit coins and others related to theft and Arms Act.By September 13, the UP Police, which was also tracking the gang, arrested Luthra and his three associates – Anurag Pal, Janardan Kumar, Kuldeep and Himanshu – while they were shifting their unit from Sonipat to Saharanpur.“Jain had collected coins from Luthra for circulation. They would sell coins with a face value of ₹1 lakh for ₹70,000 in markets. They would also use them in daily transactions to blend them with legal coins, often at liquor shops, local paan shops, toll plazas and grocery stores,” a senior Delhi Police officer said.A team led by deputy commissioner of police (Crime) Harsh Indora and ACP Raj Kumar found that the gang had manufactured counterfeit coins worth more than ₹40 crore over the past decade by repeatedly shifting its factories between cities.To be sure, according to Reserve Bank of India data from November 13, 2026, coins worth over ₹43,000 crore are currently in circulation in the country.Also Read | Delhi: 4 arrested for allegedly minting counterfeit coinsHow the coins were madeInvestigators found that the gang had built an extensive network of workers who collected scrap and other materials containing aluminium, copper and nickel.“They would procure the mixtures from different factories and scrap yards in Delhi, but later expanded their collection network to more than seven towns and villages around NCR. Since Luthra was a goldsmith in Mohali, he had knowledge of using machines and dies,” a second investigator said.He added that Luthra and Himanshu met in Tihar jail in 2019 and became friends. They subsequently planned to manufacture ₹10 coins and set up a small unit in Delhi.After the pandemic, in 2021, the gang identified greater potential in manufacturing ₹20 coins, which had been introduced in the market around 2020, police said.“The material was almost the same and the margin was good. The gang had six to seven machines used to turn metal pieces and alloys into circular shapes. These machines cost ₹2-3 lakh, but using Luthra’s contacts, the gang acquired them for ₹80,000 to ₹1 lakh. Luthra also used his contacts in Delhi to gain access to specialised dies to replicate the outer and inner layers of ₹20 coins. The dies were pressed onto the metal mixtures to make the coins,” the investigator said.Also Read | Keep Bishnoi’s lawyer away from rival gang, court tells Tihar adminAccording to officers familiar with the investigation, the gang established a supply chain for brass and nickel through multiple sources to avoid attracting suspicion by procuring large quantities from a single supplier.Inspector Ashish Sharma and his team found that most of the brass was purchased from hardware stores and scrap dealers for ₹100-200 per kg. The gang relied on contacts with scrap dealers across Delhi-NCR, police said.Nickel, largely obtained in the form of scrap cupronickel – an alloy made primarily of copper combined with nickel and minor additions – was procured at ₹300-500 per kg.Police said procuring scrap metal instead of high-grade metal in large quantities also helped the gang avoid the need for expensive smelting equipment. Instead, it relied on stamping the metal, a considerably cheaper process. “They had no smelting equipment. They would procure only sillia (rectangular-shaped) alloys or ring-shaped alloys. These would then be cut with metal saws. After this, they would use a die machine to press the metal into a coin. A refining machine would then be used to make it look like a proper coin, with the correct width and weight,” an officer said.Also Read | Delhi gang used stolen health care data to sell fake drugs; 12 arrestedPolice have recovered more than 40 dies from the gang. “The gang had multiple specialised dies made exclusively in Delhi. We are yet to trace their source. The dies and machines are well known in the Chandni Chowk and Kucha Mahajani markets, as many jewellers use similar equipment to make gold and silver coins,” a third officer said.The accused also used grinding stones and cutting saws to shape the scrap metal. The finished product closely resembled a genuine ₹20 coin. According to police, the gang manufactured more than 10,000 coins every day, with each counterfeit ₹20 coin costing just ₹4-5 to produce.The investigation revealed that Himanshu and Luthra oversaw manufacturing units across Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and Delhi.DCP Indora said the gang had continued operating for more than a decade using traditional equipment that had remained effective over the years. “They used traditional machines and dies to manufacture the coins. We are working to identify and arrest more associates involved in the racket,” he said.

headline: 7 key meetings, deadline missed, Centre wants road sweeping machines on ‘war footing’
content: Since November 2025, the Centre has flagged the need to expand mechanised road sweeping and fix operational gaps in at least seven high-level meetings covering Delhi, records reviewed by The Indian Express show. In May 2026, the Centre directed the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) and the Delhi government to expedite procurement of “all remaining Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs)” and complete the process “by September”. After the deadline was missed, the Centre said in a meeting held just four days ago that the MRSMs should be procured on a “war footing”. Nov 11, 2025: Need more mechanised road sweeping At a review meeting on air pollution control in the region, chaired by Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav, CAQM was directed to ask municipal commissioners across the National Capital Region (NCR) to identify road categories according to their width and fix minimum MRSM deployment requirements for each. CAQM was also asked to circulate best practices adopted by municipal corporations for tendering machines under an operating expenditure (OPEX) model, where recurring payments are made to the provider based on output, to speed up procurement. An internal assessment at the time had identified 8,129 km of roads in Delhi for mechanised sweeping. The meeting also called for a substantial increase in MRSM deployment to meet the requirement and cover smaller roads. Dec 19: Monitor each machine At a review meeting covering Delhi, UP, Haryana and Greater Noida, the MCD, NDMC (New Delhi Municipal Council) and the Public Works Department (PWD) were directed to assign an officer to each MRSM to monitor its efficiency and verify whether it was removing visible dust. The monitoring mechanism was to include GPS tracking and recording the quantity of dust collected and handed over to the nearest construction and demolition waste collection and processing site. Jan 12, 2026: Need 505 machines The Delhi government and MCD were directed to prepare an action plan to increase the number of mechanical road sweepers from the existing 76 to 505. The 505-machine requirement was based on the length and width of Delhi’s road network. It comprised 246 small machines for 9,855 km of roads with a right of way (RoW) below 20 feet, 91 medium machines for 7,277 km of roads with a RoW of 20-60 feet, and 168 large machines for 13,409 km of roads with a RoW above 60 feet. Feb 2: Centralise monitoring The Union Environment Ministry directed CAQM to prioritise a centralised Management Information System (MIS). In the first phase, modules were to capture the functioning of MRSMs, to enable real-time tracking of progress, identify implementation gaps and facilitate decision-making across agencies. May 26: Deadline September At a meeting chaired by Yadav, CAQM and the Delhi government were told: “Efforts must be undertaken to procure all remaining Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) in alignment with the prescribed framework by CAQM, and the procurement process should be completed by the designated authorities by September, 2026.” Sept 28: Focus on deep cleaning With the deadline to procure all the additional MRSMs missed, the Centre directed the Delhi government, MCD, NDMC and PWD to ensure regular removal of visible dust and closely monitor road-cleaning activities. Agencies were also asked to identify narrow lanes and open spaces for repairs, paving and removal of accumulated dust. The Delhi government reported that the number of MRSMs had increased from 76 in the previous year to 98, including those operated by the MCD and NDMC — far below the 505 sought earlier. The meeting directed that deep cleaning of all roads, including market roads, be completed by October 31. Nov 19: 'War footing' At another high-level meeting, the Centre directed civic agencies to augment the capacity of MRSMs on a “war footing” and ensure their “full utilisation”, including through double-shift operations during winter, the Government said in an official statement. The Government also said in the statement that the various agencies involved were directed to ensure GPS-enabled monitoring of the road sweeping machines.

headline: Delhi to develop resting zones for gig workers in major markets, busy areas: Kapil Mishra
content: The Delhi Government plans to develop resting zones for gig workers in major markets and busy areas of the Capital, Labour and Employment Minister Kapil Mishra said on Monday, urging e-commerce and delivery companies to partner in the initiative.Addressing the annual conference ‘Sampark 2026’, organised by the Flipkart Foundation at Bharat Mandapam, Mishra said the government was ready to provide space for such facilities, while companies could contribute to their development and maintenance.He said a model centre had already been set up in Shalimar Bagh, where delivery partners could rest, charge their mobile phones and access drinking water. Similar facilities were being planned in areas with high delivery volumes.Emphasising the need to improve working conditions, Mishra said gig workers continued to work during extreme heat, heavy rainfall, waterlogging and severe cold, often late into the night. Their safety, health, rest and mental well-being needed attention, he said.The minister said the gig economy had become an important part of India’s employment landscape and that ensuring the social and economic security of workers and their families required coordinated efforts by the government, companies and social organisations.He said the Delhi Government had held meetings with representatives of employers and employees under Chief Minister Rekha Gupta to discuss the welfare of gig workers. Efforts were also under way to strengthen social security measures, including the formation of Gig Workers’ Welfare Boards in states.Mishra also called for skill development programmes to help delivery partners explore better career opportunities. Training in store management, warehouse operations and inventory management could open up avenues for career advancement, he said.Highlighting the changing employment landscape in the era of Artificial Intelligence, he said practical skills would become increasingly important. Companies should develop long-term plans for upskilling workers and supporting the education and skill development of their families, he added.

headline: South Delhi to get 8km elevated corridor with 4 flyovers
content: NEW DELHI: Delhi govt is planning an 8km elevated corridor comprising four flyovers along Mehrauli-Badarpur (MB) Road to ease traffic congestion in south Delhi. While Public Works Department (PWD) has received cabinet approval for two flyovers, consultants have been appointed to study the other two stretches.MB Road is among the busiest roads in south Delhi and has long faced congestion. The proposed corridor is expected to improve vehicular movement along the stretch from Saket G-Block to Badarpur, said a senior official. It will also ease the flow of traffic between Ambedkar Nagar, Khanpur, Sangam Vihar and Pul Prahladpur, reducing travel time for commuters.Of the two approved projects, a 2.4km flyover between Saket G and Sangam Vihar has made more than 50% progress, according to officials. The structure is being built over an underground Metro line and is an integrated flyover being executed by Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC).The second project is a 2.5km elevated stretch between Maa Anandmayee Marg and Pul Prahladpur. Work has started on this section and funds have been sanctioned, said officials. However, the project has encountered hurdles related to land acquisition. PWD has written to Delhi Development Authority (DDA), seeking the transfer of land parcels required for construction, the officials added.The cabinet had sanctioned over Rs 1,471 crore for the two approved flyovers. The move was part of govt’s plan to develop a six-lane elevated corridor on MB Road to address congestion in the area.The remaining two sections -- a 2.7km flyover between Sangam Vihar and Maa Anandmayee Marg, and a 450-metre stretch between Pul Prahladpur and Badarpur -- are at the planning stage. Consultants have been engaged for both the projects, and studies are currently under way.The detailed project reports for these two sections are expected to be ready by Jan 2027 and will subsequently be placed before govt for financial approval, officials said. Govt is also assessing the number of trees that may have to be felled to execute the proposed projects.A senior official said govt has also directed PWD to finalise the alignment of the remaining stretches towards Badarpur at the earliest. Once all four sections are completed, the elevated corridor is expected to provide smoother movement along one of South Delhi’s important arterial roads, he added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news.
