headline: Guide youth away from drugs, urges PM
content: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi Monday called for a collective effort to combat drug addiction, urging gurdwaras, families and communities to guide young people away from drugs and help them build a better future.Addressing a gathering at the official residence of lieutenant governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu to mark the 557th Parkash Purab of Guru Nanak Dev, Modi said, “An entire family suffers when a youth falls prey to addiction. Our families, Sikh gurus and sangat can play a vital role in... helping youth choose the right path.”BJP has turned the issue into its key political plank ahead of the 2027 assembly elections in Sikh-majority Punjab.Sandhu said this was the first time a serving Prime Minister had attended Parkash Purab celebrations at LG’s residence.Modi said the teachings of Guru Nanak and other Sikh gurus continued to inspire the country, particularly at a time when the world was witnessing considerable unrest. The community’s tradition is synonymous with the spirit of sacrifice for the country and its culture, Modi said, emphasising that his govt has worked to promote their heritage as an inspiration for society.“India endured hundreds of years of slavery. Our gurus kept the flame of protecting the country alive even in the most difficult period of its history. Now, when our big goals and the resolve of building a developed India (Viksit Bharat) are ahead of us, we can complete this journey only with the inspiration and strength of our gurus’ ideals,” said PM, who began his address with slogans of “Waheguru” and “Bole So Nihal”.After being presented with a siropa by the head granthi, PM greeted the gathering with “Parkash Purab di lakh lakh wadhaiyaan”. The message of universal welfare remains relevant, he said.Recalling his longstanding association with gurdwaras, Modi said he had always made it a point to offer prayers, participate in langar and perform seva. The Sikh principles of “Kirat Karo, Wand Chhako, Naam Japo” had been central to his own approach to life, he said. Modi also spoke about efforts made by his govt to familiarise younger generations with the sacrifices of Sikh gurus, and referred to the three-day Gurmat Samagam being organised at Red Fort from Nov 23 to 25 to commemorate the 350th martyrdom anniversary of Guru Tegh Bahadur. Referring to his visit to Philippines’ oldest gurdwara, Manila’s Khalsa Diwan Gurdwara, PM recalled India’s contribution to its redevelopment.Paying tribute to Sandhu’s grandfather, Teja Singh Samundri, one of the founders of Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, Modi recalled his contribution to society and the development of gurdwaras. The occasion also marked the 100th anniversary of his martyrdom.Sandhu said Samundri’s efforts strengthened Hindu-Sikh unity and recalled his death in Lahore Central Jail in 1926.Modi sat through the prayers and the recital of Gurbani by ragi Harjinder Singh Srinagarwale.The gathering was attended, among others, by chief minister Rekha Gupta, Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and his wife, and US ambassador Sergio Gor.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: CJP’s Saurav Das stopped from taking flight to Oxford at Delhi airport
content: Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das on Monday alleged that he was stopped at Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport from travelling to London, where he was scheduled to deliver a lecture at the Oxford Union.In a post on X late Monday, Das blamed the Narendra Modi-led government for the action, writing: “I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi government at the Delhi airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford.”The alleged interception comes days after The Tribune first reported that Das, along with CJP legal head Ratna Singh, was scheduled to travel to the UK to address a panel at the Oxford Union on December 1.The event was part of the youth-led outfit’s efforts to take its campaign on education, unemployment, and political accountability beyond India.No official reason for stopping Das from travelling had been made public at the time of writing. It was also not immediately clear whether the action was linked to any pending police proceedings against him.Das was among the CJP leaders detained at Delhi airport on October 10 ahead of the outfit’s proposed protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He was subsequently arrested again following a protest at Jantar Mantar on October 13 and spent seven days in judicial custody before being released on October 21.The latest development comes amid continuing legal proceedings involving CJP leaders following their protests in the Capital.

headline: Feasibility of retaining Krishi Bhawan mosque must be examined: Delhi Waqf Board
content: New Delhi The Delhi Waqf Board on Monday told the Delhi High Court that authorities must examine the possibility of retaining the century-old Qadeemi Mosque at Krishi Bhawan within the Central Vista redevelopment project. In a reply filed before the court, the board said the feasibility of preserving the mosque and allowing its continued religious use should be assessed against the approved redevelopment plans and relevant technical material. “The board’s primary request is for consideration of the preservation and retention of the existing mosque. The board’s limited objective is to facilitate a lawful and practical resolution that safeguards public interest, respects the documented religious character of the existing mosque and permits the redevelopment project to proceed in accordance with the law,” it said. Qadeemi Masjid, a more than 100-year-old notified waqf property situated within the Krishi Bhawan premises, is facing demolition due to the Central Vista redevelopment project. The Waqf Board further argued, “The feasibility of retaining the existing mosque within the redevelopment layout deserves examination on the basis of the approved plans and relevant technical material without compromising the essential requirements of the public project”. The Delhi Waqf Board was represented by advocate Tushar Sannu. It maintained that the construction of Common Central Secretariat (CCS) buildings on the site could not, by itself, justify disregarding the mosque’s religious character and notified status. “Any proposal for redevelopment must consider feasible alternatives which would preserve the existing mosque and its religious use, rather than treating its removal as an inevitable consequence of the proposed project,” the board said. The board’s response came on a petition filed by the caretaking committee of Qadeemi Masjid , also known as Masjid Krishi Bhavan, seeking to restrain authorities from demolishing or disturbing the mosque without a fair, transparent and reasoned assessment of the possibility of retaining it. Justice Anish Dayal on Monday granted time to the caretaking committee to respond to the Waqf Board’s stand and listed the matter for hearing in January. Appearing for the committee, senior advocate Salman Khurshid urged the court to ensure that access to the mosque was not obstructed in the meantime. The court also directed the Waqf Board and the Land and Development Office (L&DO) to respond within four weeks to representations submitted by another petitioner, a worshipper, seeking preservation of the mosque, which is primarily used by Central government employees. During the hearing, the court asked Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, to explore whether a solution could be worked out, noting that the mosque had existed for several years and its worshippers were government employees. Mr. Sharma responded that government-controlled office premises currently did not have facilities for offering prayers. He suggested that the Waqf Board could make a representation to the Centre on behalf of the employees. The Centre has previously opposed the plea maintaining that the mosque must be removed as a permanent religious structure within a government office complex was impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of the government property.

headline: What makes cycling risky in city? Parked vehicles, wrong-way driving
content: NEW DELHI: Delhi’s roads are becoming increasingly hostile to cyclists, with parked vehicles, wrong-way driving and poorly managed roadside activities emerging as major safety hazards, according to a study by researchers at IIT Delhi.The study, published in Elsevier’s ‘Journal of Transport & Health’, found that on-street parking was associated with 2.6 times higher odds of a bicycle crash. Cyclists riding on the wrong side faced 3.1 times higher odds, while motor vehicles driving against traffic were associated with 2.5 times higher odds.The findings are based on interactions with 844 cyclists across 27 locations in Delhi. Researchers identified 106 self-reported non-fatal crashes at midblock locations and compared them with 319 control locations along the cyclists’ pre-crash routes. While midblock locations refer to sections of road between two intersections, control locations are randomly selected points along the same cyclists’ routes.The extent of roadside parking emerged as a particular concern. Researchers observed parking-related activity at 72% of the control locations against nearly 90% of the crash locations. The definition included not just parked cars and two-wheelers but also autos, e-rickshaws and taxis stopping to pick up or drop off passengers, and vehicles halting for loading and unloading.The researchers estimated that eliminating on-street parking could potentially avert 55% of non-fatal midblock bicycle crashes, assuming other risk factors remained unchanged.Other road features also showed significant associations with crashes. The presence of a bus stop was associated with 2.38 times higher odds, while flyovers and U-turns were associated with 2.44 times and nearly twice the odds, respectively. Researchers suggest that widely spaced U-turns and the removal of convenient crossings may force cyclists to navigate multiple lanes or take longer detours.There was, however, dedicated cycling infrastructure in some areas, and the presence of a segregated cycle track was associated with fewer crashes.The study also found that arterial roads with fewer kerbside hazards had one-ninth the odds of a crash compared with the most hazardous category of national highways with a high concentration of roadside activities. The research recommends physically segregated cycle tracks, designated parking and vending spaces, dedicated pick-up and drop-off zones, and stronger enforcement against unauthorised parking and wrong-way driving. They also call for traffic-calming measures where separate cycle tracks are not feasible.The findings are significant for a city where cycling’s share of travel has fallen from 36% in 1957 to 5% in 2013. Delhi recorded an average of 41 cyclist deaths annually between 2021 and 2023, according to figures cited in the study.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. headline: Delhi govt to launch dedicated portal for domestic consumers to claim power subsidy
content: New Delhi, Nov 23 (PTI) The Delhi government will soon launch a dedicated portal for domestic power consumers to opt for subsidy, officials said on Monday. After the launch of the portal, expectedly in the first week of December, the consumers will have a month to register on the portal using the required documents and opt for the subsidy, a senior government officer said. The consumers will need to opt for the subsidy every year. Those who do not opt in will forfeit it, he said. Power discoms will verify the consumers using their electricity consumer number and Aadhaar details, the officials said. The Delhi government led by the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) began providing power subsidy in 2022 exclusively to domestic consumers who applied for it. Under the existing subsidy scheme, the Delhi government offers free electricity to domestic consumers who use up to 200 units per month.

headline: 'Anti-intellectual govt': CJP's Saurav Das says he was stopped at Delhi airport from flying to London for an Oxford event
content: New Delhi: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Co-Convenor Saurav on Monday night claimed that he was stopped at Delhi airport from flying to London where he was scheduled to attend a programme at the University of Oxford. Das said in a post on X, "I have been stopped by this cowardly Modi Govt at the Delhi Airport from flying to London to deliver a lecture at the University of Oxford." .There was no immediate reaction from the authorities on the reason why Das was stopped from flying out of the country. Das along with CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and Co-Convenor Abhishek Ranka were in the forefront of a youth movement that led to the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. They were also part of the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Cases were registered against the trio in connection with the protests. Both Das and Ranka among others were questioned by Delhi Police’s Crime Branch recently. In a video on ‘Instagram’, Das said he was to take a flight to London at 1 AM but as he approached the immigration gate, he was told his passport has been flagged by the government and that he cannot fly out of India. He said he was invited by the students union of the University of Oxford to participate in a panel discussion. .“The anti-intellectual government is scared of me going to a prestigious university. Why is the government so scared of an educated youth having an intellectual discussion with youngsters? The Indian students had invited me,” he said. “It seems I have done something bad! I should have been Nirav Modi or Vijay Mallya that I have looted the country. Then they would have allowed me to fly to London,” he alleged. Modi and Mallya, who were accused of defrauding banks, had left the country for the United Kingdom earlier.

headline: BJP targets AAP over drugs, gangsterism in Punjab
content: The BJP on Wednesday accused the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab of failing to curb drug trafficking, gangsterism and extortion. Delhi minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa alleged that criminal networks were operating under political protection.Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Sirsa warned that AAP leaders allegedly accepting money from drug smugglers or protecting criminal networks would face imprisonment if the NDA formed the next government in Punjab. He specifically named senior AAP leaders Manish Sisodia and Satyendar Jain, asserting that political influence would not shield anyone from action.Questioning the effectiveness of the Mann government’s anti-drug campaign, Sirsa cited figures released by the AAP government claiming that 94,746 arrests had been made in 632 days. He compared this figure with Punjab’s reported prison capacity of around 26,000 inmates and questioned how such a large number of accused persons could have been detained.He alleged that cases were being registered under less stringent provisions of the law, enabling accused persons to secure bail instead of ensuring sustained action against drug trafficking networks.Sirsa also referred to the killing of Punjab Police Sub-Inspector Iqbal Singh in Tarn Taran and a reported police advisory against off-duty personnel travelling in uniform. He argued that the incidents reflected growing concerns over the safety of police personnel.Accusing the AAP government of worsening Punjab’s financial position, Sirsa claimed that the state’s debt had increased from Rs 2.5 lakh crore to Rs 5 lakh crore during its tenure.

headline: 20 Punjab bureaucrats summoned by ED in two months, AAP cries foul | Hindustan Times
content: The recent Enforcement Directorate (ED) action, which has seen 20 Punjab bureaucrats, including 10 IAS, eight PCS and an IPS and a PPS officer each, summoned and questioned in three separate investigations over the past two months, has brought the state’s bureaucracy under unprecedented federal scrutiny.The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has snapped back, accusing the Bharatiya Janata Party-led Centre of misusing central agencies to target the Punjab government, alleging that the summons are politically motivated and aimed at disrupting its functioning.The high-profile list includes chief secretary KAP Sinha and two principal secretaries. Of the 10 IAS officers, two are retired.The investigations span alleged irregularities in land dealings involving the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), real estate transactions linked to Ritesh Properties and Industries Ltd (RPIL), later renamed Hampton Sky Realty Limited, and the bribery and disproportionate assets case against suspended DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar.Also read: Punjab: IAS, IPS officers among seven summoned by ED in PMLA probe linked to Bhullar graft caseGMADA land deal probeNearly two months after conducting searches at the Punjab Urban Planning and Development Authority (PUDA) headquarters, the ED has intensified its probe into alleged irregularities in GMADA land dealings, summoning several serving and former officials of the housing and urban development department.Those summoned include GMADA chief administrator Sandeep Rishi (IAS); principal secretary, housing and urban development, Vikas Garg (IAS); and former chief administrator Sakshi Sawhney (IAS).Among the PCS officers are land acquisition officer Rohit Jindal, estate officer Aman Gupta, former additional chief administrator Rakesh Kumar Popli, additional chief administrator Amarinder Singh Mali, and former land acquisition officer Hardeep Singh.The agency has also summoned chief secretary KAP Sinha and principal secretary, finance, Alok Shekhar, to appear on November 26 in the money-laundering investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).Also read: ED summons two Punjab AAP MLAs in land fraud, money-laundering probeED examines alleged manipulation of land prices and auction conditionsOn September 22, the ED conducted searches at 26 premises across Delhi, Mohali, Chandigarh, Panchkula and Ludhiana, including the GMADA headquarters at PUDA Bhawan and offices of the housing and urban development department. The probe concerns alleged bank fraud and subsequent money laundering involving real estate developer Tirupati Infraprojects and its associated entities.The agency is examining whether changes in land-use policies, reserve prices, auction conditions and master plans benefited select private entities. It alleged that manipulation of reserve prices of unsold GMADA land could have caused a potential loss of nearly ₹10,000 crore to the authority and the Punjab government.Earlier, former chief secretary Anurag Verma, who headed the housing and urban development department in 2024, was questioned in September in a separate probe involving Mohali-based Suntec City and Altus Space Builders Private Limited over a Change of Land Use (CLU) issue. Director, town and country planning, Kanwal Preet Brar was also questioned in the same case.The investigations have also affected routine administrative work. A senior department officer said officials were spending considerable time compiling records and preparing replies to the agency.AAP MP and party spokesperson Malwinder Singh Kang accused the BJP-led Centre of misusing central agencies to target the state government, alleging the summons were aimed at derailing its functioning.Also read: GMADA land deals probe: ED summons Punjab chief secy, finance secy on Nov 26Real estate transactions under scannerIn the second case, the ED questioned Vikas Hira (PCS), chief administrator of the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA), in August and September in connection with a real estate and money-laundering probe.The agency is examining land and property transactions, including records related to RPIL, subsequently renamed Hampton Sky Realty Limited and linked to AAP minister Sanjeev Arora.Bhullar graft caseIn the third case, the ED has summoned serving and retired officials in a money-laundering investigation stemming from the corruption case against suspended DIG Harcharan Singh Bhullar and his alleged associates.Those summoned include health and family welfare administrative secretary Kumar Rahul (IAS), special secretary, general administration, Neeru Katyal Gupta (IAS), and Anand Sagar Sharma (PCS), staff officer to the commissioner, Faridkot division.Also read: Punjab: Bhullar’s aide acted as middleman for several officials, says EDLudhiana police commissioner Swapan Sharma (IPS) and Fazilka SSP Gagan Ajit Singh (PPS) have also been summoned.Two retired IAS officers, former Jalandhar commissioner Gurpreet Kaur Sapra and former divisional commissioner Arun Sekhri, are also among those called. They have been asked to appear on November 26 and 25, respectively.The PMLA probe stems from two CBI FIRs against Bhullar and his associates on charges of bribery and alleged possession of disproportionate assets. Bhullar, then DIG, Ropar Range, was arrested by the CBI in October 2025.

headline: Punjab farm fires cross 7,000; 2,144 FIRs lodged
content: Bathinda: Punjab recorded 37 fresh farm fire cases on Monday, pushing the state’s seasonal tally to 7,086—over 38% higher than last year’s total of 5,114—even as Uttar Pradesh (174) and Madhya Pradesh (154) led daily stubble burning incidents across seven northern states.According to data from the Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modeling from Space (CREAMS), 404 farm fires were detected across the seven states on Monday, taking the cumulative tally to 17,420 across 179 districts, including all 23 districts of Punjab.With the surge in cases in other states, Punjab’s share in the seven-state total has dipped to 40.67%.Four Punjab districts feature among the top 10 worst-affected districts nationwide: Ferozepur (909 cases), Sangrur (801), Tarn Taran (711), and Bathinda (645).To curb the spike, authorities have intensified penal action across Punjab, registering 2,144 FIRs under Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (disobedience to an order duly promulgated by a public servant) and marking red entries in land records in 2,268 cases.Environmental compensation (EC) worth Rs 1.2 crore has been imposed in 2,446 cases, of which Rs 43.3 lakh has been realised so far.Action has also been initiated against officials for laxity, with warning or show-cause notices issued to 2,193 nodal and supervisory officers, and prosecution launched against 41 supervisory officers under Section 14 of the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) Act, which carries imprisonment up to five years, a fine up to Rs 1 crore, or both.

headline: HC pulls up Punjab Govt officials over lapses in land acquisition cases
content: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has rapped Punjab Government officials for a lackadaisical approach and failure to properly defend land acquisition compensation cases. The Bench observed that inadequate evidence, failure to verify sale deeds and selective filing of appeals were creating financial liabilities for the state.Taking note of the pattern during the preceding four months, Justice Jagmohan Bansal directed the high court registry to send the order’s copy to the state chief secretary and the principal/additional chief secretary (law and justice) for bringing the concerns to the attention of the state’s senior-most administrative and legal authorities.Justice Bansal observed: “During the last four months, I have noticed that in most of the cases, the state does not lead requisite evidence before the reference court and as per evidence led by landowners, huge state’s fiscal liability is created.”The Bench was hearing a batch of 55 petitions filed by landlords against different awards passed by reference court/additional district judge, Ropar. They were seeking enhancement of compensation following acquisition of land in nine villages for the construction of the Ropar bypass, while the state was claiming otherwise.A reference court in land acquisition cases is the judicial forum that adjudicates objections raised by an interested person who does not accept the compensation or terms awarded by the land acquisition collector/officer.Flagging the failure to scrutinise transactions relied upon for determining compensation, Justice Bansal observed: “No effort is made to find out genuineness of sale deeds comprising small pieces of land and that too executed just few months before the initiation of acquisition process.”Justice Bansal also questioned the state’s approach to challenging compensation awards. Referring to the matters placed before the Bench, Justice Bansal observed: “Appeals have been filed in a few cases and no appeal has been filed where a higher amount was awarded.”Justice Bansal noted that even specific judicial directions had not ensured production of essential documentary evidence. “Despite specific orders of this court, the state does not produce a site plan disclosing the location of the acquired land as well as exemplar sale deeds,” the court observed.Justice Bansal asserted: “A very casual and lackadaisical approach is adopted by all officials dealing with the matters.” Referring to the need to balance the rights of landowners with the protection of public money, the Bench made it clear that compensation was required to be fair without imposing an unjustified burden on the government exchequer. “A land loser deserves just and fair compensation; however, he cannot be paid an exorbitant amount at the cost of the government exchequer,” the court observed.

headline: Scientific management of crop residue in Punjab must for better soil health, financial stability
content: Every autumn, Punjab witnesses a familiar cycle. As paddy harvesting nears completion, farm fires spread across the state, raising concerns over air pollution and public health. Farmers often become the focus of the blame game, but stubble burning is also linked to the economics of farming and the lack of affordable alternatives for managing crop residue. headline: Haryana’s Neeti Chaudhary Wins Best Oral Presentation Award At E-MRS 2026 In Warsaw -
content: Researcher from Kaithal’s Bhana village recognised for work on nanomaterials and sustainable energy storage technology Chandigarh: Neeti Chaudhary, a daughter of Bhana village in Haryana’s Kaithal district, has brought recognition to Haryana and India by winning the Best Oral Presentation Award at the E-MRS 2026 conference in Warsaw, Poland. Her award recognises her impressive presentation of research in the field of nanomaterials and sustainable energy storage technology, highlighting the growing contribution of young Indian researchers to advanced scientific research. Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini congratulated Neeti Chaudhary on the achievement and extended his best wishes for her future endeavours. The Chief Minister said that her recognition for presenting research in the field of nanomaterials and sustainable energy storage technology was a matter of pride and an inspiration for young people pursuing science and research. He wished Neeti a bright and successful future and expressed hope that her achievement would encourage more young people from Haryana and across India to pursue scientific research and innovation. The recognition at an international scientific conference in Warsaw marks a significant achievement for Neeti Chaudhary and brings the name of Kaithal, Haryana, and India into the international research community. The E-MRS 2026 Fall Meeting & Exhibit took place from September 14–17, 2026, at the Warsaw University of Technology in Warsaw, Poland. Because awards at E-MRS meetings are often given by individual symposia, sessions, or announced by institutions, multiple researchers have reported receiving oral presentation awards at the event.

headline: CM Saini to lead UK, Germany investment push
content: In a major push to attract global investment, Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will lead a high-level delegation to the United Kingdom (UK) and Germany from November 28 to December 5 to explore opportunities for trade, industrial cooperation, education, skill development and artificial intelligence (AI).Industries and Commerce Minister Rao Narbir Singh and senior officials will accompany the CM. The delegation will hold meetings with global firms, investors, universities, research institutions and industry representatives to showcase Haryana as an attractive investment destination.During the UK leg, Saini will interact with business leaders, investors and a Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) delegation to discuss investment opportunities and industrial partnerships. He will also meet members of the Haryana diaspora and invite them to contribute to the state’s economic growth through investments.On November 30 and December 1, the Chief Minister is scheduled to hold one-to-one meetings with representatives of leading companies and educational institutions. Roundtable discussions will explore trade and investment opportunities under the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), with special focus on education, vocational training and skill development.His engagements will also include meetings with representatives of the Centre for Science and Policy at the University of Cambridge and Indian students at Oxford University. A visit to Queen Elizabeth’s School, Barnet, is planned to explore educational cooperation and the possibility of setting up an educational campus in Haryana.In Germany, a Haryana investment roadshow will be organised on December 2 to highlight the state’s industrial infrastructure, connectivity, skilled workforce and investor-friendly policies.On December 3, Saini will meet representatives of the Fraunhofer research and technology institution to discuss setting up a Centre of Excellence in Haryana. An MoU is also scheduled to be signed in this regard. The delegation will conclude its visit with meetings with leading German companies, industrialists and potential investors on December 4 and 5.Pilgrimage train to Varanasi to depart on Dec 15The Haryana Government will organise a free four-day pilgrimage to Varanasi for senior citizens under the Chief Minister Teerth Yatra Scheme from December 15.Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini will flag off a special train carrying the pilgrims. A portal has been opened to invite applications from eligible devotees. Senior citizens aged 60 and above will be eligible for the scheme.Registration is being carried out through the Antyodaya-SARAL portal at https://saralharyana.gov.in.‘Govt committed to creating equal opportunities for all’Kurukshetra: Saini said ensuring equal opportunities for every section of society and bringing the last person into the mainstream remained key priorities of his government. He was addressing a welcome ceremony for the Samrasta Sankalp Yatra at Umri here. The yatra is being organised to commemorate the 650th birth anniversary year of Guru Ravidas.

headline: Boundary wall broken, villagers dump garbage on CHC premises in Rewari district
content: Inadequate infrastructure, lack of blood bank, insufficient OPD space and number of beds for admitted patients and residential quarters for the staff members have been ailing the Community Health Centre (CHC) at Meerpur village in Rewari district.The CHC, which was upgraded from a Primary Health Centre (PHC) long ago, is still functioning from the same old building which often needs repairs and maintenance.Sources point out that the CHC building underwent special repairs recently as the roof used to leak badly.“However, proper electric fittings have not been made after the special repairs, due to which we face frequent power outages and short-circuits,” maintains a doctor serving at the government hospital.The doctors lament that the infrastructure of the hospital is inadequate for the patients coming for treatment on a daily basis as well as the staff members serving here.“The CHC should have 30 beds, but it has only nine. The space for OPD patients is also insufficient. There are no residential quarters for the doctors and other staff members,” states another staffer.The inadequacy of resources can be gauged from the fact that ideally, there should be a CHC on a population of 1 lakh residents, but this CHC has been catering to a population of nearly 2.5 lakh.Strangely, the neighbouring town of Dharuhera, which is a major hub of industry and real estate sector and houses big manufacturing, storage/supply and other units of Hero MotoCorp, Jtekt India, Lumax Industries, Rico Auto Industries, Amul dairy plant, Carlsberg and Indian Oil Corporation, merely has a primary health centre (PHC). Indira Gandhi University (IGU) is also located in Meerpur village.On the other hand, the building of the Meerpur CHC is in such a dilapidated condition that its boundary wall is broken and the compound has been reduced to a garbage-dumping ground by the local residents.“Taking advantage of the broken boundary wall, villagers dump their domestic waste in the hospital compound. Stray animals like cattle and dogs also enter the hospital premises,” laments an employee.The hospital runs OPDs and emergency services and also admits patients, but those requiring blood have to be referred to the Civil Hospital as there is no blood bank at the CHC.The hospital also faces a shortage of staff. Of the 140 sanctioned posts of all categories 32 are lying vacant.Contacted for her comments, Dr Saroj Ranga, Senior Medical Officer in charge of the CHC, said the authorities concerned have been apprised of the constraints.

headline: Haryana BJP reorganises Kisan Morcha; 27 district heads named | Hindustan Times
content: Focusing on regional and caste balance, the Haryana BJP has reorganised its Kisan Morcha by appointing a new team of state office-bearers, executive committee members and district presidents, giving representation to leaders from different regions and social groups across the state.The appointments, announced by Kisan Morcha state president Mahesh Chauhan on Monday, include four state vice-presidents, two general secretaries, four state secretaries and heads of various organisational wings, besides 16 members of the state executive committee and 27 district presidents. The appointments have been made with the consent of state BJP president Archana Gupta and the party’s senior leadership and will come into effect immediately.Mandeep Virk from Kurukshetra, Isham Sakra from Kaithal, Babita Dahiya from Sonepat and Pradeep Kamboj from Karnal have been appointed state vice-presidents. Harivardhan Mann from Bhiwani and Sandeep Gurjar from Yamunanagar have been named general secretaries.The party appointed Prithvi Bijroi from Dabwali, Manoj Goyal from Panipat, Dinesh Saini from Rewari and Prinsi Chahar from Gurugram Mahanagar as state secretaries. Ashok Mandewal has been appointed treasurer, Dharambir Jakhar from Hisar office secretary, Mangeraam Kaushik from Kurukshetra media head, Sandeep Panwar from Gurugram IT head and Naveen Yadav from Gurugram social media head.The newly announced state executive committee includes Gautam Rana from Panchkula, Rambir Chauhan from Ambala, Mukesh Bhardwaj from Jind, Satish Bhoria from Rohtak, Baldev Beniwal from Sirsa, Veer Singh Jathlana from Yamunanagar, Pawan Yadav from Mahendragarh and Layak Ram Gudwal from Fatehabad.The other members of the state executive committee are Divyanshu Gaur from Palwal, Aadesh Yadav from Faridabad Mahanagar, Ramphal Bhura from Hansi, Jitender Bhardwaj from Faridabad, Jagvinder Khattana from Gurugram Mahanagar, Monu Jaldhar from Nuh, Sonia from Gohana and Raj Rani Sangwan from Charkhi Dadri.In the district-level appointments, Rajiv Rathore has been made president in Panchkula, Nirmal Singh in Ambala, Nitesh Rana in Yamunanagar, Charan Ajit Singh in Kurukshetra, Mohipal Rana in Kaithal, Surender Tyagi in Karnal, Subhash Kuhad in Panipat, Sumit Antil in Sonepat and Pradeep Badwasni in Gohana.The other district presidents are Ramphal Morshi (Jind), Ravi Hooda (Rohtak), Vinod Baudas (Jhajjar), Kuldeep Jat (Dabwali), Bhagwat Singh (Sirsa), Chhatar Pal Kapado (Hansi), Ajay Beniwal (Hisar), Avtar Singh Ladv (Fatehabad), Lavkesh Banti (Bhiwani), Sandeep Chairman (Charkhi Dadri), Pardeep Badkhera (Rewari), Dinesh Dalal Singh (Mahendragarh), Mukesh Jaldhar (Gurugram), Naresh Dayama (Gurugram Mahanagar), Manish Yadav (Nuh), Sachin Kumar (Palwal), Jagbir Phogat (Faridabad Mahanagar) and Raju Thakur (Faridabad).

headline: Haryana court sentences man to 20 years for sexually assaulting minor girl in Tohana | Hindustan Times
content: A district court in Fatehabad sentenced a man to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment (RI) for raping a minor girl in Tohana.Additional district and sessions judge Amit Garg pronounced the verdict convicting Sunil Kumar alias Gill alias Gillu in the case registered at Tohana City police station.According to district attorney Devender Mittal, who conducted the prosecution, the court awarded him seven years of RI and a fine of ₹50,000 under Section 137(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 10 years of RI and a fine of ₹50,000 under Section 87 of the BNS, and 20 years of RI and a fine of ₹50,000 under Section 4(2) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.All three sentences will run concurrently. In case of default in payment of the fines, the convict will undergo an additional six months’ RI under each of the two BNS provisions and one year’s additional RI under the POCSO Act.Also read: Supreme Court flags dangers in rape case settlementsVictim to receive ₹1 lakh from fine, additional compensation recommendedThe court also ordered that ₹50,000 out of the total fine of ₹1.5 lakh be deposited in the state treasury towards case expenses, while ₹1 lakh be paid to the victim as compensation. Additionally, it recommended another ₹50,000 in compensation for the girl under the Haryana Victim Compensation Scheme, 2013.The district legal services authority (DLSA), Fatehabad, has been directed to complete the necessary formalities and ensure compliance with the compensation order within six weeks.The incident took place on November 2, 2024, when the accused allegedly lured the minor girl onto his motorcycle on the pretext of taking her to a doctor. Instead, he took her to his shop and forcibly took her to a room on the upper floor, where he sexually assaulted her. He left her after she raised an alarm.Also read: Over 1,300 rape cases in state in 3 years, Himachal Pradesh CM tells HousePolice collected medical, forensic and age-related evidenceDuring the investigation, police recorded the victim’s statement, conducted her medical examination, inspected and identified the crime scene, recovered the motorcycle allegedly used in the offence and collected documents establishing her age. A chargesheet was subsequently filed before the court.In its judgment, the court observed that the accused had abused the trust reposed in him and sexually exploited a minor. It held that awarding a lesser sentence would be unjust to the victim and convey a wrong message to society.

headline: Modern facilities to boost technical education in rural areas in Himachal: Minister
content: Education Minister Rohit Thakur today inaugurated a Government Industrial Training Institute (ITI) building, constructed at a cost of Rs 10.62 crore, and a lift drinking water scheme, built at a cost of Rs 1.04 crore, at the Atal Bihari Vajpayee Government Institute of Technology (ABVGIET) at Pragati Nagar in the Jubbal-Nawar-Kotkhai Assembly constituency of Shimla district.Speaking on the occasion, the minister said the state government was prioritising the expansion of educational infrastructure, improvement in the quality of education and employment-oriented technical education. He said the government was committed to providing students in rural and remote areas with better educational facilities and equal opportunities to excel.He added that efforts were underway to further improve facilities for students and faculty members at the institute.Thakur said the tender process for the construction of a Kendriya Vidyalaya in the Kotkhai area was underway. The technical tender would be opened on December 1, 2026, while the financial tender was expected to be opened on December 15, 2026. “It is also expected that Prime Minister Narendra Modi will lay its foundation stone virtually,” he added.The minister said projects worth Rs 100 crore were underway to strengthen educational infrastructure in the region, including Kotkhai and Gumma. He said the process of affiliating the Government School at Gumma with the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) had been affected due to inadequate infrastructure. The government would consider CBSE affiliation once the construction of the school building was completed, he added.Addressing the students, Thakur said their future achievements and contributions to society and nation-building would depend on their dedication, hard work and determination. He said the younger generation was the future of the state and the country and urged students to make the most of the improved educational environment and opportunities available to them to hone their skills and talents.

headline: Colleges must adjust to education shift: Himachal MLA Ashish Butail
content: The 27th National Conference on ‘Higher Education in the Era of Industry 6.0’, organised at Goswami Ganesh Dutt Sanatan Dharma (GGDSD) College, Rajpur, under the joint aegis of the Society for Education and Economic Development (SEED) and the Himachal Pradesh Chapter of the Indian Colleges Forum (ICF), concluded on a grand note.The three-day conference was inaugurated by Prof Lalit Kumar Awasthi, Vice-Chancellor of Sardar Patel University, Mandi. Addressing the gathering, chief guest Ashish Butail congratulated the college management, organisers and participants on the successful completion of the conference. Appreciating the rich legacy and academic contributions of GGDSD College, he emphasised the need for higher education institutions to adapt to the rapidly evolving educational landscape by providing students with greater practical exposure and wider opportunities.He highlighted the crucial role of higher education institutions in promoting quality education, innovation and skill development. He also noted that such academic platforms provide educators an opportunity to deliberate on policies and initiatives that can shape the future of young people.Dr GD Sharma, head of SEED and former UGC Secretary, outlined the genesis and objectives of SEED and the Indian Colleges Forum.

headline: Chandigarh: City’s air quality deteriorates, AQI hits 146
content: Air quality in the city continued its downward slide on Wednesday, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) climbing to 146 and slipping into the ‘moderate’ category.According to the daily bulletin issued by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), the city witnessed a sharp deterioration in air quality within a span of just 24 hours, from an AQI of 109 recorded on Tuesday. Data from Continuous Ambient Air Quality Monitoring Stations (CAAQMS) across Chandigarh revealed varying degrees of particulate pollution in different pockets of the city. The monitoring station at Sector 53 recorded the worst air quality in the city on Wednesday with an AQI of 153, followed closely by Sector 25, which registered an AQI of 146. Meanwhile, Sector 22 fared slightly better, logging an AQI of 116.Experts and officials attribute the steady spike in pollution levels to a combination of local civic activities and unfavourable meteorological conditions. Ongoing road recarpeting works across several major stretches of the city have kicked up significant amounts of coarse dust, adding to the particulate load in the atmosphere. Compounding the problem are the seasonal dip in night temperatures alongside sluggish wind speeds.With winter setting in and calm atmospheric conditions prevailing, pollutants and dust particles are getting trapped closer to the surface instead of dispersing into the upper atmosphere. Under CPCB parameters, an AQI between 101 and 200 falls in the ‘moderate’ category, which can cause breathing discomfort to people with lung diseases such as asthma, as well as children and older adults.Health experts have advised vulnerable residents to limit prolonged outdoor exertion, particularly during early morning and late evening hours when particulate concentration tends to peak.With no immediate spell of rain predicted in the coming days, officials indicated that dust-mitigation measures, including regular water sprinkling along stretches undergoing road work, need strict enforcement to prevent the city’s air quality from slipping into the ‘poor’ category.

headline: 6 Congress leaders join SAD ahead of Chandigarh MC polls | Hindustan Times
content: Ahead of the Chandigarh municipal corporation elections on December 23, six members of the Congress joined the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) here on Monday.Former Congress leaders who joined the SAD include Jagtar Singh, Parvinder Singh, Avtar Singh, Pawan Kumar Goyal, Ishpinder Singh Batra and Manmohan Kaur.SAD secretary and party observer for Chandigarh Daljit Singh Cheema also held a meeting with the Chandigarh unit leadership to review poll preparations and discuss the party’s strategy.The meeting focused on strengthening the party’s organisational structure, with ward-wise and booth-wise responsibilities assigned to leaders and workers to improve coordination at the grassroots level. SAD Chandigarh unit president Charanjit Singh Villy said the meeting provided fresh direction to the party’s election preparations. He said the allocation of responsibilities across wards and booths would help strengthen the party’s grassroots network.Villy said the Chandigarh unit was working to expand its organisational presence across all wards and emerge as a strong political alternative in the forthcoming elections.Senior party leaders, including Bibi Harjinder Kaur, Arshdeep Singh Kler, Harjit Bhullar, Bibi Satwant Kaur Jauhal, Balwinder Singh, Zabarjang Singh, Mandeep Singh, Surjit Singh Raja and Nirbhai Singh, attended the meeting.

headline: Delhi Nursery Admission 2027-28: Up to 70 points for home-school distance, check age limit, documents and
content: Delhi Nursery Admission 2028: Private schools in Delhi have started publishing their admission criteria for the 2027-28 academic session, with neighbourhood distance emerging as a major factor in the selection process. Schools are offering between 50 and 70 points to applicants based on the distance between their residence and the school.The admission exercise will cover Nursery, KG and Class 1. More than 1,700 private schools in the national capital are preparing for the process. While several institutions have released their criteria, schools reported that the Directorate of Education's (DoE) criteria module was not operational on Monday evening, preventing them from uploading the prescribed details.Distance carries significant weight in admission scoringSchools have adopted different point systems under their neighbourhood criteria. Vidya Bal Bhavan Senior Secondary School in Mayur Vihar has allocated 50 to 70 points according to residential distance. Its 100-point assessment framework also includes 20 points for siblings and 10 points for alumni-related eligibility.Delhi Public School (DPS) has assigned 20 to 50 points based on distance. Children living within six kilometres receive 50 points, while those residing between six and eight kilometres get 40 points. Applicants living more than 15 kilometres away receive 20 points. Sibling applicants can receive 26 points, while children whose parents are alumni receive 12 points for each eligible parent.Application process and important datesOnline and school-level application forms will become available from December 1, 2026. Schools must keep forms accessible until December 28. The schedule for subsequent admission activities is as follows:Admission activityDateApplications beginDecember 1, 2026Applications closeDecember 28, 2026Applicant details uploadedJanuary 4, 2027First selection listJanuary 20, 2027Resolution of queriesJanuary 21-28, 2027Subsequent list, if seats remainFebruary 22, 2027Age eligibility for Nursery to Class 1The prescribed age will be calculated as of March 31, 2027.• Nursery: Above 3 and below 4 years• LKG: Above 4 and below 5 years• UKG: Above 5 and below 6 years• Class 1: Above 5 and below 6 yearsDocuments required for admissionParents should keep the child's birth certificate, identity proof, Aadhaar card, electricity or water bill, telephone bill, child's passport or ration card ready.The DoE has also clarified that private schools cannot compel parents to purchase admission prospectuses. Schools must upload applicants' details along with the points awarded to each child on the department's portal.Get the latest Education News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

headline: Will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, says Supreme Court amid winter pollution crisis | India News
content: The Supreme Court on Monday made it clear that only vehicles complying with BS-VI emission standards should be allowed to ply in Delhi during the winter months, even as it described the capital’s relatively better air quality this November as a matter of good fortune, saying favourable winds had prevented pollution levels from slipping into the ‘severe’ category.“We are clear we will allow only BS-VI vehicles in Delhi, if not NCR,” a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed, signalling its intention to continue restrictions on polluting vehicles during the winter months.Court says favourable winds helped Delhi avoid severe pollutionThe bench, hearing the court’s ongoing suo motu proceedings on air pollution in Delhi-NCR, said the region was “lucky” to have avoided ‘severe’ category pollution this November, attributing the relatively better conditions primarily to favourable meteorological conditions.“We have also been lucky this winter. There is no ‘severe’ category pollution till now because of the winds,” it remarked.When additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM), pointed to the efforts made by authorities to contain pollution, the court responded: “Primarily nature.” Bhati, however, maintained that enforcement measures had also contributed to the situation. Senior advocate Aparajita Singh is assisting the court as amicus curiae.Also read: AQI worsens slightly; Delhi could see single-digit minimum soon, says IMDThe bench also explored a five-year roadmap to progressively eliminate the entry of polluting commercial vehicles into Delhi without disrupting supplies of essential commodities. “Why not have this during five years? To ensure that no single commercial vehicle enters Delhi,” it suggested.The court clarified that the idea was not to prevent residents from accessing essential goods but to change how these supplies are transported into the city.“Why not how to ensure that commercial vehicles don’t enter Delhi at all? But it does not mean that Delhi people don’t require. They have lot of necessities. They require vegetables, they require fruits, they need other day-to-day items,” the bench observed.It suggested developing warehousing facilities at the city’s borders, where goods could be unloaded and transported into Delhi through battery-operated or other non-polluting vehicles. Acknowledging that such an arrangement might not be feasible immediately, or even next year, the bench said authorities should work towards implementing it over the next five years.Also read: CPCB’s AQI method understates severity of Delhi’s worst pollution days It also indicated that any directions should cover the entire National Capital Region (NCR), rather than Delhi alone, given the contribution of vehicular movement across state boundaries to the region’s pollution burden.Delhi’s winter restrictions cover older vehicles registered outside the capitalThe observations assume significance as the Delhi government has already introduced restrictions on vehicles that do not meet BS-VI emission standards during the winter months. Under its notification, vehicles registered outside Delhi that comply only with BS-IV or older emission norms are barred from plying in the capital between November 1 and January 31 every year.The government announced on November 7 that the restriction would be an annual measure rather than a one-off intervention for the current winter. The prohibition also covers BS-IV and older commercial goods vehicles, including light, medium and heavy goods vehicles, as well as buses entering the capital. CNG and electric vehicles are exempt, along with specified emergency and other exempted categories.Over 2,100 vehicles denied entry during first half of NovemberIn an affidavit filed before the court, the Delhi government’s transport department said enforcement teams had been deployed at major border checkpoints. Between November 1 and 15, 37,315 vehicles were inspected, 2,183 were denied entry and 10 were challaned.The department also said it had installed automatic number plate recognition (ANPR)-based cameras at approximately 500 locations, including petrol pumps and inter-state bus terminals, to identify vehicles operating without a valid pollution under control certificate (PUCC). The system checks number plates against electronic records to verify the validity of pollution certificates.Between January 1 and November 15, the department issued 304,952 challans for vehicles operating without a valid PUCC, 1,350 for visibly polluting vehicles and 8,433 for overloading. It also impounded 5,846 end-of-life vehicles and handed them over to registered vehicle scrapping facilities during the same period, the affidavit said.The government informed the court that it was preparing a vehicle scrapping policy to encourage the voluntary scrapping of old, unfit and highly polluting vehicles. It also proposed one-time financial assistance of ₹1 lakh to eligible existing PUCC centres to modernise their testing infrastructure, besides implementing the upgraded PUCC 3.0 system once introduced by the Union government.The affidavit also outlined Delhi’s electric mobility plans. The transport department and Delhi Transport Corporation currently have a combined fleet of 6,988 buses, including 5,238 electric buses. The fleet is projected to increase to 13,810 by 2028-29, of which 12,060 are expected to be electric.The Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy, 2026, envisages incentives for electric vehicle purchases, exemption from road tax and registration fees for eligible vehicles, and incentives linked to scrapping BS-IV and older internal combustion engine vehicles followed by the purchase of eligible electric vehicles.In its separate status report, the CAQM pointed out that about 94% of vehicles in Delhi-NCR are either two-wheelers or light motor vehicles. It also highlighted the substantially higher pollution potential of older vehicles compared with those complying with BS-VI norms, strengthening the case for a region-wide transition to cleaner mobility.The focus on vehicular emissions comes amid repeated judicial interventions and continuing debate over the relative contribution of local and external sources to Delhi’s air pollution.Also read: The AQI paradox: Why the official count may be downplaying the pollution problemTransport accounts for 21.5% of Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution, estimates showThe Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology’s Air Quality Early Warning System, in its source-apportionment estimates for November 23, attributed around 21.5% of Delhi’s PM2.5 pollution to transport within the city. It estimated that 60% of the particulate pollution load came from sources outside Delhi, underlining the need for coordinated action across the NCR and neighbouring states.The same estimates put the contribution of stubble burning at less than 1% on that day, although the contribution of crop-residue burning can vary considerably during the season.Favourable winds have also helped prevent pollutants from accumulating close to the ground. The India Meteorological Department’s November 23 forecast indicated predominantly northwesterly winds over Delhi, with speeds reaching around 10 kmph during the afternoon. Such winds, along with a relatively deeper atmospheric mixing layer, help disperse pollutants rather than allowing them to remain trapped near the surface.Also read: Delhi’s air quality shows modest year-on-year improvement; meteorology plays a roleThe respite, however, remains fragile. Delhi’s air quality has continued to fluctuate between the ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ categories. The CAQM invoked Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) on November 6 after forecasting a possible deterioration into the ‘severe’ category. The emergency measures were withdrawn on November 17 as air quality improved.The bench said it would examine what further short-term and long-term interventions were necessary to address the recurring pollution crisis.

headline: Man attacks cops with knife, injures 9
content: NEW DELHI: Nine police personnel were injured within a span of two hours after a man allegedly attacked them with a knife in central Delhi Monday. Five personnel were initially injured inside Jama Masjid police station, following which a team chased the suspect as he fled to Chitli Qabar. When he resisted and allegedly injured four personnel, police opened fire, leaving him with six bullet injuries.Police said the incident happened at 2.30pm when Nabeel, a 30-year-old resident of Kala Mahal near Jama Masjid, was called to the police station for counselling following a complaint lodged by his mother and sister, who alleged he was troubling them. Nabeel is unemployed.During an interaction with cops at the station, he allegedly pulled out a knife and, without warning, attacked the staff, inflicting injuries to their faces and necks. Sub-inspectors Ajay and Arvind and head constable Harender sustained serious injuries while assistant sub-inspector Shri Krishna and head constable Baljeet were also injured. All five were shifted to Sir Ganga Ram Hospital.Sources said Nabeel’s mother and sister were present inside the police station when the incident took place.DCP (Central) Rohit Rajbir Singh said following the attack, Nabeel fled and allegedly snatched a scooter from a passerby, Mustakeen, to escape. A joint team of Anti-Auto Theft Squad and Central district special staff launched a search operation and tracked him to Chitli Qabar, under Chandni Mahal police station’s jurisdiction.Around 4.30pm, when the team tried nabbing him, Nabeel allegedly attacked the personnel with a knife again, injuring four special staff members -- constables Ankit, Jayant, Lokesh and Parminder. The injured personnel were rushed to Lok Nayak Hospital.Police said as the suspect continued to pose a threat, the team resorted to controlled firing, with all shots aimed below the waist. A total of eight rounds were fired, six of which hit the suspect in his legs. He was taken to hospital for treatment.Police sources said Nabeel, who lived with his mother, sister and two brothers, was known to have an aggressive temperament. This was the first time his family had approached the police with a complaint against him over his behaviour. “He was a drug addict, and his wife had left him because of his aggressive behaviour,” a source said.Sources claimed Nabeel had brought a pocketknife with him to the police station and was prepared to use it. “Witnesses said it appeared to be a routine case for cops. But he suddenly pulled out the knife and went on a rampage. The personnel were caught off guard and tried to defend themselves, as they were not prepared for such an attack,” a source said.The sources said the entire episode inside the police station unfolded within three-four minutes, and Nabeel allegedly attacked anyone who came in his way. A similar situation arose when the police team tried to apprehend him in Chitli Qabar, they added.Police said a case was previously registered against Nabeel under IPC Section 324 (voluntarily causing hurt by dangerous weapons or means) at Daryaganj police station in 2022. Cases under relevant provisions of law are now being registered at Jama Masjid and Chandni Mahal police stations.In 2022, a 28-year-old man had gone on a stabbing spree inside Shahdara police station in east Delhi.Monday’s incident raised several questions over security at police stations. How did Nabeel manage to enter the premises carrying a knife without being frisked or detected? Where were the duty guards positioned when he fled?Questions have also been raised over the preparedness of trained police personnel to disarm or overpower a lone assailant armed with a knife. Another key concern is whether the police assessed the suspect’s background before calling him to the station in connection with a domestic dispute. The failure to immediately seal the station’s main gate and prevent his escape into the crowded lanes of Old Delhi has also come under scrutiny.

headline: Rising toll: Why Delhi continues to struggle with road safety
content: NEW DELHI: Fatal road accidents in Delhi increased by nearly 7.7% between Jan and Oct 2026 compared to the corresponding period last year, according to official data.Delhi recorded 1,429 fatal accidents, up from 1,327 in 2025. The total number of accidents rose 13%, from 4,673 to 5,281. The number of persons injured increased 20%, from 4,362 to 5,235, while the number of persons killed was up 8.6%, from 1,359 to 1,477.Factors contributing to the accidents included speeding, reckless driving, inadequate road infrastructure, and shortcomings in enforcement.136118379Joint commissioner of police (traffic) Sanjay Tyagi said Delhi Police was committed to making roads safer for commuters. “Through sustained road safety awareness campaigns, strict enforcement of traffic regulations, identification of accident-prone stretches and close coordination with civic agencies, we strive to reduce accidents, save precious lives and foster a culture of responsible road behaviour,” he said.Rohit Baluja, president, Institute of Road Traffic Education, said lack of scientific investigation into accidents, coupled with a high proportion of hit-and-run cases, remained a major concern. Calling for “clear institutional accountability,” he said, “It reflects a systemic failure that we invariably end up blaming the driver for every incident without examining the larger factors contributing to the accident. Studies and recommendations have been submitted to govt, yet the problem persists. Even road signage and traffic control devices, in many cases, don’t conform to the prescribed codes of practice.”Anil Chhikara, former Delhi deputy transport commissioner, said infrastructural deficiencies like inadequate segregation of traffic at flyovers, signals located at poorly visible spots and non-dynamic traffic lights also contributed to accidents.“Ineffective enforcement of traffic rules, heavy congestion, and the absence of sufficient foot overbridges and underpasses also expose road users to greater risks. Moreover, the lack of regular road safety audits, inadequate public transport facilities, overloading of roads with mixed and heterogeneous traffic, and widespread encroachments contribute to unsafe road conditions and increase the likelihood of collisions,” he said.Addressing road safety and traffic management challenges required professional leadership and an integrated institutional framework, along the lines of Singapore’s Land Transport Authority model, Chhikara said: “Under such a framework, all key stakeholders and govt agencies involved in transport, traffic management, road infrastructure, urban planning and civic services would function under a unified authority responsible for land transport and road management. Such an authority can ensure clear ownership of road infrastructure, coordinated planning, regular maintenance, effective traffic management and accountability.”

headline: Labour Minister invites pvt. companies to develop resting space for gig workers, says govt. will provide land
content: Labour Minister Kapil Mishra on Monday invited private companies to develop resting space for gig workers and assured that the Delhi government will provide land for it. He emphasised that merely providing employment to gig workers is not enough, ensuring safe and convenient working conditions is equally important. “Delivery partners continue to work even during extreme heat, heavy rainfall, waterlogging and severe cold. At times, they are also required to provide services late into the night. Therefore, special attention must be given to their safety, health, rest and mental well-being,” Mr. Mishra was quoted in an official statement from his office. Taking part in the ‘Sampark 2026’, organised by the Flipkart Foundation at Bharat Mandapam, Mr. Mishra called upon the foundation and other companies to become partners in the Delhi government’s initiative. “The government is ready to provide space for developing resting zones for gig workers. A model centre has already been started in Shalimar Bagh, where gig workers can sit and relax, charge their mobile phones and avail facilities such as drinking water. The Delhi government is also working towards developing similar centres in major markets and busy areas with high delivery volumes,” Mr. Mishra said. The Minister also said that new avenues for career advancement should be created for delivery partners. By providing training in areas such as store management, warehouse operations, inventory management and other related fields, they can be equipped for better employment opportunities, he added. “Alongside this, efforts should be made towards the education and skill development of their families and children, opening up new avenues of employment and growth for the next generation,” the Minister said.
